I’ve been told I’ve got a "london brogue" because of how I say "th" sounds. I mean, I swear it's just the way I was raised.      Oh, totally. I’ve had students tell me they can’t understand me because I’m from the South East. But actually, I’m just someone who grew up near the coast. That’s just the way it is.      And I’ve heard people say I sound like I’m from Cyprus because of my accent. I mean, I was born in England, but my dad's from Cyprus. So I guess it’s a mix of both. Sometimes it’s easier to just say I have a "Bedfordshire accent," but people always want to know the full story.      I remember once trying to explain where I was from to someone, and they thought I was from the West Midlands. I said, “No, I’m from Bedfordshire,” and they were like, “Oh, I’ve heard of Bedford. That’s where the famous onions come from, right?”      Exactly! It’s like trying to explain a regional dialect without slipping into a joke. I think it’s a good thing that people are more curious about accents these days. It makes conversations more interesting.      I think it’s also a way to connect. When you hear someone’s accent, you can almost tell where they’re from.

Hmm, I just got an email about the new car insurance quote. I was thinking maybe we should save up for a used car instead of buying a brand new one. I mean, with the cost of living going up, it’s not really worth it, is it?      Yeah, I guess you’re right. I’ve been meaning to look into used cars too. My cousin had a great deal on a 2015 model, and it’s been running like a dream. It was cheaper than buying a new one, and the maintenance costs are way lower. But, I still feel like I need a new one because my current car is getting a bit old.      That’s true. I’m driving a 2012 Ford, and while it’s still in good shape, I’m starting to feel like it’s not worth the trouble. Plus, I’m thinking about eventually moving out of this area and maybe needing something more reliable. But I’m not sure if we can afford it right now.      I get that. I’ve been trying to save up for a few months, but with rent and all the other bills, it’s hard. Did you know I’ve started using public transport more often? It’s not the same, but it’s cheaper. I’ve even been taking the train to work a few times a week because the cost of buying a new car is just too high.      Oh, I’ve heard you talking about that. I think it’s a good idea. But I’m not a big fan of buses and trains. I always feel like I’m waiting forever. Plus, I have to commute through some pretty heavy traffic, so it’s not really practical.      I know what you mean. But maybe we can compromise. What if we start saving a little bit each month and see how it goes? I mean, we’re both in a good place financially, right? We’re not struggling, but we’re not exactly rolling in money either.      Yeah, I think that’s a good plan. I can set up a savings account specifically for the car, and you can do the same. It might take a while, but it’s better than just trying to stretch our current budget. I’ll check the used car listings this weekend and see if there’s anything that looks promising.

So, I was just telling my granddaughter about the time her nan tried to fix the plumbing in the old house in Hull. She thought she could do it with a spanner and a bit of grit. Turned out, she just clogged things up more.      Yeah, I remember that. You didn’t even let her use the spanner, did you? I think you just stood there and laughed as she tried to turn the valve.      Oh, I tried to help, but I was still learning. My husband said I was more of a matchstick and a marmalade jar than a plumber. You know how he is.      I remember that. He was always the one who got upset when the water pressure dropped. He thought it was an omen or something. Made us all breakfast when he thought it was the end of the world.      That’s right. Still do. He even made a stained glass window out of jam jars and string, thinking it was a way to catch the light in the kitchen.      You’ve got to be kidding me. That was a disaster. The only light it caught was from the toaster, and it almost set the curtains on fire.      Oh, he did have a way with things, didn’t he? He’d fix the TV, the kettle, and then the toaster. All before breakfast. It was like magic.      And he’d always say, “It’s all in the details, love.” He made about five different kinds of toast every morning. One for the tea, one for the coffee, one for the juice, and the rest were just for show.      And the best part was he’d make them all different shapes. He used to say it was a way to make breakfast more interesting.      Yeah, and he still doesn’t know what a bagel is. He tried to make one once with a bread cutter. Ended up with a sad, lopsided thing that looked like a sad golem.      Oh, I remember that. It looked like it could cry. You had to give it a pat and say it was okay. I think he still feels bad about it.      He still talks about it, you know. He’s got a whole folder of “failed breakfast inventions.” Says it’s for posterity.      Well, I think it’s a testament to his creativity, even if it didn’t end up on the menu.

So, I was just telling the kids about the pirate ship—the Black Sails—what a wild bunch they were! You know, they had maps, treasure, and all sorts of gadgets. I think they were the most exciting people ever.      Yeah, I remember when we watched that movie with the pirate who had a parrot. It was so funny. I wanted to be a pirate when I grew up, but now I just want to be a baker instead.      Wait, when are we going to Stratford? I heard there's a Shakespeare play happening this weekend. I want to see  Hamlet  again. It’s my favorite!      Oh, we’re going to the Stratford Festival next week, and I think there’s a special performance for kids too. Maybe even a workshop where we can act out parts of the play. It’s part of Shakespeare week, and it’s going to be amazing.      Can we wear costumes? I want to be a knight or something. My friend Emma said she’s going to dress like a queen.      I’m going to be a pirate! I got a little sword at the toy store last week. I can duel with it all day long.      You’ll be the best pirate in the world, that’s for sure. But just make sure you don’t lose your sword. You know how those things can go missing.      I won’t. I’ve got a  very  strong grip. Also, I’m going to bring a treasure map. I found one in the attic last weekend. It said “Treasure of the Sea Breeze” or something like that.      Wait, can we go to the circus too? I heard there’s a workshop where you can learn how to juggle and do tricks. I want to be a juggler like in the movies!      That sounds like a great idea. I’ve heard there’s a real circus coming to town, and they have a kids’ workshop every Saturday. It’s part of their Easter celebration. We could go there instead of the Stratford Festival. It’s a big event, and the kids always love it.      Yeah! I want to learn how to ride a unicycle. I saw one in the park last week, and it was so cool.      I want to do ring toss. I saw that on TV, and it looked like fun. Also, I want to learn how to ride a trapeze.

So, I was just telling the others about the time I got arrested trying to sail a boat from Jeddah to Cyprus. It was a real doozy. I had a friend who was into sailing, and we thought we could take a shortcut through the Red Sea. But, well, it was a bit of a mess.      Oh no, really? That sounds like a story I’d love to hear. What happened exactly?      So, what did they do to you? Did they just give you a fine or did they take you away?      Oh, they  took  me away, alright. I was only a few miles off the coast of Jeddah when the coast guard boarded our boat. I suppose they thought we were smuggling something or stealing fuel. We were just trying to get from one place to another, but apparently, it wasn’t allowed.      That’s ridiculous. Why would they even think that? You’re just sailing, for heaven’s sake.      I know, right? We were in a place where I had never been before, and I wasn’t aware of the rules. I tried to explain that we were just tourists, but they weren’t having it. They kept saying we had to show our passports, and then it all went downhill from there.      So, did you end up getting a fine or something?      They put me in a cell for a few hours, and then let me go. I was so embarrassed, and I had a bottle of wine with me. Can you believe it? I spent the whole time in a cell with a bottle of wine, trying to figure out what to do with it.      That’s madness! I mean, if you’re going to be arrested, at least you should have a glass of wine in hand.      I would have told them to give me a glass of wine and then let me go. That’s the British way—always asking for a drink.      Exactly! But I was so nervous, I didn’t think to ask for a drink. Anyway, the point is, I learned a lesson: never sail without knowing the rules of the country you’re in.      And I can relate to that. When I was teaching in Saudi Arabia, I had to be extra careful about what I said and what I did. It was a different kind of restriction, but equally frustrating.

So, I've been meaning to talk to you about the bathroom renovation. I think it's finally time to update it. The tiles are starting to look a bit shabby, and the toilet’s been leaking again. I don’t want to let the kids use it when it’s not safe.      Oh, I understand. I was actually thinking the same thing last week. The kids have been complaining that the shower is too cold, and the sink isn’t working properly. I was going to mention it to you, but I figured you were the one who’d take charge of the project. You’ve always been the one with the plans and the tools.      True, but I also want to make sure it's done right. I've got a few ideas about replacing the fixtures and maybe even adding a new mirror and some better lighting. I think it would make the space look more modern. And I've heard that new bathroom trends are all about open layouts and minimalist designs. I might look into that.      Wait, can I speak? I was thinking about the bathroom, too—personally. I mean, I don’t really care about the design, but I’ve started using the toilet in the living room sometimes. It's just easier when the main one’s broken. My friends say it's trendy to have a ‘toilet corner’ or something. They call it ‘the black hole’ because it's always dark and damp.      Oh, you're just being dramatic. But I get it. You’re a teenager, and you’re always looking for the latest trends. I remember when I was your age, I thought having a  pool  in the backyard was a must. I mean, I still don’t know why that was a thing.      And you know what else you’re missing out on? Real opportunities. I was talking to a friend last week about work experience. There are programs for teenagers to get real-life skills, like customer service or event planning. I think it’s a way to build your resume and learn what you really want to do. You should consider it.      I don’t know. I’m just going to stick with my friends and my latest obsession—online gaming. Yeah, go ahead and talk about work experience. I’m not interested.      Well, I’m not saying you have to jump on the bandwagon, but it doesn’t hurt to explore.

So, what do you think about that truffle oil they served us at the restaurant in Pula? I swear it tasted like a more expensive version of a chip shop fry.      Oh, it was worth the price. You know how much they charge for that stuff, and it was worth every penny. But if you ask me, truffles are a bit of a gimmick. I mean, they’re not even native to this area.      Yeah, and I heard that some people use them as a status symbol. Like, if you’re eating truffle oil, you’re supposed to be rich or something.      Oh, you’re telling me. I’ve seen it on Instagram, people in fancy restaurants, and I think it’s just a trend. I’d rather eat a proper steak with some real butter than that stuff.      That’s the problem with trends, isn’t it? They come and go, and by the time you know what you’re doing, it’s already out. I remember when people were obsessed with kale. Now they’re all about ... what’s the latest thing?      Oh, it’s got to be stem cells, right? You hear that everywhere. People talking about it like it’s the future of medicine.      Honestly, I get it. It’s a big deal in the UK, especially with all the research going on. But I’d rather have a good cup of tea and a bit of football on the telly than worry about stem cells.      Yeah, and I heard that they’re doing some research on using stem cells to help with football injuries. Like, if you break your leg, they can fix it with stem cells instead of just waiting for it to heal.      That sounds like something out of a sci-fi movie. I mean, I support medical advancements, but I’d rather not have to deal with a new kind of surgery just to play football.      I think it’s all part of the journey. You know, like how we used to have to drive on the left side of the road. Now it’s the right, and everyone’s used to it.      Yeah, and I think we’re all just trying to figure out life as we go. Like, food, football, and even cigarettes. I still can’t quit, even though I know it’s bad for me.      I tried once, and I swore I’d never touch one again.

Oh, I just got an email from the university about the new language project. It’s going to be a big one—cross-linguistic analysis of dialects in the UK. I’m excited, honestly. It’s going to be a challenge, but I think it’s exactly what I need to keep my research moving forward.      Yeah, I heard about that. I think they’re doing a lot of work on regional variations, right? It’s interesting to see how dialects are evolving. But honestly, I still can’t wrap my head around why people in East Anglia sound so different from us in Cambridge.      Oh, you know, it’s all about the vowels. It’s like a musical scale—each region has its own tune. I remember once trying to understand someone from Manchester, and it was like trying to read a foreign language. I thought they were speaking a different dialect of English!      I can’t even tell you how many times I’ve had that experience. I grew up in Aylesbury, so I’m used to the “Aylesbury accent”—it’s like a mix of RP and something more regional. But it’s such a struggle when you’re in a place like Cambridge, where people speak so fast and with such a clipped tone. It’s almost like they’re hiding something.      That’s the Cambridge thing, though. We’re all pretty efficient. If you can’t keep up, you’re not really part of the club. But I have to say, I’ve learned a lot from being immersed in different accents. It makes me more aware of how language shapes identity.      And it makes you more empathetic, too. I mean, I used to think people from London were so arrogant, but now I realize it’s just their way of speaking. It’s not about class—it’s about culture.      Exactly. I think that’s what makes language such a fascinating subject. It’s not just about words—it’s about how people connect, how they express themselves, and how their environment shapes the way they speak. I find it really rewarding to study all of that.      I couldn’t agree more. And it’s amazing to be in a place like Cambridge, where so many people are passionate about language and communication. I mean, it’s like we’re all in the same room, even if we don’t all speak the same way.

So, I just wanted to check – do you think we should stop off at that petrol station on the motorway or just keep going? I’m a bit run down from all this driving today.      Honestly, I think we should take the detour. The station is only a few miles ahead, and it’s a chance to grab some snacks and maybe even check the map again. Plus, I’ve been meaning to ask you something about that Polish language class you mentioned.      Oh, you mean the one I was thinking of taking when I was in Cambridge? I’ve been meaning to get back into it. I mean, I still have that old textbook I bought years ago. It’s like a relic now, but I’ve been revisiting it.      That would be great. I know how much you love learning languages. It’s actually why I started teaching English abroad. I mean, I teach EFL in Manchester, but I’ve always wanted to work in Poland. I thought maybe after this trip I could look into it.      That’s ambitious, but I think it’s worth considering. I mean, your teaching experience is solid. And with the way things are going in education, there are opportunities everywhere.      Yeah, I guess that’s true. I’ve been thinking about it for a while. I just need to figure out how to get my CV over there. I mean, I don’t know if I’d be able to work full-time in Poland right away, but even part-time could be a good start.      I think you’d do really well. I mean, you’ve got the qualifications, and your personality is just right for teaching. You’re so patient and enthusiastic. I remember when I was a kid, my English teacher was like that. She made everything feel fun.      That’s sweet of you to say. I think I’d be more nervous than excited, to be honest. I mean, moving to a new country, learning a new language, getting a job. It sounds like a lot.      It’s not all that scary, really. I mean, you’re already in a country where English is spoken. Polish is a bit more of a challenge, but it’s doable. Plus, you have friends here. I think you’d fit in just fine.      Yeah, you’re right. I mean, I’ve been to Poland before, and it’s a lovely place.

So, I just got this idea for a new football strip design. You know, it’s not like the usual kits they sell at the stadium. I think it could be something more modern, maybe with a gradient color scheme. Not too flashy, but something that looks sleek on the pitch.      That sounds interesting. I mean, they’ve done a lot of creative stuff lately, especially with the sponsorship deals. I remember reading that one of the top teams had a collaboration with a tech company, and they came up with some pretty cool-looking kits. It was more about branding than just functionality.      Yeah, but I think there’s a balance to strike. You don’t want the design to overshadow the players, you know? I mean, the kit is part of the team’s identity, but if it’s too complicated, it can look messy. Plus, I was thinking about the materials. Maybe they could use something more sustainable this time. Less plastic, more recycled fabric.      That’s a good point. Sustainability is becoming more important, especially with the younger generation. I think a lot of fans are starting to care about that. But it’s not just about the environment—there’s also the performance aspect. You can't just have a cool design if the kit is uncomfortable or doesn’t wick sweat properly.      Exactly. I’ve seen some kits that are so heavy, they look like they're made of lead. I’d love to see a design that’s both stylish and practical. And maybe even a few different color options for different match days? Some teams do that, right?      Definitely. I remember when my team used to have those special editions for big games. It was a way to get fans excited. But I wonder if they’re going to start using that strategy more often now, especially with the sponsorship deals. I mean, if they can tie the kit design to a brand, they can make more money.      That’s true. But I still think there’s room for creativity. I was just thinking about the latest McDonald’s ad they did with a football team. It was pretty bold, but I’m not sure if it’s the best use of their brand. I mean, their main goal is to sell burgers, not to promote sports.      Haha, yeah, I get that. But I guess it’s all about getting the brand in front of as many people as possible.

So, I've been trying to record these conversations for my thesis, but it's such a pain. I got the recorder working yesterday, but now I can't find it. I've checked everywhere — under the couch, behind the fridge, even in the garden. It's like it vanished into thin air.      Wait, you didn’t just leave it on the kitchen counter, did you? I remember seeing it there last night after you said you were going to use it for the interview with that guy from the university.      No, I thought I put it in my bag. I had it with me when I came back from the train station. That was the last time I saw it. I even called the train station to check if someone found it, but they said they didn’t have anything like that.      That’s not the only thing that’s gone missing. I’ve been trying to get my job seeker’s allowance sorted, but the council is being a nightmare. They said I have to provide proof of income, but I don’t have any. I’ve been unemployed for over a year now.      I know, I know. I tried to help you fill out the forms last week, but it got too complicated. You just need to get your benefits sorted, and then you’ll be fine. I mean, you’re not the only one struggling. I’ve been working part-time, but it’s not enough to cover the gas and electricity.      Yeah, I’ve been thinking about that. I’ve had this idea about taking the kids on a day trip to Margate. I heard it’s nice this time of year. I even ordered a few things off eBay — the tickets, the snacks, and a little souvenir for the kids. But I’m worried they’re going to be late.      You just need to tell them you’re taking them. They’ll be excited. You know how they love going out. And if the eBay stuff is late, I’ll just buy the snacks myself. It’s not like we’re short on money.      Thanks, I appreciate it. I just feel like I’m not doing enough for the kids. I go out of my way to help, but I’m still stuck in this rut. I don’t know what else to do.      You’re doing your best, and that’s all anyone can ask.

I can't believe how much easier everything is now with the sat nav. I used to drive my kids to school every day and get completely lost, even though I knew the route. It’s like having a GPS in my head, but sometimes it just doesn’t work. Do you remember that time I got stuck on the A1 for an hour because the sat nav said it was “the fastest route”?      Oh, I remember that! You were so frustrated. You even had to pull over and ask a motorist if the sat nav was right. I still laugh about it. I mean, I don’t even trust the sat nav now. My job is cleaning, so I don’t drive much, but I got into a bit of a mess the other day trying to get to the nearest convenience store. I followed the sat nav, and it took me all the way to the end of the road, where there was a sign that said “Left turn only.” I had to turn back and find another way.      I know what you mean. I used to drive every day when I was working, but now I just walk. I can’t even remember how to get to the local market. I rely on people now. I’m too old for sat navs. I’d rather ask someone than get lost. Although, I have to say, I remember when you used to get stuck in traffic and you’d say, “I should’ve just taken the back road.” But you never did.      That’s what I used to say. I’d always be late for meetings because I’d be stuck in traffic, trying to take the “short cut.” And then I’d end up going the long way. It’s funny how things change. I’ve got a new job now, and I’m not driving to meetings anymore. I’m actually considering buying a car for my kids, though. They’re getting older, and it’s time for them to learn.      That’s a good idea. I can’t imagine doing what you do without a car. I mean, I walk everywhere, but I still rely on buses and taxis. I’ve heard that some of the supermarkets even go out of their way to help people like me. They give me discounts and even leave the doors open when I’m in a hurry.

Hey, have you seen the new trainee teachers at school? I swear, one of them looks like she stepped out of a drama class. She’s always acting out scenes in class like she’s in a play. It’s funny, but honestly, I don’t think she’s ready to teach us.      Oh, I saw her too! She tried to read a poem in English class and suddenly started whispering to herself like she was confused. Everyone was staring at her, and she just blushed and kept going. I mean, okay, she’s a trainee teacher, but isn’t that like, a bit much?      Yeah, I don’t think she even knows how to use a whiteboard properly! She tried to write on the board with her finger, like she was drawing, and then the teacher had to step in. It was so embarrassing.      I bet she’s got some kind of drama degree or something. I heard her talking to one of the teachers about “performing in front of an audience.” She said something like, “I want to engage the students through storytelling.” I’m like,  engage ? You’re just making us look like we’re in a show!      I mean, I can see why they’re using trainee teachers. The school is trying to modernize, and they’re trying to make learning more interactive. But I think some of them don’t understand what that means. Like, someone said in one of the assemblies that we should “question everything.” So we did. And then the teacher got really upset.      Oh, I remember that! You know, the one about the science experiment? We all started asking questions about the chemicals, and she just said, “Wait, why are you doing that?” It was so weird.      Exactly! And then the art teacher tried to do a project about emotions. She said we should “express ourselves through any medium.” So some of us tried to paint, some tried to write poems, and one guy just started drawing a cat.      I think that’s the point, though. Like, you don’t have to be perfect. I mean, the cat guy was really creative. Maybe if more teachers were like that, we’d actually like school more.      Yeah, I guess. But still, I can’t wait for the tests. I heard one of the trainee teachers said something like, “Tests are just a way to measure understanding.”

So, what do you think about all that stuff? I mean, I know it’s got a lot of weird parts, but I guess it’s all kind of like a belief system, right?      I guess. I mean, it’s not like religion is the only thing people believe in. I read about Scientology before. It’s like they think they’re getting help from the “auditors,” or whatever. But I don’t think it’s real. I mean, why would they be helping us if they’re not even real?       Matrix ! That’s the one with the blue pills and the red pills! My daddy said if you take the red pill, you’ll wake up and see the truth!      Oh, you’re watching  The Matrix  again? I remember when you were old enough to watch that. It was like a big deal. I didn’t get it at first, but now I think it’s kind of like a metaphor for life. Like, we’re all being guided by some system, and we don’t even know it.      Yeah, like religion. I mean, it’s all about belief. Some people say the world is made by God, others say it’s all just random. Some say it’s the Matrix, and some say it’s Scientology. I don’t know what to believe, honestly.      That’s the thing, isn’t it? I think what matters is that you have a belief system that makes you feel safe. Like, I used to be really into the idea about nuns and the Church. I thought they were the real deal. But then I started reading more and realized that some of the stuff they say isn’t true. It’s all kind of tricky.      But what about the nuns? Like, the ones who help people? Do you think they’re real or just part of the Matrix?      I think they’re real. I mean, they help people in real ways, even if the Church isn’t perfect. I think it’s about the good they do, not just the stuff they say.      I guess. I mean, I don’t know much about religion, but I do know that people have different ideas. Like, my friend’s mom is into scientology, and she says it’s the only way to be happy.      I like  Matrix  better. It’s cooler. I want to be like Neo.

So, I just got an email about these dancing lessons that they’re offering at the community center. You know, those ones where you learn salsa and ballroom? I thought it might be fun to try something new, especially with the summer coming up. What do you think?      Honestly, I’m all for it. I mean, I’ve never really been into dancing, but I’ve heard how it’s great for confidence and exercise. Plus, it’s a chance to meet people. Although, I’ve got to say, I’m still not sure about the salsa. I’m more of a slow dance kind of guy.      Oh, I get that. But I think it’s worth giving it a go. You know, I’ve been thinking about the holidays too. I was talking to my cousin about going to Cornwall this year. She’s got this place she rents out, and the view is amazing. I was just wondering if you’d want to come along?      Cornwall sounds amazing! I’ve always wanted to go. I mean, I’ve been to the south coast before, but Cornwall is a different vibe. I’d love to go with you. But, you know, I’ve got this engineering project due in a couple of weeks. Maybe I can squeeze it in?      That’s fair. I wouldn’t want you to miss out on your work. But seriously, you’ve got to try the dancing. I’ve been doing some research on Old English and the way people spoke back in the day—just for fun. It’s kind of fascinating how much the language has changed over the centuries.      That’s cool. I’ve always been interested in how language evolves. I mean, I even remember the days when the BBC still used to say “couple of” instead of “a couple of.” It’s a bit of a nostalgia trip for me.      Exactly! I think it’s one of those things that people forget how much language is tied to culture. Speaking of culture, have you seen that new TV show about the history of the British Isles? It’s on LoveFilm, and it’s got some amazing shots.      I haven’t, but I’m going to check it out. I’ve been busy with work, but I’ll make time. Speaking of work, I think I might be applying for a job in Manchester.

So, what do you think about that olive oil we bought in the market in Pula? I mean, it’s got this really strong flavor, like it’s got a bit of a bite to it. Not sure if I like it, but it’s definitely not the kind of oil you’d find in a British supermarket.      I actually like it, but I’ve got to say, I’m more of a wine person. You know, the local Istrian wine is just so good. The reds, especially. We had one at the restaurant in Pazin that was to die for. I mean, it was like,  wow , you could taste the mountains in every sip.      Yeah, I’ve been wanting to try the local wine. But I’m still not sure if I like reds. I’m more into the lighter stuff. But I do love the way the sun sets here. The colors in the sky, it’s like a painting.      Absolutely. It’s one of the things that makes Istria so beautiful—these dramatic sunsets. You’ve got to take a few moments to stop and just enjoy it. Speaking of which, I was thinking about where we should go tomorrow. We’ve got a few days left, and I think we should check out some of the nature parks around here.      That’s a good idea. I’ve heard the parks here are amazing. Oh, look at this! I still remember the time we all went to the Royal Ascot together. It was the summer after I finished sixth form, and we thought we were so grown up. I just watched this new horror movie last night, and it gave me nightmares for days. You would  not  believe the ending. It was so twisted, I couldn’t even sleep properly. Oh no, really? So, I've been thinking about getting an iPad for work. I know it's supposed to be really useful for taking notes and organizing lesson plans, but I'm a bit nervous about how much it might cost. So, I've been meaning to ask you, have you read that new book by David Mitchell?  The Glass Hotel —it’s supposed to be brilliant. Well, I've been thinking about the times, you know. When I was younger, things were different. You could walk into a shop and get a loaf of bread for a few pennies. I mean, we’ve all been through hard times, but it’s not fair that the younger generation is struggling too. They’re trying to build a future, but if the cost of living keeps going up, they’ll never get anywhere.

I could even bring a few bottles to share.      That sounds like a good plan. I’ve been trying to learn more about wine too, mostly to impress my friends. I’ve even been experimenting with some basic wine and cheese pairings in my kitchen.      That’s brilliant! I’d love to hear your recommendations. It’s always good to have a few options in case we’re not sure. Speaking of, have you both thought about what car you’ll be driving on the trip?

So, I was going through some old photos the other day, and I found this one from when we were in Japan. It's from the Kyoto temple, right? I remember we were there in early spring, and the cherry blossoms were just starting to bloom. It looks like we were wearing those silly bright yellow raincoats, and we were both laughing like crazy.      Oh man, that was  so  embarrassing. I still remember how we both got caught in the rain, and you said, “Well, at least the photos will be interesting!” And then we both slipped on the wet stones, and we both fell over like a pair of clumsy tourists.      I still have that photo. You look like you’re mid-fall, and I’m holding my camera like it’s the last thing I’ll ever see. I swear, if I could edit that photo, I’d somehow make it look more dignified.      You’re not the only one who remembers that. I still get a laugh every time I see it. I think it’s one of the few photos of us that I actually like. It’s not about the scenery—it’s about  us .      Exactly. I was thinking the other day that we should go back to Japan someday. I’ve been meaning to revisit some of the places we went. And maybe take better photos this time. You know, not just for the memories, but to capture the moments properly.      I’d love that. Besides, I’ve been teaching photography to a few kids at the local community center. Maybe I could even take them with us. They’d love to see the temples and try their hands at capturing the real thing.      That sounds like a great idea. I bet they’d get a kick out of it. I was thinking, too, about the badgers we saw near our cabin in Norfolk. I have a photo of one staring at me from the window. It’s like it’s judging me.      Oh, I remember that. You were trying to take a photo of it from the window, and the badger just looked at you like you’d stolen its breakfast. That was one of the best moments of our trip.      I think it was trying to tell us we were wasting our time. But what can I say? We were just too curious for our own good.

So, I was just telling my mates about that time I tried to skinny dip in the loch near my grandparents’ house in Scotland. You know, that one with the murder by the water? Anyway, I thought it’d be a fun way to cool off after a day hiking. But it was so cold, I couldn’t even last five minutes. I was shivering like a leaf.      Oh no, really? That sounds intense! I mean, I've never done it, but I can imagine the cold would be brutal. I once tried to chase a stray cat through a puddle in the rain, and I ended up soaked and shivering for hours. What did you do after that? Jump back in?      No, I just ran back to the house, wrapped myself in a towel, and then I spent the whole evening crying because I was too cold. It was a disaster. I’ve never gone near water since. Although, I did once try to cook a roasted chicken in a pan, and that ended up being a total mess too.      You’re not the only one with bad cooking experiences. I once tried to make Claudia Roden’s Jewish recipes, and I ended up with something that tasted like a mix between a cake and a sauce. My customers at the café were confused. I almost had to explain that it was a “mistake.”      I bet that was worse than my attempt at making mexican food in the flat I shared with my roommate. He thought he was a chef, and he ended up making a meal out of something that looked like a science experiment. It was like a zombie apocalypse in the kitchen. You couldn’t even tell what was edible.      I can imagine. I once had a friend who tried to make a “Jewish dip” and accidentally used the wrong kind of cheese. It looked like it had been baked in a nuclear reactor. I had to laugh so hard I nearly choked on my own laughter.      Speaking of which, have any of you ever heard a good Jewish joke? My Auntie once told me one about a Jewish baker and a loaf of bread. She said, “I told my bread I loved it, and it started to crumble.” It’s one of those classic ones.      Oh yeah, I’ve heard that one. But I think the best one is the one where a Jewish man goes to a restaurant and orders kasha varnishkes.

So, I was just talking to my cousin about border security. She’s really into it, like, how it’s affecting travel and stuff. You know how things have changed since Brexit, right? It’s a bit of a headache for people who travel a lot.      Yeah, I’ve heard about that. I mean, I’m a PhD student, so I’ve had to deal with all sorts of travel restrictions. It’s not just the EU countries—now even some of the US and Canada have started requiring more documentation. It’s kind of a pain, especially when you’re trying to get to a conference or something.      I can imagine. I mean, I work in research management, so I travel a lot too. I’ve even had to deal with some of the more strict security checks at Heathrow. But I was thinking—do you think all this border security is actually making us safer, or is it just making it more inconvenient?      Hmm, that’s a good question. I think it’s a bit of both. On one hand, it helps prevent some of the bad stuff—like terrorism or illegal immigration. On the other, it’s not really stopping the real problems. You can still get through if you’re not flagged, and it’s just adding more queues and delays for everyone else. Plus, I’ve heard stories about people getting turned away for silly reasons.      Exactly. I mean, I remember reading an article about a guy who got stuck for hours because someone at the airport thought he looked suspicious. He was a tourist, just trying to see the sights. That’s not really security, that’s just being rude.      Yeah, that’s the thing about security—it’s like a game of guesswork. You can’t really trust anyone, and you can’t really be sure who’s a threat. It’s kind of like those computer games we used to play—where you have to guess which level is safe and which isn’t. It’s all about risk assessment, but with real people.      You’re right. I was actually thinking about that the other day. I mentioned it to my mate, and he said it’s like theme parks—everyone’s there for fun, but they have to follow the rules. Yeah, go on, I think he was comparing it to roller coasters.

So, I’ve been thinking about getting back into rowing. I’ve always loved the rhythm of it—like, the way the oar cuts through the water and the silence around you. I’d love to see if I can get a spot on the local club again.      That’s great! I remember when I first started rowing, I was completely out of my depth—literally. I once tried to row during a storm and ended up nearly capsizing. But it’s such a rewarding sport. Did you know you need the right kind of clothing for it? Especially if you’re rowing in wet weather?      Oh, I know, I’ve been trying to figure out what to wear. My friend mentioned something about neoprene gloves and waterproof trousers. But I’m not sure I’m ready for all that gear yet. I think I’ll start with just a decent raincoat and proper shoes.      You’ll need more than that if you’re planning to be out for a while, though. I always carry a waterproof jacket, a pair of quick-dry shorts, and even a waterproof cap. Oh, and I’ve got this old pair of wetsuit socks I use for when the water’s really cold—it’s a lifesaver.      Hmm, maybe I should start with something less intense, like kayaking. I’ve been meaning to try that. It’s more manageable, and I can even do it in the nearby river. But I’ve never really had someone to help me get started. Did you ever do that?      Oh, I did! I met my cousin at a local kayaking event a few years back. We ended up kayaking together, and it was such a nice way to reconnect. She’s been living in France for a while, and we hadn’t seen each other in years. It was a real emotional moment—like, we had so many memories to catch up on.      That sounds lovely. Speaking of family, have you heard about my uncle? He’s been unwell lately, and I’m really worried about him. He’s been in and out of the hospital, and the whole family’s been trying to support him.      I’m sorry to hear that. I hope he’s getting better. My father passed away a few years ago, and I still struggle with that. It’s always hard when you lose someone close.

Dad, do you know how to send a text message? I keep getting confused with the emojis.      Oh, I know how that feels. I used to think the 💔 meant something different—like a smiley face with tears. But I’ve got a friend who’s a teacher, and she taught me how to read them properly.      Yeah, I’ve tried using them, but I end up sending something completely wrong. Like the 😂 and 😭 are the same to me.      It’s tricky. I remember when I first got a mobile phone, I had to learn Morse code too. It was like learning a whole new language.      Wait, you know Morse code? Like the dots and dashes?      Yeah, I learned it in the army. It’s amazing how it works, especially when you’re out and about and need to send a message without a phone.      I never thought about using it like that. Do you still use it today?      Not really. But I remember when I used to send messages with a phone that had no internet. You had to type everything out.      That’s so old-fashioned. Now, everything’s just texts and emojis. I don’t even know how to write a full sentence without autocorrect.      I remember when I had to write letters by hand. I used to make mistakes with the spelling, and the stationery shop had this thing called a "glass water bottle" that you used to dip your pen in.      A glass water bottle? Like a fountain pen?      Yeah, that’s what they called it. I miss that. I used to write my essays in those days. Now, I just order from Amazon and eBay.      I guess technology has changed a lot. But I still need to study for my exams on results day.      Yeah, I remember that day like it was yesterday. Time flies. You should get some pens and stationery for your university campus.      I’m planning to get some new shoes too, and maybe some food for the weekend.      Sounds like a plan. Just make sure you don’t spend too much on the shoes.      You don’t have to tell me. I’ve already spent too much on food shopping last week.      Alright, let’s get going. Dinner is waiting, and I’ve got a glass water bottle in my bag.      I don’t know what you’re talking about.

Hey, man, it's been ages! I couldn't believe it was you when I walked in. How’ve you been?      Mate, I’ve been decent, just a bit stressed with exams. You know how it is—load of essays, deadlines, and trying to keep up with the grind. How about you?      Honestly, I’ve been surviving. I’ve been getting into some coding side projects, but honestly, I’m just trying to keep my GPA up. Speaking of which, I heard you're going to Tokyo next semester?      Yeah, I’m applying for a study abroad program in Japan. I’ve always wanted to visit Tokyo, and since I’ve got the chance to study there, it’s just too good to pass up. You should consider it, man. It’s a chance to see the world and get a new perspective.      I’d love to, but honestly, the cost is a bit too high for me right now. Plus, I’m not sure if I’d even get accepted into any of those exchange programs.      It’s not impossible. You just need to start early and put in the work. I’ve been working on my application all week. I’m even thinking about doing some research on Japanese culture and tech because I heard Tokyo is one of the most tech-savvy cities in the world.      That sounds cool. I’ve been trying to get into coding more seriously. I even got a new laptop last week. It’s a bit of a pain trying to get everything set up, but I’m getting there.      Dude, I know the feeling. I just spent the weekend setting up my Windows 11 system and trying to get all my school apps installed. It’s a nightmare, but once you get it sorted, it’s like a whole new level of productivity.      Exactly. I was thinking about getting a second monitor for work too. You ever think about that?      Yeah, I’ve been thinking about it too. I just haven’t had the budget. Maybe when I get that scholarship from Japan, I can finally splurge on some gadgets.      I hope it works out for you. You’ve always had a way of making things happen.      Thanks, man. I owe a lot of my success to you and your advice. Anyway, I better get going. I’ve got a meeting with my study abroad advisor tomorrow.

So, I just got a photo from Facebook of that trip we took to Buckfast Abbey last year. It’s so weird, I can’t believe it’s been over a year already.      Oh, I remember that! I had to take a photo of the bell tower for the whole family. You know how we always end up with that one awkward shot where someone’s face is half in the frame.      Ah, yes, that’s the one. I still get a laugh every time I see it. You were standing in the doorway, looking like you’d just woken up from a nap!      I told you I was tired from the hike up the hill. Still, I’m glad we got to see the monks there. It was like stepping back in time, and I love the whole history of the place.      Absolutely, and the monks were so friendly. They even gave us a little tour, explaining the history of the abbey and the wine they make. I think I still have that bottle of Buckfast on my shelf.      Oh, I’ve got one too. I even took a sip once, just to see what it tastes like. It’s a bit like a strong herbal tea – very strong, but not unpleasant.      I’ve heard people say it’s got a strong effect, but I think it’s more about the ritual than the drink itself. Anyway, I was just thinking—what do you think about a trip to Cornwall next summer? The weather’s usually better, and there are so many places to explore.      That sounds great. I’ve been meaning to take the kids there. I heard there’s this amazing coastal path near St. Ives. Maybe we could combine it with a visit to the Eden Project?      You know, I was thinking about that too. The Eden Project is a fantastic place, especially for the kids. But I also think we should consider a cruise. My friend Margaret said she’s planning one to the Canary Islands next year.      Cruises? I’ve never been on one, but I’ve heard they can be a bit pricey. Though I do think it would be a good way to relax and see some beautiful places.      Yes, but if we can get a good deal, it could be worth it. Oh, and we should check out the insurance too. I was talking to a friend the other day about how some policies cover travel cancellations.

So, how was your trip to Belgium, Mum? I mean, I know you said it was amazing, but I’m dying to hear all the details!      Oh, it was  so  good, Lottie. We had the best time. The weather was perfect, and we even got to see the sights. You know, I actually got a bit of a tan from all that sunshine!      It was lovely, really. The markets were amazing. I got so many souvenirs, but the most interesting thing was the cheese. I had never seen so many types before. And the chocolate—oh, that was  delicious .      I’ve heard about the chocolates, but I didn’t know they had so many different varieties. Did you try the ones with the raspberries? I think I read somewhere that’s a local specialty.      We did! And, you know, I had to ask for directions a few times. I was using the sat nav, but it kept giving me the wrong turns. Felt a bit like I was in a maze!      I remember that. You got so frustrated, Dad. I had to take over and use my phone because the sat nav didn’t know where you were. But that’s what you get for driving in Europe without a proper map.      I remember you got stuck on a tiny road that was oddly named ‘The Wall’ or something like that. It was so narrow, you couldn’t even fit the car in!      I can still hear the screeching of the tires as I tried to reverse out. I was so embarrassed. But it was a funny story to tell the kids.      And don’t even get me started on the driving. You told me you were so stressed about it, but you actually did pretty well. I was really proud of you.      Yeah, and speaking of driving, have you thought about getting that new phone yet? I’ve been meaning to ask—did you go for the one with the best sat nav?      I was thinking about it, but I’m still a bit nervous. I mean, I can handle a few turns, but I’d rather not get lost again. You know how I feel about that!      Don’t worry, Dad. I’ll be there if you ever need help. And besides, you’ve always been good at finding your way around. Even when you’re not supposed to!

Okay, I've got the potatoes peeled and the onions chopped. I was just wondering, do you think we should make the steak with some rosemary or maybe stick to the classic garlic butter?      Hmm, I think the garlic butter would be a safe bet. It’s simple and always works. But if you want to jazz it up, rosemary would be great—especially with the herbs you’ve got in the kitchen.      True, and the herbs are fresh. I do love how the rosemary adds that earthy aroma. But I also thought about the flowers we had earlier. Maybe we could use some lavender for a nice touch?      Lavender? That’s a good idea. I remember you saying you found some at the market the other week. But I thought you were going to use it for perfume. What’s the deal with the flowers?      Oh, I was going to make a batch of perfume as a gift for my sister’s birthday. But I thought why not use some of the lavender in the meal, too? It’s a bit of a luxury to have such a wide range of flowers and herbs in the kitchen.      It’s quite a treat. I mean, most people don’t have access to such a variety. Speaking of which, have you seen the weather forecast? It’s supposed to be colder than usual this week.      Yeah, I’ve been thinking about it. Maybe we should test out the fireplace. I remember we had a few logs in the shed. I think it would be nice to have some warmth as the evenings get cooler.      That sounds perfect. I can bring the logs in after we finish cooking. I’ve also been checking my Facebook friends list. I noticed some of the old friends from university are still active, but a few have left the country.      I know, it’s surprising how some people just disappear. I still keep in touch with most of them, though. It’s funny how time flies.      Absolutely. I was just thinking about how we used to spend our evenings here, chatting around the fire. I wonder what we’ll go through in the years to come.      I hope we’ll still be able to sit here, cooking and laughing, even when we’re older. It’s moments like these that make life worth living.      You’re right.

So, I've been meaning to ask, what do you think about people from the North compared to Southerners? I've often heard that there's a bit of a divide, especially when it comes to dialects and attitudes.      Oh, I've heard that too. I think it's more about perception than reality. I was born and bred in Manchester, and I've always thought that the North has a lot more grit and resilience. But I've also met some Southerners who are just as hardworking.      I agree. I'm from Sheffield, and I've always had a bit of a strong accent. Some people think it's uneducated, but I like it. It's part of who I am. Speaking of accents, I once worked in Bristol, and the way they speak is so different. They have this soft, melodic way of talking that I almost missed when I came back to Yorkshire.      That’s interesting. I grew up in Almondsbury near Bristol, so I've heard that accent too—very refined, almost posh. But I’ve always thought people in the South are a bit more formal. I’ve also heard that some people from the South are not too keen on people from the North.      That’s a common stereotype, isn’t it? I’ve heard the phrase “South of the border” used as a slight. But I think it’s more about class and background than geography. I was in business for a long time, and I noticed that people from different backgrounds often had more in common than their accents would suggest.      True. I taught English as a foreign language, and I always found that the way people speak can be a barrier, but it’s not always a bad one. I once had a student from Queensland who had a very distinct accent, and I found it fascinating.      Oh, I’ve been to Australia a few times. I was teaching there for a year, and I remember the way people there spoke—so casual, so laid-back. They say “g’day” and “no worries.” It’s such a different culture.      I’ve never been, but I’ve heard so much about it. I’ve always wanted to go. I was thinking about taking a loan from the bank to go on a trip, but I’m not sure. The interest rates are so high now.

So, I just saw this article on social media about how people are starting to take podcasts more seriously. Like, some influencers are even using them as a way to build their brand. I mean, I listen to a few podcasts myself, but I never thought they'd become such a big deal.      Yeah, I’ve noticed that too. I actually started a podcast about teaching English as a foreign language a few months ago. It’s just me talking about my experiences, teaching tips, and even some of the funny things that happen in the classroom. It’s been surprisingly popular.      That’s awesome! I’ve been meaning to start one too. I’ve got the idea, but I’m just not sure how to get started. I guess I’m a bit intimidated by the whole thing. Plus, I’m not even sure if there’s an audience for someone like me—someone who’s unemployed and semi-retired. I feel like I’m not in the right place for that kind of thing.      Oh, don’t say that! I think people like you are actually the ones who can tell the most authentic stories. You’ve got life experience, and your perspective as someone who's taken a different path in life might be exactly what others are looking for. I mean, people are drawn to real voices, not just polished ones.      That’s true. I guess I’ve been too focused on my own insecurities. I mean, I’m not even sure if I can afford a decent microphone or anything. But maybe I can start with just a phone and upload it to a platform like Spotify or YouTube. I’ve seen people do it with their phones, so it’s not that hard.      Exactly! And besides, you can always start small. Maybe just post a few episodes and see how it goes. I mean, I started with just one episode, and now I have over a hundred followers. It’s been a steady growth. And besides, it’s a way to stay connected with people and share your experiences.      I guess I need to stop being so hard on myself. I’ve always had a lot of opinions, and I think it’s time I started sharing them. I mean, I still have a lot to say, even if I’m not working or doing much these days.

Okay, so I just got a message from Pippy. She wants to know if we can get a photograph for her Blue Peter badge. She’s really excited about it, and I think she’d love to see it on the show.      Can I come too? I want to be in the photo with her.      Me too! I wanna be in the photo. I’m not scared of the camera!      Of course you can, both of you. It’s going to be a fun day. But before we get to that, I need to talk to you about something. I was talking to ANON the babysitter, and she mentioned that you kids are going to see her Travelling Circus next weekend.      Is it going to be cool? Can we ride the carousel?      I heard they have a lion! I want to see the lion!      Well, that sounds amazing. But I have to ask—has ANON told you about the pocket money she gives you?      She gave me a pound for helping her with the groceries. Was that right?      I got a fiver for cleaning my room. That’s a lot!      It’s a fair amount, but don’t get used to it. ANON is just trying to teach you responsibility. Anyway, I also need someone to help me get a passport for the Blue Peter badge photo. Do you know where I can get one?      I think you need to go to the post office or the council. I saw a sign about that.      I think you can get one online too! I know my dad does it that way.      Thanks, that’s useful. I’ll look into that. Oh, and by the way, I overheard ANON talking about the Chinese eating old eggs. I don’t know if that’s true.      Is it true? Does the Chinese really eat old eggs?      I think it’s a myth. I’ve never seen anyone eat eggs that are too old.      It’s probably just an old story. Anyway, we need to start planning the Blue Peter photo. I’m going to need you both to be dressed nicely and bring your best smiles.      I’ll wear my favourite dress! It’s blue with stars on it.      I’ll wear my superhero costume!      Perfect. That’s going to make the photo even more memorable. So, let’s plan to do it this weekend.

So, I was just thinking about that talk we had last week about sex and all... I don’t know, maybe it’s just me, but I’ve been feeling a bit... I dunno, low. Like, not the same as before.      Yeah, I’ve been feeling that too. It’s weird, isn’t it? You know, I’ve been reading up on this stuff online, and I heard about erectile dysfunction. Is that what you’re talking about?      I don’t know. I mean, I’ve had some issues. Not sure if it’s me or just the stress of uni. You know, like, the lectures, the deadlines, everything. It’s like my brain just can’t switch off sometimes.      I get that. I’ve had some of the same thoughts. I think it’s all the pressure of trying to keep up with everyone else. And don’t get me started on the anxiety. It’s like, every time I’m with someone, I’m thinking, “Am I doing this right?” or “Is this even going to work?”      Tell me about it. I’ve been so worried about it that I’ve been avoiding sex altogether. It’s not fun anymore. I mean, it used to be something I looked forward to, but now... It’s just this huge expectation.      I know, right? Like, someone said to me once, “If you can’t perform, just don’t.” And I was like, “That’s not fair.” It’s not like I’m trying to make it perfect, you know? I just want to feel connected.      Exactly. I think part of it is just lack of communication. Like, we don’t talk about it enough. We assume we’re both on the same page, but we’re not. I’ve been so scared to bring it up, in case it makes things awkward.      I agree. You know, maybe we should talk about it more. Like, honestly. I mean, if we’re going to be together long-term, we need to be open about these things. It’s not like we’re the only ones dealing with it. It’s just... we’re not talking about it.      Yeah, maybe. I’ve been thinking about seeing a doctor about it. I mean, it’s not like I want to be in denial. I just don’t want to be stuck in this loop of stress and anxiety over something that’s not even my fault.

So, I just got my veg box today, and I’m already loving it. That kale is so fresh, and the cauliflower cheese recipe from the leaflet is genius. I mean, it’s got that creamy texture, but it’s also low in syns. You know how much I hate cooking, but this is kind of therapeutic, honestly.      I totally get that. I’ve been trying to use that Quorn range too. I made this amazing stir-fry with it last night. It’s like it’s just pretending to be meat. But honestly, I still can’t get past the texture. I like to think of it as  meat-like , but sometimes it feels like it’s trying too hard.      Oh, I get it. I’ve tried the Quorn mince, and I can feel the difference. But I think I’m getting better at it. And hey, it’s plant-based, so it’s good for me, right? I mean, I’m still trying to keep my weight in check, and the scales have been acting up again. Last week they said I weighed 63, and then this week I’m 65. It’s like they’re conspiring against me.      Ugh, I know. I’ve got those unreliable scales too. I swear one day I’m 58, the next day I’m 62. It’s so frustrating. Anyway, I was thinking—what about our treat day Saturday? We should plan something. Maybe we can get some of that 0 calorie syrup and just have a little treat. I’m still allowed to have a glass of wine and a piece of cake, right?      Yeah, I think that’s what the Slimming World rules say. Although, I have to be careful with the artificial flavor stuff. I’m trying to cut down on that. But I still like the mint syrup. It’s so refreshing. Wait, do you remember when we were at the supermarket and the lady was yelling about ‘syns’? I tried to count them in my head while we were there, and I got so confused.      Oh, I remember. I thought the chocolate sauce was going to be a disaster, but it turned out to be the best thing ever. We had it with our vegan chocolate cake, and it was like heaven. Anyway, I’m trying to save money on groceries, so I’ve been using the frylight.

So, I've been thinking about our holiday plans for next year. I’d love to take a break from the usual routine and maybe go somewhere a bit more exotic. I’ve been meaning to visit New Zealand for ages—those landscapes are just stunning.      New Zealand sounds amazing. I’ve always wanted to go there too. But I was wondering if we could still do something closer to home. Maybe somewhere in the south of France? I’ve heard the countryside there is beautiful, and we could easily get around by train.      That’s a good idea. I love the idea of a slower pace, even if it’s not as far as New Zealand. I’d also like to visit some historical sites, like the ancient Roman ruins. I think it would be a great way to mix culture with relaxation.      I like that. But I was thinking, what if we had a hypothetical situation where we couldn’t go anywhere? Like, if we had to stay home for some reason. Would you still want to go out and do something? Or would you prefer to stay in and have a quiet day?      Honestly, I’d prefer to stay in. A perfect day for me is probably something like reading by the fire, maybe making a nice meal together, and just enjoying each other’s company. I think sometimes it’s the small moments that mean the most.      I agree. I think a perfect day for me would involve some kind of creative work—like writing or drawing. I’ve been thinking of starting a blog about travel and life lessons. Maybe that’s something we could do together? You could write the stories, and I could take the photos.      That sounds like a great idea. It could be a way to document our travels and also share some of the experiences we’ve had. But I was also thinking about tattoos. Do you ever consider getting one? I’ve been eyeing a small design on my wrist—maybe something meaningful.      I’ve thought about it, but I’m a bit scared. I like the idea of having something personal, but I’ve never been brave enough to commit. What do you think about the concept of a tattoo as a permanent reminder of something important?      I think it’s a great way to hold onto memories or values.

So, I've got a few things to discuss before we settle in for dinner. First, about the birthdays. I've been thinking about the weekend arrangements. Okay, so I was thinking about the request from the local charity about helping out with the Syrian refugees. So, I was just thinking about how things have changed since we first met. Remember when we were both first-year lecturers and thought we'd never be in a position to have a baby?      Oh, how we laughed about that! I think it was the year we both got promoted to senior lecturer roles. I meant it. You’ve always been there for me, even when I was in the thick of it with my PhD. And now, with the baby on the way, I’d say it’s the same. It’s not just about the teaching anymore; it’s about life.      Exactly. I think the thing that’s changed the most is how we’ve grown as friends. So, I was just thinking—do you ever get that feeling when you’re walking somewhere and suddenly you’re convinced the police are watching you? Like, you’re in the countryside, you’re just meandering through fields, and all of a sudden you’re like, “Oh no, have I broken the law?”      Oh, I’ve been there. I once had this experience on a train. I was sitting reading a book, and I got this weird vibe that someone was watching me. Then it hit me— it was the police . Didn’t even look like them, but I thought, “Did I just get caught doing something illegal?”      That’s terrifying! But you know, I’ve also heard some crazy superstitions about the police. Like, if you see a police car, you’re supposed to cross the road immediately—like it’s a sign of bad luck.      I remember my grandma used to say that. She said the police were like fairies who showed up when you were in trouble. Or something like that. I never really believed it, but I’ve always found superstition fascinating. Like, why do people believe in things that don’t make sense?      It’s kind of like how people used to think that if you saw a black cat, you were going to have bad luck. I guess it’s just that human thing—looking for patterns where there are none. Though I have to say, in this part of the country, I’m not sure why anyone would need to worry about the police.      True, but then again, I still remember that time when I was in university and I accidentally got caught by campus security for eating a sandwich in the library. I had no idea it was against the rules. They were so strict!      That’s the kind of thing that could happen. I once had a lecturer who was really into publicity. He used to say that if you got caught doing something, it was a publicity opportunity. Like, “Oh, you got caught eating in the library? That’s a story!”      Sounds like he lived for the spotlight. I, on the other hand, prefer the quiet life. Though I do get that it’s part of the job. I mean, we’re in the academic world, and we’re always trying to get our name out there.      Exactly. But you know, I think those superstitions—whether about the police or the university—come from a place of fear.

Dad, you remember that phone you bought last year? I think it’s still on its third battery.      Oh, I know, love. It’s been a real pain. I tried to fix it once, but now I just use my old one for texting. You’d think with all the tech these days, it’d be easier to keep things running.      Yeah, I guess. But I’m still stuck with my old phone. I got one of those fancy ones last year, and now it’s always crashing. I don’t know what’s wrong with them!      You know, I heard about this new thing called a 'smart van' that you can hire to move stuff. I was thinking, maybe I should try that. I’m thinking of taking a trip to Dorset for the steam fair. I’ve always wanted to see one of those old trains. And I thought, why not take a van and bring everything with me?      That sounds amazing! But wait, are you going with someone? I heard the fair is a big deal.      Not yet. I was hoping to meet up with your Uncle Ben and his family. He said he’s going too. But I’ve been a bit stuck on the logistics.      Maybe I can help you with that. I’ve been looking into hiring a van online. It’s about as easy as buying a phone these days.      Oh, really? Maybe I should start looking. I’ve barely left the house since the lockdown.      That’s true. But you know, I heard about this lottery win that could change your life. You should check the numbers.      Not again. I’ve already had enough of that. I’d rather spend my time on antiques. I found this old fishing reel in the attic the other day. It’s got the stamp of some guy from the 1800s.      That’s cool! I’ve always wanted to try fishing. You know what your dad used to do with that old boat?      We used to fish all the time. It was a real way of life, you know. These days, it’s all about the apps and the screens.      Yeah, I know. But I think there’s something to be said for the real thing.

So, I was just thinking about the local library again. I mean, it's such a cornerstone of the community, and now they're saying it might be demolished to make way for something else. It’s ridiculous. I wonder if there’s a way to get the community involved. Maybe a petition? I mean, if enough people show up at the council meetings, they might actually listen.      That’s a good point. It would give it that old-world charm without sacrificing comfort. I’ll check out some of the online fabric shops.

So, I've been thinking about getting a new car. My old one's starting to cough up more than it should. So, I've been thinking about getting a used car for the weekend trips. You know, the kind that’s reliable and doesn’t cost a fortune to run. So, I was just thinking about that talk I had with the boss last week. I got so stressed, I almost choked on my chicken curry. You know what I mean?      Yeah, I can relate. I’ve been feeling that way too. I mean, school’s been tough lately with exams and stuff. I don’t know how people manage with all that stress.      You know, I used to think stress was just something you felt in your head, but now I realize it’s all over the body. You can tell someone’s stressed just by looking at their face. That’s why the doctor told me to take some time off and relax.      Exactly. I’ve been reading up on stress management. Some people say you should test your stress levels with heart rate monitors or even voice analysis. Wait, does that even work?      I don’t know. I guess if you can measure it, it makes it more real, right? I mean, it’s not like we can just listen to our windpipes and figure out if we’re stressed. That sounds more like a bad joke than science.      You’re telling me. I tried talking to my brother about stress, and he just said, “You’re overthinking it.” That’s not helpful at all. I mean, we’re all Irish, right? We’re supposed to be tough and not show our emotions. But sometimes, you just need to let it out.      Hey, you know what I’ve been thinking about? The Irish present. I heard that people who are over 50 years old can get it now. I’m only 45, so I’m still waiting. Doesn’t it feel like the country’s moving on, but we’re just left behind?      Yeah, and then there’s the equal marriage vote. I don’t know how people can still be against it. It’s not like it’s a big deal anymore. It’s just about people being treated fairly.      I think it’s a huge step forward. I mean, it’s not just about marriage—it’s about equality for everyone. You know, in the UK, it’s been legal for a while, but in Ireland, it’s still a hot topic.      It’s strange how we can be so divided on some issues, but when it comes to food, we all agree. I mean, who doesn’t love a good Chinese takeaway?

So, I was just thinking about that time we drove up to the hilltop village last summer and got lost for ages. You’ve got the view, the quiet, and the sense of being above it all. I’ve been thinking about buying a place like that. Maybe somewhere near the countryside.      I agree. So, I just read this article about the new lab-grown meat thing. You know, the synthetic meat that’s being developed to replace traditional meat? It’s actually being used in some restaurants now. I think it’s called “shmeat” or something like that.      Oh yeah, I saw that too! I mean, I’ve always been on the fence about vegetarianism, but this seems like a middle ground. Like, you can still eat meat, but without all the ethical issues. But honestly, do you think people are ready for that? I mean, it’s still a bit of a weird concept to some.      I think it’s the future, honestly. Especially with the environmental impact of traditional farming. I’ve been reading about how much water and land it takes to raise cows, not to mention the greenhouse gases. Plus, I’ve seen some studies that show the carbon footprint of lab-grown meat is actually lower than that of conventional meat.      That’s true. I mean, even if you’re not a vegetarian, it’s still a way to reduce the harm you’re doing to the planet. But I also think people are a bit resistant to change. It’s not like you can just walk into a supermarket and say, “Oh, I want some lab-grown chicken.” There’s still a lot of stigma, I think.      Exactly. It’s not just about the food itself—it’s about the culture, the rituals, the taste. Like, someone who grew up eating red meat every Sunday might not be ready to switch to something that looks and feels like chicken but isn’t. I mean, it’s not even like a vegan burger. You’re still eating meat, just in a different form.      I get that. But I also think the more people start to understand the cruelty and the environmental impact, the more they’ll be open to alternatives. And I mean, if you’re against hunting, then lab-grown meat could be a win-win. No animals are harmed, and you still get what you want.      Yeah, and I know some of my friends who are vegan but still keep some meat in their diet for special occasions. I think it’s a personal choice. But I also think the more options we have, the better. I mean, I’m still taking vitamin tablets, just in case I’m not getting all the nutrients I need from my plant-based diet.

So, I just got this new phone, and it’s got all these internet features. I was thinking, maybe I should start using it more for online shopping instead of going to the shops. I mean, maybe I need to figure out what I want to do. I’ve been watching a lot of movies lately. Like, that one about a guy who starts a business and ends up rich. I mean, it’s inspiring, right?

It’s a bit overwhelming, but I think with a bit of guidance, we can figure it out.      Well, if we’re going to be planning for the future, why not start with a nice lunch?

So, I've been thinking about redecorating my bathroom. I know it's a bit of a hassle, but I want to make it more modern. Have you ever had to do that?      Oh, I've had a few bathroom renovations. They can be a bit of a nightmare, especially if you're not careful with the tradespeople. I had a plumber who completely messed up the water pipes and caused a serious leak.      Oh no! My friend John had a similar problem. He got a tiler who did a terrible job, and the whole wall ended up looking like a patchwork of different tiles.      That sounds exactly like what I went through. I ended up having to call in another tradesman just to fix the first one’s work. It cost me a fortune, and I still feel like it’s not right.      I can imagine. It’s like trying to play chess with a bunch of people who don’t know the rules. I’ve been looking into hiring a designer too – just to make sure everything looks cohesive and functional.      I think that’s a good idea. Maybe you should get some inspiration from magazines or online. I found a few sites that have some great ideas for small bathrooms. It makes the space feel more personal. Speaking of which, are you planning to do anything with your kitchen soon?      Actually, I’ve been thinking about it. You’ll be the first to know. I’m planning to get some quotes from a couple of contractors next week.

So, I was telling my wife earlier that I think I’ve finally found the perfect recipe for curry. It’s not the usual stuff from the shop, though. I’ve been experimenting with some spices I picked up from that market in Dublin.      Cool! What’s different about it? I mean, I’ve tried a few curries, but most of them just taste like the same thing.      Oh, it’s not just the spices—it’s the way you cook it.
