That sounds fancy. But I’m still not sure about the whole curry thing. I mean, I’ve had it when I was in Ireland, but it’s not really something I ever cook. I’m more of a soup or stew person.      Yeah, I can relate. I like things that are easy to make. Though I guess I should try your recipe. Maybe I’ll ask my mom for some spices. She always has a thing for cooking.      You should. And if you’re up for it, I can bring some over. I’m trying to get my kids interested in cooking too.      Mom, are we having curry tonight?      That’s what we’re talking about, little man. But you better be ready to clean your plate.      I can already tell this is going to be a great night. Maybe we should also talk about that night deposit box idea I had.      Oh no, not that again. You said that last week.      It’s a good idea! You know, like a safe place to put your money. I’ve seen those in movies.      Yeah, but how do you even get one? Is it like a secret place or something?      I think it’s more like a metal box. You put your money in it and lock it up. But I don’t know, it feels a bit like a fairy tale.      That’s the point! It’s fun to think about. It’s a way to get kids interested in saving money.      I want a deposit box. And I want to put my Legos in it.      You’re gonna have to wait till you’re older for that.

Well, I've been meaning to tell you all about that Halloween we had last year. I know it’s not the same as when I was a kid, but I still remember how we used to dress up and go door to door. I even had a sort of skeleton costume, though it was more like a paper mache thing, and I felt like I was haunting the whole neighborhood.      Oh, I remember when I was your age too. I used to love it. My mum would always make us a nice treat, and we’d collect all the sweets. But I suppose now with the kids, it’s more about them having fun and not worrying about the candy. Although, I still think it's amazing that kids today still get excited about it. I mean, it’s not like they have real ghosts or anything!      I think it’s still a great way to bring the community together. When I was teaching, I used to take the kids out for Halloween parties, and it was always a blast. We’d have a costume contest and a few spooky decorations. I even got into the spirit a bit, dressed up as a wizard for one year. It was a bit over the top, but the kids loved it.      Yeah, I think it’s still super fun. I got dressed up as a witch last year because I thought it was cool. My friends thought I was actually going to cast a spell or something. But honestly, I just wanted to be the spooky one. I guess it’s also a way to get out of the house and have some fun. Although, I’d rather have a Halloween party than go trick-or-treating because I’m not really into the whole knocking on doors thing. I’m more of a “stay in the house and decorate” type of person.      That’s a good point. I think we’ve all changed a bit, but the spirit of Halloween still lives on. Speaking of which, did you all hear about the horse-riding event coming up at the local equestrian center? I heard there’s a special event for kids and adults. I’ve always wanted to try riding again, but I’ve never been confident enough. It’s a bit scary, but I think it might be a good way to get out and do something different.

So, I just got a ticket for parking in a disabled space at the fair. I thought it was a disabled zone, but turns out it was just a regular one. I saw someone with a mobility aid and thought, “I can do this,” but then realized it was a mistake.      Oh, I remember when I was younger, I got pulled over for something like that too. I was in a hurry to get to the fair and didn’t realize the signs were different. It’s just so confusing now with all these different zones and rules.      It reminds me of the time when I tried to get a disabled parking permit. The council took forever to process it, and by the time I got it, I realized I didn’t even need it anymore. I was still walking, but I guess it’s better to be safe than sorry.      Yeah, I feel like disability parking is a bit of a mess in general. People get confused about what qualifies, and then there’s always the issue of the spaces being taken by someone who doesn’t even deserve them. I mean, it’s not fair for people with real needs to be stuck in a regular space.      It’s not just parking, though. I’ve been thinking about the housing situation for elderly people. I mean, I know my mum is getting older, and she’s not moving out, but I worry about what will happen when she needs more support. There’s just not enough proper housing for people who need it.      That’s exactly what I was saying. I work in care, and I see firsthand how hard it is for people to get suitable housing. I know a few people who have had to move into care homes because they couldn’t afford a house that was accessible. It’s not just about the cost—it’s about the availability.      And the council housing system is a joke. I’ve heard friends talk about waiting years for a council flat, and when they do get one, it’s in a terrible area. It’s like they’re just trying to get people out of the city and into the countryside with no real support.      You’re not wrong. I’ve been on benefits for years, and I’ve seen how the system doesn’t really support people who are in need.

So, I've been thinking about getting an allotment. I've had this idea for a while now, but I've been too busy with teaching and my own garden. I mean, I have a small patch in the back, but I feel like I could do so much more.      That sounds like a great idea! I actually have an allotment myself, and it's been a lifesaver. It’s not just about growing food—it's a way to unwind and connect with nature. You should definitely go for it.      Thanks, I’d love to. I just don’t know where to start. I’ve heard allotments can be tricky to get hold of, especially in the city. I’m not even sure if there’s one available near where I live.      Oh, there are plenty. I know a few in the South of England. I even helped a friend find one through a local council website. You just need to be persistent. They often have waiting lists, but if you’re flexible with the size or the location, you’ll find something.      That’s reassuring. I’ve been meaning to check the local council’s website, but I’ve been procrastinating. I’m a little nervous about what I’ll need to bring. Do you need a lot of equipment?      Not really. Allotments usually provide basic tools like spades and gloves, but it’s a good idea to bring your own if you have them. You might also want a tarp for covering plants when it rains and some compost. Oh, and don’t forget to bring your own seeds or seedlings—there’s a lot of variety available.      I think I’ll start with some vegetables I like, like tomatoes and beans. I’ve heard they’re relatively easy to grow for beginners. I just need to figure out the best time to plant them.      Exactly. Timing is key. I usually plant tomatoes in April or May, depending on the weather. If you’re starting early, maybe you can get some seedlings from the local nursery. It’s also a good idea to check with the allotment owner for any rules or guidelines.      That makes sense. I’ll start looking into it soon. I think once I get the hang of it, it’ll be so rewarding. I can’t wait to see what I can grow!      You’ll be amazed at what you can do.

So, I was just thinking, have you ever had that moment where you’re like, “I need to plan something, but I just don’t know what?” Like, where are we even going to go this weekend?      Oh, I’ve had that! I was just sitting on the couch the other day, scrolling through social media, and I thought, “I need to do something, but I don’t even know what.” It’s so annoying, isn’t it?      Yeah, totally. I mean, I’m in Doncaster, and I’ve got a bunch of friends here, but I’m still like, “Where can we go that’s not the same old places?” I feel like everything is so predictable. You know, the usual pubs, the same cafes, and I’m like, “Where’s the adventure?”      I know what you mean. I feel like in Cambridge, everything’s so different, but we’re still stuck in this loop of “let’s go to the park” or “let’s have a picnic.” I think maybe we should try something different. What about that new art gallery that opened up in the town center? I heard it’s pretty cool.      Oh, I remember that! I’ve been meaning to go, but I just haven’t had the time. You know how it is—between uni work and hanging out with the lads. But, hey, if you want to go, I’m in. That could be a good plan.      That would be awesome! I’ve got a few friends from uni who might be free, too. I’ll text them and see if they can come. Maybe we can even get a few burgers or something after. You know, to celebrate the adventure.      Yeah, burgers and art. Sounds like the perfect combo. I’m just worried about the weather. Doncaster is known for its weather, right?      Oh, I know. It’s always either raining or freezing. But maybe that’s the charm? I mean, if you’re going to do something, you might as well do it in the rain. It adds to the vibe.      True. I’ll bring an umbrella just in case. And maybe a thermos of tea. It’s all part of the plan.      A thermos of tea? You’re telling me you’re planning this out like it’s a military operation?      Only in the best way. You know, it’s not just about going out—it’s about making the most of it.

So, I was just thinking about that game we tried to play last night. That one with the weird alien creatures? You remember, the one where you had to collect all the keys to escape the spaceship?      Oh yeah, that was a real nightmare! I got stuck in the third level for like an hour. I kept trying to find that key, but it was like it was hiding in plain sight.      That’s why you need to play the game when you're not exhausted. I tried it last night and barely made it through the first level. I was so tired from studying, I just gave up and watched some videos instead.      I did the same. I watched a documentary on the history of gaming. It turned out to be way more interesting than the game itself. Wait, did you guys know that the first video game was made in the 1950s?      Really? I thought it was like the 1980s or something.      Yeah, it was called  Tennis for Two , and it was basically a simulation of a tennis match on a computer. Pretty basic stuff, but it was a start.      Oh, I did a project on that for my history class. The teacher said it was a big deal because it helped pave the way for modern gaming. Like, it was the first time people interacted with a computer in a fun way.      That’s true. I mean, it’s about how far we’ve come. I remember the days when all we had was a Game Boy and some cartridges. Now it’s all high-definition, online multiplayer, and VR. It’s crazy how fast things have changed.      Yeah, I used to play on a Nintendo 64. I still have that controller. You can’t even play the games anymore, but I keep it as a memento.      I still have my Game Boy. I got it from my cousin when he moved away. It’s got some scratches, but it still works. I think I’ll keep it for a while.      I’m actually thinking about getting a PlayStation 5. I’ve been saving up for it. I’ve had my eye on that new FIFA game.      That’s a good idea. I’m going to check out the new  Call of Duty  game. I heard it’s pretty intense.      Let’s see who’s the best at it when we play together.

So, I was just thinking, do you remember that time we went to that film festival in Bristol? It was the one with all those indie films. I still remember that one about the old man who tried to make a film with his grandkids. It was so heartfelt, wasn't it?      Oh, I remember that one! It really touched me. But honestly, I couldn’t get over that scene where the granddad tried to fix the camera, and it kept breaking. It was so funny yet so sad at the same time. You know, it made me think about how we all have these little quirks, even if we don’t realize it.      Exactly! It’s like that movie,  The Pursuit of Happyness , you know? I mean, the struggles, the persistence, and the hope. Sometimes life feels like that – you’re just trying to make it through, and then suddenly you’re in a situation where you’re not even sure if you’re getting anywhere.      Yeah, I think that’s why that movie resonated with me so much. I was going through a tough time in my job a while back, and it reminded me that even when things aren’t going well, you can still keep going. But I have to say, I’m still not sure about that last film we saw together. The one with the time loop? It was so cliché, wasn’t it?      Oh, I know! I couldn’t help but laugh at the whole thing. It was like they thought we were all still in the 90s. But hey, I guess some people still like that kind of thing. I mean, I did enjoy the ending though – the twist with the wife? That was clever.      Yeah, it was a bit of a letdown, but I’ll give it that. I think I’m just getting tired of films that don’t really challenge me. I prefer stories that make me think, you know? Like those dramas that deal with real issues. I was reading about this new film coming out about mental health. It’s supposed to be really powerful.      That sounds interesting. I’m always up for something that makes you feel something. Although, I do miss the old days when we’d just go to the cinema and not worry about what the film was about. Just sit back, relax, and enjoy the story.

So, I just got back from this weekend trip to the spa. I know it's not exactly the first thing you'd think of when you're hanging out with friends, but it was actually pretty chill.      Oh, a spa? That sounds like a great escape. I was in the middle of an interview last week and felt like I was about to lose my mind. It was like a job interview that never ended.      I can imagine. I used to dread interview days, but now I’ve gotten used to the pressure. Didn’t you get into the new editorial role?      Yeah, I did. I’m still getting used to the pace, but it’s a good challenge. Although, I did get a bit annoyed when the team started talking about the  Undateables  last week.      Oh, the dating show? I still can’t get over that. I mean, everyone has a story, but some of the people on there are just… wow. I once had a friend who tried to date someone from the show and it turned into a disaster.      Honestly, I’ve seen it all. I think the worst part is when they start talking about their "bad experiences" in relationships. It’s so dramatic.      I know, right? But I guess it’s the kind of show that people love to binge-watch. Speaking of binge-watching, have you seen the new series that came out? It’s about friends and board games.      I haven’t. I’m still catching up on my DVDs from the last few months. I’ve been trying to get through that stack of old films.      That’s the thing about DVDs—once you start a movie, you can’t stop. I know I’ve been guilty of that. Maybe we should do a board game night next week.      That sounds like a plan. I’ve got a few board games that I haven’t played in ages. I remember we used to play  Ticket to Ride  all the time. It’s always been one of our favorites.      Yeah, I’d love that. I’ve been thinking about it for a while now. It’s one of those things that brings everyone together.      Hey, that’s a great idea. I can bring some snacks and drinks. It’ll be like old times.      We’ll have to make sure we all agree on the games.

So, I was just thinking—should we get a new washing machine? The old one’s been giving us trouble for ages. I mean, it’s not exactly  dying  or anything, but it’s starting to feel like it’s working against us.      Honestly, I think it’s time. I’ve been meaning to suggest it for weeks. My mum had one of those old models that only worked if you yelled at it. I don’t want to go through that again.      Oh, come on, you’re not serious. That’s just your mum’s drama. My aunt once told me that her washing machine used to  choke  on socks. It’s like the appliances are all just living with us now.      Yeah, and I don’t know about you, but I’m not going to risk my favorite t-shirts getting ruined because I forgot to close the door. It’s not worth it.      Fair point. I guess we should look into a new one. I mean, I’ve been thinking about getting a new fridge too. My current one smells like old socks and regret.      You’re not going to get away with that. I saw you put the onion in the fridge the other day. You know it’s not supposed to be there.      I did not! I swear, I put it in the bin! Or maybe the microwave? I can’t remember. But I also can’t remember why I thought that was a good idea.      It’s not funny. You’re supposed to be a  research manager . You’re supposed to have  control . That’s the kind of thing that makes you lose your job.      Okay, okay. I’ll take it down. But seriously, I think we should plan for the new washing machine. Maybe we can even celebrate with a movie night. I’ve been meaning to catch that new film about time travel.      That sounds perfect. I’ve been dying to see it. I even got a ticket for the midnight showing. But I’m not going unless you’re coming.      Deal. But I’m bringing my snacks. I’ve got these weird trail mix things made with my mum’s recipe. She says it’s good for the brain.      You mean the one that tastes like a mix of regret and cheap candy? I’ll take one. But only if you promise not to overdo it.

So, I've been thinking about moving house again. I mean, it's not like I have much money, but I've been meaning to get out of this place for a while.      Oh, really? That’s interesting. I've been meaning to talk to you about that. Have you considered the market in the north? I heard house prices have been more stable lately compared to the south.      Yeah, I’ve heard that too. It's funny, isn't it? All the talk about the south being the place to be, but with the VW scandal and everything, I guess people are starting to realize that not everything is perfect out there.      I know, I know. The VW scandal’s been a real eye-opener for a lot of people, especially those who bought cars from there. It's made me think a lot about how things are going in the economy. I mean, with the housing market, it's like you're always chasing something, but the prices are just so high.      Exactly. I feel like the media always keeps telling us about the north being a better place to live, but when it comes to the economy, it's still not the same. I remember when I was in university, people always said the south was the best, but now I'm in the north, and I have to say, there's a lot to like.      I’d say the north is starting to come into its own. I mean, I've been in the oil industry, and I've seen the shifts. It's not all doom and gloom. The government’s pushing for more investment in the north, and I think it's working. But the problem is, people still have this idea that you have to be in London to be successful.      That’s the thing, isn’t it? I mean, I grew up in Dublin, so I always thought the south was the way to go, but now I'm in Cumbria, and I can see the differences. The cost of living’s lower, and the people are more friendly. It’s just a different vibe.      And the house prices. I mean, even if you're not wealthy, it's more manageable here. I mean, I'm not in the same boat as you, but I know people who’ve managed to get on the property ladder in the north.

Well, I've had enough of this. I've been watching the news for the last hour, and it's all about rising living costs and the poor state of public services. I've had enough of people complaining about everything, but no one seems to be doing anything about it.      I know, I know. I’ve been reading the papers too. It's all very upsetting. The government keeps talking about helping the working class, but when you're retired and on a pension, there's not much you can do. It's like they don’t even care about people like us anymore.      Oh, I’m sorry to hear that, but I think it's more about the pension system itself. I mean, I’ve been on my pension for a few years now, and I still feel like I’m getting the short end of the stick. Living costs have gone up, and yet the pension doesn’t keep up. It’s just not enough.      Exactly. I remember when I was working, I had a decent salary, and I thought that once I retired, things would get easier. But now, I’m stuck in this cycle of rising bills and falling income. It's like the government is trying to push us out of our homes and into the streets.      That’s not fair, and I know it’s not just us. I’ve been talking to my neighbor, and he’s in the same boat. We both used to work, and now we’re just sitting here, trying to make ends meet. I wish there was some sort of support out there for people like us.      I know, but I think people are just too afraid to speak out. I mean, the younger generation might not care as much, but I can see the frustration in their eyes. I think we need to organize, somehow. Maybe we can start a group, like a local support network for retirees.      That’s a good idea. It could give us all a voice. I’ve been thinking about joining a local community center too, just to stay active. I’ve always liked being around people, and I think it would help with the loneliness.      Yeah, I agree. I’ve been thinking about that too. I’ve been staying at a bed and breakfast just to keep my mind off things.

So, I just saw this video online about evolution and human development. It was super interesting, but honestly, I got confused halfway through. Like, how do we even know all this stuff?      Yeah, I saw that too. I mean, it's all about DNA and how humans evolved from apes or something, right? But I still don’t get how they figure all that out. I mean, how do they even know what happened millions of years ago?      Oh, it’s all based on fossils, genetics, and comparisons between species. Like, they look at the bones and DNA of different animals and see how they match up. It’s like solving a puzzle.      Yeah, but I still think it’s kind of weird. I mean, if we evolved from monkeys, why are we so different? And what even defines a “monkey”?      That’s a good question. I mean, I guess it’s more about how we share common ancestors, not that we descended directly from monkeys. Like, we’re all part of the same family tree.      I get that, but it’s still confusing. I mean, I’ve heard people say that evolution is just a theory. Does that mean it’s not real?      No, it’s not just a theory—it’s a scientific explanation supported by a ton of evidence. Like, if you're a biologist, you can’t just say “this is how it happened” without proof. But I guess some people don’t like it because it challenges their beliefs.      I mean, it’s not just about evolution. It’s also about how people treat each other. Like, I’ve seen a lot of stuff online where people get really defensive about what they believe. It’s like, you can’t even have a conversation without someone getting upset.      That’s true. I’ve noticed a lot of people online are really into feminism or religion, and they can’t stand the other side. It’s like, “You’re not even allowed to disagree.”      Yeah, and sometimes it’s just based on stereotypes. Like, I’ve heard people say women can’t be scientists or something. That’s so outdated. I mean, if you look at female scientists, they’re just as smart as anyone else.      Exactly. And it’s not just about gender. I’ve heard people say things like “they don’t even deserve to be in this country” just because of the color of their skin.

So, how’s your MOT going? I heard you were supposed to get it done last week.      Oh, I got it done this morning. Turned out the mechanic said I had a few things to fix—brakes, lights, and the exhaust. I was dreading it, but I reckon it’s worth it.      I had mine done a month ago. They said my car is in reasonable condition. But you know, I still don’t trust those machines. I always feel like they’re just trying to get more money out of you.      You’re not wrong. My car’s been in the shop more times than I can count. I told the guy I was gonna get it done and I’ll be back in a month, and he just smiled and said, “You’ll be back when you’re ready.”      Sounds like a fair deal. You know, I was thinking about getting my car checked too. I’ve been putting it off for ages. Between work and the kids, it’s just been slipping my mind.      I get that. I was doing the same. But once you get it done, you feel better. And it’s one less thing to worry about.      Speaking of things to worry about, I had a hospital appointment this week. They found something on my scan. Not sure what it is yet, but I’m going for another one next week.      That’s not good. Are you okay?      I’m fine, but they said I need to take more tablets. I’ve been on some for a while, but I still feel like I’m on a medication merry-go-round.      I know what you mean. I take a bunch of tablets too. It’s just part of life these days, isn’t it?      It’s one of the things I miss about being younger. I used to run with the kids and the dogs, and go out on weekends. Now I’m always tied up with work or helping out with the family.      I can relate. I used to play rugby in my younger days. Still do, actually. It’s the only thing that keeps me moving.      That’s a good thing. You know, I tried acupuncture for my back pain. It worked better than any pill.      Really? I’ve heard about it, but I’ve never tried it. Maybe I should give it a go.

You know, the people who lived in the Americas a long time ago didn't always have the same rights as everyone else. Some people were treated very unfairly because of the color of their skin.      What do you mean,  Mummy ? Why didn’t they have the same rights?      Well, a long time ago, there was a system called slavery. It meant that some people were forced to work for others without being paid. It was a very bad thing, and it happened in many places, including the Americas.      Was that like when people are taken away from their home?      Yes, in some cases. People were taken from their homes and forced to work on plantations or in other dangerous jobs. They weren’t allowed to live freely, and they couldn’t choose where they wanted to go or who they wanted to be with.      That sounds really sad. Why did people do that?      A lot of people believed that some people were less important than others, just because of the color of their skin. That was wrong and cruel. It’s important to remember that people should be treated equally, no matter who they are or where they come from.      So, did people fight back against that?      Yes, many people did. They organized movements and worked together to end slavery. It took a long time, but eventually, laws were created to protect people from being treated like that.      I think that’s why we learn about it in school. It’s important to know what happened so we don’t repeat the same mistakes.      Exactly. And it’s also important to remember that there have been other times in history when people have fought for freedom and equality, like during wars. But I think the most important thing is to always stand up for what’s right.      So, is that why we have rules now?      In part, yes. But rules are just one part of it. It’s also about how we treat each other every day.      I think I understand now. It’s about fairness, isn’t it?      Yes, it is. And it’s something we can always work on, no matter how old we get. It’s what makes our world better.      I like that. I want to help make things fair.      Then you’re already on the right path. Well done, my little heroes. ✨      We’re heroes?

So, what do you think of the new series on BBC2? I’ve been trying to catch up with it, but it’s been a bit of a struggle between football and this show.      I’ve seen a few episodes. It’s a bit slow at times, but the character development is really good. I think it’s got a lot of potential. I’ve been telling my cousin about it—they’re a big fan of dramas.      Yeah, I’ve heard it’s one of the best of the year. Didn’t you say the lead actor was in a few big films before?      He was in a couple of independent films, but I think the show is more about the storytelling. I think it’s got a lot of heart.      That’s the thing about British drama—it always manages to pull you in. I remember when I was working late shifts, I’d watch some of these shows to unwind.      Aye, I used to watch a lot when I was working in catering. I’d always have a pint and catch up with some decent telly. But since I’ve retired, I’ve started reading more.      That’s a good way to spend your time. I’m actually planning to start a book club with some friends. We’re going to read  House of Leaves  next. It’s a bit intense, but I think we’d all enjoy it.      That sounds like a great idea. I’ve read a few of those types of books before. It can be a bit confusing at first, but once you get into it, it’s really rewarding.      I still haven’t finished  The Da Vinci Code . I got halfway through and got stuck. I think it’s a classic, but I’m just not into that kind of mystery stuff.      That’s okay. You can always come to my book club. We don’t do too much waiting. I’m reading  The Alchemist  right now.      Oh, I’ve heard of that one! It’s supposed to be inspiring, right?      Aye, it’s got a message that stays with you. I think it’s one of those books that you read once and then keep coming back to.      I’ve been reading a lot of autobiographies lately. It’s interesting to see how people from different backgrounds ended up where they are.      That’s a good angle.

Okay, I've got the dishwasher all unloaded. Let me just put the plates in the rack. Oh, look at these mugs—so much better than the ones we had last week.      Mum, those aren’t the same mugs. They’re the ones we had on the shelf since  Harry Potter  started. Remember when we watched the first movie and thought it was going to be just a regular film?      Yeah, I thought it was a movie about a wizard! I was like, “Why is there a magical train?” But then I got hooked. I even memorized all the spells.      Well, you were only five at the time, so I guess you had to start somewhere. But I still remember the first time I saw the movie. It was like seeing the world through a magical lens.      And then there was the steam engine. I mean,  George Stephenson —the man who invented the first practical steam locomotive. I still remember the first time I saw a model of the  Rocket  in the museum. It looked like a dragon.      Wait, wasn’t that the one that won the Rainhill Trials? I think it was called the  Rocket . I remember my dad telling me about how it was the first real steam engine that could actually move people.      Exactly! And it wasn’t just about the engine. It was about the whole idea of connecting places. People could travel faster, goods could move more efficiently. It changed the world.      It’s funny how things like that come up in conversation. I was just thinking about George Stephenson the other day when we were watching  Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban . There’s this scene where the Ministry of Magic uses some kind of advanced transportation.      Yeah, I thought it was just a magical shortcut. But then I realized it was like the steam engine—except with magic. Like, instead of coal, they use spells.      Exactly! It’s the same idea—innovation, progress, connecting people. Whether it’s a steam engine or a magical portkey, it’s all about getting from one place to another.      And let’s not forget the Hogwarts Express! That’s the real one. It’s like the original steam engine, but with a sprinkle of magic.      I think I prefer the real one, though. I mean, I can’t even ride a broomstick without falling over.      Well, you’re not 10 yet.

So, I just got a message from my sister saying her Words With Friends score has gone up again. I’m starting to think she’s cheating.      Nah, she’s just finally getting the hang of it. Remember when she used to lose every game? Now she’s the top player in our group.      Yeah, I remember. But I still think she’s using some kind of app to get hints. I mean, it’s not like she’s actually reading the board.      You’re just envious because you lost to her last week. Besides, the real issue here is that you haven’t even played since university. You’ve been too busy working on your thesis.      I’ve been busy, okay? I’m in the final stages of my master’s. But seriously, if I had time, I’d definitely be better at Words With Friends.      You’d be better if you stopped blaming your phone for everything. I’ve been working in a café for a while now, and I’ve seen people lose their minds over coffee orders.      You’re a barista, not a chef. I mean, you know the difference between a latte and a flat white?      Oh, I know the difference. I just don’t have the patience for people who order them wrong.      Maybe you should start a supper club. You could charge people for being rude.      I’d charge them double. I’ve had enough of people who don’t know what they want.      I know what you mean. I run a café, and I’ve had customers ask for “a bit of everything” on their toast. Like, what does that even mean? Do they want bacon, eggs, jam, and avocado?      Yeah, that’s the kind of thing that makes me want to throw the menu across the room.      Don’t go there. You’ll end up like me, with a legal issue over a wrong order. I had a customer who sued me for not giving them what they ordered. It was ridiculous.      Did you really?      It was a guy who ordered a "large extra cheese pizza" and got a small one. He claimed it was a breach of contract.      I could see that happening. You’re just like me—too generous with your customers.      I’m not that bad. I just like people to be happy.      That’s the problem. You’re too nice.

So, how's life treating you these days, Emma? I haven’t seen you around much lately. You’ve been buried under work or something?      Oh, you know, it’s been pretty hectic. I’ve been dealing with some IT issues at work, and I’ve had to extend my hours a bit more. But it’s manageable. How about you? You seem to have a bit of a schedule too.      I’m keeping busy, yeah. The cover supervisor job is never dull. I’ve had to step in for a few days when the main staff were off, which means I’ve been running around like a headless chicken. Still, I’ve been trying to fit in some time for myself.      That sounds exhausting. I know what you mean, though. I’ve been trying to make time for hobbies too. I’ve been into photography again, actually. I took some pictures of the campus garden last week and they came out pretty well. Maybe I should start a portfolio.      That’s great! I’ve always thought photography is a beautiful hobby. I’ve never really got into it, though. I’m more of a foodie. I love cooking, especially experimenting with new recipes. Have you ever tried making anything new?      Honestly, I haven’t been much of a cook. I rely on takeout most of the time. But I’ve been wanting to change that. Maybe I should try something simple, like making pasta. I’ve read some recipes online, and I think I could give it a go this weekend.      That’s a good idea. You know, I made a chicken and leek pie the other day, and it turned out really well. It’s not fancy, but it’s comforting. Speaking of food, have you tried any good local places around here?      Not really. I’ve been sticking to the campus cafes. I think I should explore more. There’s a farm shop nearby, and I’ve heard they have really good fresh produce. Maybe I’ll check it out this week.      That sounds like a plan. And don’t forget, you’re not alone. If you ever go for a walk with the kids, or if you need help with anything, just let me know. We’re colleagues, but we’re also friends.      Thanks, Lucy. I appreciate that. I think I’ll take you up on that offer.

So, I just saw a baby blanket that looks like it's made of clouds. I almost bought it, but then I thought, “No, I need something practical, not a mood ring for my sofa.”      You’re in a baby mood again, aren’t you? I swear, since you started thinking about having kids, every product in this shop has a tiny face on it.      Yeah, and don’t get me started on the wine. I almost bought a bottle called “Baby’s First Mimosas.” I thought, “Okay, who’s gonna drink that?” But then I realized, it’s for when the baby’s old enough to sip on juice.      I’d rather drink water, thanks. I mean, the water here is so good, it’s like it’s been through a spa. You know, the kind that makes you feel like you’re in the mountains?      I know, right? I’ve been thinking about getting a water filter for home. It’s one of those things that’s not as important as buying a new sofa, but still... it’s on my list.      Yeah, but we’re in Preston, not the Alps. Still, water’s water. I’ve been telling my kids, “If you want to live well, you’ve got to drink well.”      But I’m not even a kid anymore. I’m a student, and I’d rather have a coffee than a bottle of expensive water. Although, I did get a free sample at the shop. It’s like a type of mineral water that smells like the sea. I almost named it “Mum’s Surprise.”      You’re so creative, you know that? I’d call it “Mum’s Mistake.” But anyway, the point is, we’re all here for the baby stuff, right?      Yeah, but also to check out the renovations. I’m thinking about moving out of the old house and into something newer. It’s getting a bit too close to the road for my liking.      Oh, really? You’re thinking about moving? I thought you were happy with your house.      I am, but it’s time for a change. I’ve been doing this customer service job for years, and I think I’m ready for something different. Maybe something that doesn’t involve so much talking to people all day.      You’ve got a point. I’ve been thinking of going back to college.

Hey, did you see that new internet game that came out last week? I’ve been playing it non-stop. It’s like a mix of strategy and adventure. I can’t get enough of it!      Oh, the one with those giant robots? I tried it for a day, but I got stuck on level three. I didn’t even know what I was doing. You don’t need to be a genius to play, do you?      Yeah, I think it’s designed to be tough on purpose. I’ve been watching some YouTube walkthroughs. You just have to learn the controls and the mechanics. But honestly, I’m not into games like that. I’d rather read a book or something.      I know, I get that. But I find it so engaging. It’s like solving a puzzle every time. And the story is amazing. I even started feeling like I was in the world of the game.      That’s what worries me. I think I’m starting to feel a bit like I’m losing touch with real life. I’ve been up late playing and then just falling asleep at my desk. I need to take a break.      You’re not the only one. I’ve noticed that too. I’ve been feeling a bit down lately, like I’m not sure what I want to do with my life. Should I go back to university or just take a job?      That’s a big decision. I’m still in university, so I can relate. But honestly, I think it’s okay to take time. You don’t have to rush. Maybe you can explore your options.      I wish I had that time. I’ve been working for years now, and I feel like I’m just going through the motions. I used to love traveling, but I haven’t gone anywhere in ages.      I totally get that. Travel is so important. I’ve been meaning to go to Scotland for a while now. I hear the countryside is beautiful this time of year.      Yeah, I’ve been reading about it. I think I’d love to go there for Christmas. I’ve been feeling a bit homesick lately, even though I’m in my own country. It’s weird.      I can understand that. Christmas is such a big deal for family and traditions. I think we should all plan a trip together this year.

Okay, so I was thinking about metals and fabrics the other day, and it made me remember when I was a kid. I used to love making little gadgets out of scrap metal and old fabric scraps. I even made a tiny robot out of a tin can and some string. It was ridiculous, but it worked!      Was it really? I mean, I just wear clothes, not make things. But I do like Minecraft. I’ve been playing a lot lately, building castles and exploring. I found this new world with all these different metals—like gold, iron, and even some rare ones I’ve never seen before. I’m trying to collect them all!      Cool! I like Minecraft too, but I’m still learning. I’m trying to make a sword, but I keep breaking them. I think I need the right type of metal. Wait, aren’t there special recipes for that?      Oh, yes! In real life, the type of metal you use determines the strength and flexibility of the object. For example, steel is stronger than iron, but you have to mix it with carbon. I remember learning that in one of my postgrad classes. It’s fascinating how the properties of metals can change based on their composition.      That’s really cool! I guess it’s like how fabrics work too. Like, wool is warm, but cotton is more breathable. I use different fabrics for my Minecraft clothes too. I made a robe out of velvet and a cape out of silk. It looks super fancy!      I made a sword out of leather and a stick. It’s not great, but I like it. I also found this legend in Minecraft about a treasure chest that’s hidden in the mountains. I think it’s a made-up story, but it’s fun to imagine.      Legends are great, they’re like the stories we tell to make things more interesting. I remember a legend from my childhood about a magical stone that could turn any metal into gold. It was obviously a myth, but it got me really excited about metals and their properties.      I think I’ve heard that one too. Maybe it’s a common legend. I like how the stories make things more magical. I also started taking vitamins recently. I feel more energetic now, even though I’m still not sure if it’s all that helpful.

So, I was just telling my mates about the time I saw this guy in the park with a guitar, and I thought he was just some random guy playing for fun. Turns out, he was in a local band and they’re actually pretty good!      Yeah, I remember hearing about that band. They were at the gig last week, weren’t they? I think they’re starting to get some attention.      Exactly! They’ve got that raw, authentic sound. I mean, it’s not like the polished stuff you hear on the radio. It feels real. I’m still trying to figure out how to play even one chord properly, though.      You’re not the only one. I’ve been trying for months, and I still can’t get the tuning right. But hey, if you’re going to be a musician, you’ve got to start somewhere.      Yeah, I guess. Although, I’m not sure I want to go down that path. I mean, I’d rather just be a casual player, not a professional. But it’s fun to try.      You know, I got into it because of my brother. He plays in a band and he’s really into it. I mean, he’s not the best, but he’s passionate. It’s infectious, you know?      I get that. It’s like a rush, isn’t it? You’re creating something from nothing. But, hey, I’ve got to be honest—I’m not exactly sure how I feel about about all this.      You mean about… stuff?      Yeah, you know, the whole social scene. I mean, I’ve heard some stuff about people being shady, like that guy at the bar the other night.      You mean the one who was acting really weird?      Yeah, he was asking questions about the band and then just left without saying a word. It’s a bit creepy, honestly. I mean, I wouldn’t say he was a paedophile, but I’m not exactly sure what he was doing.      I get it. It’s all so confusing. You’ve got to be careful where you go and who you talk to. It’s not like we’re in the middle of some crime-ridden area, but you never know.      Guess that’s just part of being in a place like this. You never really know what’s going on. But, you know, it’s still better than being in a city, right?

So, I heard you mentioned the Montenegro trip last week. Are we really going? I mean, it’s got to be amazing, but I’m still trying to wrap my head around the logistics.      Yeah, we are! I got the confirmation yesterday. The school is funding it through the EPQ project, so we’re all set. But I still can’t believe we’re going to a country that’s not even in Europe. Wait, isn’t it in the Balkans?      Yeah, and it’s got that cool vibe. I remember reading about the history there. It’s like a mix of old and new. I think it’s the perfect place to do our EPQ about cultural exchange. Speaking of which, did you get your topic settled, Speaker_1?      Not yet. I’m still trying to decide between something on vegetarianism and something on teaching. I’ve been thinking about how people’s eating habits change in different cultures. It’s kind of tied into my interest in humanitarianism.      That sounds like a solid angle. I mean, vegetarianism is such a hot topic these days. Especially with all the climate change stuff. But then again, I’m not sure how much of a difference it really makes.      I think it does, especially in big cities. I mean, I’ve seen how many people are cutting out meat for ethical reasons. But then again, I’m not a vegetarian myself. I just think it’s important to be aware of the impact of our choices.      Yeah, I get that. It’s not just about what you eat, but  why  you eat it. I’ve been thinking about how food is tied to identity and tradition too. Like, how some people in my family grow up eating certain things because of their culture.      That’s true. And I think that’s why cooking can be such a powerful way to learn about other cultures. Speaking of which, have you thought about trying some vegetarian recipes for the trip?      Definitely. I’ve been experimenting with some Indian and Middle Eastern dishes. They’re all plant-based, and I think they’ll be a great addition to our food journal for the EPQ.      That sounds awesome. Maybe we can swap recipes? I’ve been trying to make some vegan muffins, but I’m not sure if they turn out right.      Yeah, I can help with that.

So, I just got a text from my sister saying her new flatmate paid her 20 quid to borrow a kettle. Are you  kidding  me? That’s not even fair!      Yeah, I can’t believe it. She’s like, “It’s just a kettle, it’s not like it’s a rare item or anything.” I mean, it’s not even  new —it’s like, 15 years old.      Oh, come on, don’t be dramatic. I had a flatmate who charged me  £5  for a cup of tea once. That was in the middle of the night, too. I was like, “Are you trying to start a business?”      Man, I’d charge him more than that. I’d say, “You want tea? Fine, but you’re paying me for the sugar too.” My mates say I’m the most  unreasonable  person in the whole university, but I don’t care. I’m not short-changing my flatmates.      You’re not unreasonable, you’re just  realistic . I mean, we all know this is uni, right? We’re not rich, and if we’re not careful, we’ll end up paying for everything. Like, what’s the deal with the rent again? I think it’s gone up another £100 a month.      Yeah, and the groceries? It’s like we’re being charged for  every  single item in the shop. I swear, if I had to pay for everything, I’d just move out and get a room in a hostel. That would be cheaper.      You know what, I tried that. For a week. Then I realized I was paying  more  for the room because I was sharing with strangers. Plus, no Wi-Fi. You can’t even get a good signal in that place. I’m back here, trying to study, and the whole flat’s like a warzone. I’m not even sure if I can afford to keep paying the deposit on time.      I just started working part-time at the campus café, so I’m getting at least some money in. It’s not much, but it helps. I think I’m going to start budgeting like crazy this term. I can’t afford to be broke again.      I know, I know. But you know what’s the worst? The things we don’t even think about. Like, the flatmate who’s always using the Wi-Fi and never pays their share.

So, I was just telling my sister-in-law about that time I tried to teach Christmas carols to a group of kids in Barcelona. You remember how I got so excited about it?      Oh yes, I remember! I was so proud of you. You were so enthusiastic, and I think it actually helped the kids connect with the spirit of the season.      Exactly! I mean, they were so young, but they started singing along, even though some of the words were in Spanish. It was like a little cultural exchange. It reminded me how much I love teaching, even when it’s just a group of kids in a tiny village.      You always have a way of making everything feel special. I remember when we were kids, you used to dress up as Santa and leave cookies for the neighbors. It was such a sweet tradition.      Oh, I still do that! Well, not exactly Santa, but I try to bring a little joy to others. I think that’s what being a teacher is all about—you leave something behind, even if it’s just a smile.      That’s the spirit. I think that’s why I always wanted to work in consultancy, too. You know, helping people find their own paths. Sometimes, it’s not just about the job—it’s about the people you work with and the connections you make.      That’s true. I’ve always said that teaching is a bit like consultancy. You have to adapt, you have to listen, and you have to find a way to make the most of every situation.      Exactly. I remember when I first started out, I was so nervous. I thought I had to be perfect, but now I know that it’s okay to make mistakes. You just learn from them.      That’s what I tell my students. They’re all so eager to learn, and it’s amazing to see how they grow. I think that’s what makes this job so rewarding—watching people develop.      And you’ve always been the one who could make even the most boring lesson feel exciting. I still remember the time you turned a grammar lesson into a game about Christmas traditions.      It was a disaster at first, but the kids loved it. And honestly, it’s the kind of thing I live for. I think that’s why I never get tired of doing what I do.

Hey Dad, it’s been two years since I saw you. I was just thinking about that trip to Tanzania we talked about. Remember how you said you wanted to go there with me?      Oh, I remember. That was the plan! But you know how things go—plans change, and now I’ve been stuck with this job at the call center. I’ve been thinking about it though. Maybe we can still make it happen this year.      That would be awesome. I’ve been meaning to look into flights and visas. But I’m also thinking about moving to Brighton. I’ve heard it’s a great place to live.      Brighton? My cousin lives there. She said it’s got a great vibe. But I’m not sure about the cost of living. I mean, I’m not rich, but I could do with a better place.      Yeah, I’ve been thinking about that too. Rent is expensive everywhere, but Brighton’s kind of affordable compared to London.      You should get a job there too. You’ve been teaching English, right? Maybe you could find something in Brighton.      I’m working on it. I got a few offers, but I’m not sure. I’m still figuring it out.      Speaking of work, how’s the customer service job going? You’ve been there for a while now.      It’s fine. I like the people, but it’s not what I imagined. I miss teaching. I miss the classroom.      I know what you mean. I used to be a teacher too. But I had to take this job after my wife passed away. It’s been tough, but I’ve made it work.      I’m sorry, Dad. That’s really heavy.      Thanks. It’s something I’ve had to deal with. But I’ve been trying to stay positive. Speaking of positivity, I’ve been doing a lot of board games lately. I think it helps.      That’s a good idea. I’ve been meaning to get back into that. I played a few games with my brother last week, and it was a lot of fun.      You should come over and bring some games. I’ve been looking for someone to play with.      Definitely. I’ll bring some from my collection. We can play a few games and catch up. I’ve been meaning to tell you about that trip to Tanzania.

So, I just got back from the supermarket, and I have to say, it was a bit of a disaster. I thought I’d be able to run in and grab a few essentials, but the queue was out the door, and I ended up getting stuck behind a woman with three kids who was trying to get a discount on everything.      Oh no, that sounds frustrating. I can imagine that. I went to the shops this morning and got stuck behind a guy who was clearly trying to buy a loaf of bread and was arguing with the cashier over the price. I thought he was trying to get a deal, but it just made everything slower for everyone.      Right? I mean, I know it’s part of the system, but it’s ridiculous. I had to wait over half an hour just for a couple of items. I even had to go to the bakery to get fresh bread, and that was just as bad.      Well, maybe it’s just the time of year. I was thinking the other day that we should start using some kind of loyalty cards or apps to make things faster. I read somewhere that a lot of stores are starting to use self-checkout machines, but I don’t know if they’re really making a difference.      Yeah, I’ve tried using the self-checkout before, but it always goes wrong. Either the scanner doesn’t work or the machine keeps rejecting the items. I’d rather just deal with someone at the counter. Although, maybe I should try a different store next time. I remember reading that some supermarkets have better systems than others.      I heard that Tesco and Sainsbury’s are doing better with their technology. I think the key is to have consistency. If you can trust the system, it might save you time in the long run. Maybe we should do a comparison of the stores and see which ones are actually more efficient.      That sounds like a great idea. I could do that over the weekend when I have time. I’ve been meaning to organize a little shopping review for the household. It might help us save money and time in the long run.      I like that. Let’s set up a little chart for each store and rate them based on speed, service, and prices. It might be fun.

So, I was just thinking about the bean bag I’m knitting. I was wondering if you'd like to try it out once it's done. I’m almost finished with the last few rows. It’s a bit of a challenge with the pattern, but I think it’s coming together nicely.      That sounds great, really. I’ve been wanting to get a new bean bag for the living room. The old one’s been falling apart since we moved in. But I’m not sure what color you’re going with. You mentioned something about the pattern earlier—was it the cable stitch?      Yes, it is. I thought the texture would add a nice touch to the room. I’ve also been thinking about the shower curtain. I saw this new design online with this watercolor sea theme. It’s really calming, and I think it would look amazing in the bathroom.      Oh, I like that idea. I’ve been wanting to update the bathroom décor too. The old shower curtain is so outdated, and the bathmat’s got holes in it. I was thinking of getting a new one, maybe something more modern. Do you think the sea theme would go with the rest of the bathroom?      It should. I think the blue and white would complement the tiles. Plus, it’s been a bit gloomy in there lately, and a bit of color might help. It’s not like we can just leave the bathroom looking like a spaceship anymore.      Haha, fair point. I’m glad you’re thinking about it. Speaking of which, are you planning to cook supper tonight? Or do you want me to take over?      I was just about to ask you that. I’ve got the sauce going, but I’m not sure about the rest of the meal. I was thinking of making a stir-fry with some chicken and vegetables. But I’m not sure if I’ve got all the ingredients.      That sounds good. I can help you with the veggies. I’ve got some fresh peas and carrots in the fridge. And if we need more protein, I can always add some tofu or a couple of eggs. Just let me know what you’d like.      Perfect. I’ll get the chicken out of the freezer and start heating up the wok. I’m also going to check if I’ve got any rice left.

Well, I've been meaning to ask you, old girl, about that new book club they started up in the village. I heard it’s got some decent reads, and with the weather being as bad as it is, it’d be nice to have something to do besides sit around the house all day.      Oh, I was just thinking about that too. I’ve been meaning to go along. A bit of reading would do me good, don’t you think? Though I must admit, I’m not sure how I’d manage the bus. Didn’t you say the meetings are at the community hall?      Well, I can offer to give you a lift. It’s not that far, and I’d be glad to help. I’ve got the car, and I’d rather not risk the bus with the roads being the way they are.      That’d be grand, mate. I’d be grateful for the company. I don’t know what I’d do without you two. Honestly, it’s been a long time since I’ve had anyone to talk to besides the cat.      Oh, don’t be so dramatic. We’re always here for you. Besides, it’s not just about the book. It’s the people, the conversations. You know, I’ve been thinking about getting back into some of the old hobbies. Maybe even start gardening again.      You should. I’ve got some old tools in the shed. If you’re interested, I could show you how to plant some vegetables. It’s a good way to get the blood flowing and be outside.      That sounds like a plan. I’ve always liked the idea of having a little patch of land to call my own. Maybe even grow some tomatoes. I used to have a bit of a garden when I was younger.      Good. I can help you with that too. I used to look after a few kids, so I’ve always had a knack for keeping things tidy. We could make it a bit of a joint effort.      I’ll throw in some seeds and tools. I’ve got a few things saved up from when I was running the shop. It’s a shame I had to close it down, but it gave me some time to think about what I really want to do now.      I can only imagine.

So, I was just telling my sister about the time I tried to cook a Christmas dinner and ended up setting the kitchen on fire. It was  absolutely  not a good look.      I bet you didn’t even burn the turkey, then. I mean, that’s the kind of thing that  always  happens when you try to do it for the first time. I still remember my first Christmas as a head of department; I tried to roast a goose and it ended up being more charred than cooked. Didn’t even get the kids to eat it.      I can’t even imagine that. I’m not even brave enough to cook turkey, let alone roast it. I left that to my mum. I’m more of a copywriter, not a chef. Exactly. I handle the logistics, you handle the healthcare, and I think we all have our roles. Though I must say, I do have a soft spot for baking. So, I've only been here a week, and already I’m trying to get my head around all the differences from England. Some people still feel uncomfortable talking about it. Others are more open. I’ve been here long enough to know which ones will talk and which ones won’t.      I guess it’s like anywhere. Some people like to share their stories, others don’t. I’m still figuring out what’s appropriate to ask and what’s not. I don’t want to be seen as intrusive.      You’re doing fine. It’s not easy. So, did you catch the latest lecture on climate policy? I was trying to get a few points across about the impact of pollution on urban areas, but the students were all too busy arguing about where to eat after class.      Yeah, I caught bits of it. I was actually writing up notes from my own lecture on the same topic. It’s amazing how the effects of pollution are so visible here in China compared to back home in England. I mean, I remember walking through Norwich as a kid, and the air was clean, even in the winter. Now, walking through the city near our apartment, it’s like breathing in a smog cloud.      It’s surreal, isn’t it? I still get that strange sense of being in a different country, even though I’ve been here for almost a year. I think the pollution is just one of those things that really emphasizes how different things are. I was telling my sister back home that I’d be lucky if the sky was clear for more than a day or two.      Exactly. It’s not just the air, though. I’ve noticed how the way people talk about pollution here is different. It’s more of a collective issue, something that affects everyone. Back in London, it was always more about individual choices—maybe driving less, recycling more. Here, it feels like the government is trying to tackle it on a larger scale, but the results are slower.      I guess that’s part of the challenge. It’s also funny because we’re both lecturers, and we’re always talking about how education can drive change. But I wonder if it’s enough. I mean, we can teach people the facts, but until there’s real policy support, it’s going to be hard to make a dent.      True. Still, I think it’s a good conversation to have. My students are really engaged with the topic, even if they’re not always sure what to do about it. It’s something we all need to be thinking about, even if we’re not doing much about it right now.      Yeah, and that’s why I’m glad we’re here together. Walking home from work, talking about these things—it’s a reminder that even in the middle of all this, there are still moments where you can have a real connection.

I’ve got the veg sorted, but I’m still not sure what I’m making for dinner. It’s been a long day at the hospital, and I just want something easy.      You’re not gonna make it on your own, are you? You said it was “a culinary masterpiece.”      That was a  special  occasion, and you know it. You were in the middle of a Zoom call with your agent.      You’re both too picky. If I wanted to make something complicated, I’d’ve asked for help. I just want a simple stir-fry.      Wait, are we going to take photos again? I swear, that’s the third time this week. You’re the one who wants to post it on social media like it’s a food blog.      Come on, it’s a good shot. I can do a caption: “When your day starts with a delicious stir-fry and ends with a  very  close call with the microwave.”      That’s not even close to a caption. How about “When life gives you lemons, make a stir-fry.”      You’re both impossible. But I’ll admit, I do need a hand. I’ve got the noodles, but I’m not sure about the spices.      Let me help. I’ve got a recipe I took from a food blog. It’s got garlic, ginger, soy sauce, and some gochujang for a bit of heat.      Sounds good. I’ll just heat up the oil and get the pan ready.      Alright, then. I think I’ll make myself a sandwich while we cook.      I’m not sure you’ve ever made a sandwich without burning the bread.      That’s the only reason I’m still here.      To dinner, and not burning it.      To photos, and not burning the camera.      And to us. The weird, wonderful, and slightly chaotic family.      That’s the spirit. Let’s get cooking.      And maybe a little bit of drama.      That’s our thing.      I think we’ve got our recipe for tonight.      I think I might just survive.      Let’s eat. I’m starving.

So, I heard there’s a new bus route coming in next week. You know, the one that’s supposed to connect the city center with the university more directly?      Yeah, I read about it in the local paper. They’re trying to ease the traffic around the campus, especially with all the students and staff commuting. But honestly, I’m not sure if it’ll make a big difference. I’ve been using the same route for years, and I don’t think it’s that bad.      Well, it’s always good to have more options. Especially if the new one goes through the bookshop near the Press building. I’ve been wanting to check out the Cambridge University Press bookshop for ages. They have some rare books and old editions that you can’t find anywhere else. But don’t expect anything too modern. It’s more of a traditional shop, like the old ones you’d see in Waterstones.      I guess that’s part of the charm. You know, I’ve been comparing my university with yours lately. I mean, we both have strong academic reputations, but I’ve heard your place is more of a traditional institution, and ours is more modern and experimental.      That’s true. I think it’s because of the way we were set up. We’ve been around longer, so there’s more tradition. But that doesn’t mean we don’t push boundaries. Some of the research is cutting-edge, and the students here are pretty forward-thinking.      I can see that. I mean, I’ve had a couple of lectures where the professor was using AI tools to analyze texts. It’s pretty cool. But I also have to admit, sometimes I miss the old-fashioned way of reading and discussing things face-to-face.      I get that. I think a lot of the protesters on campus are worried about how the university is changing. They’re not necessarily against progress, but they want to make sure that the core values of the institution aren’t lost in the rush to modernize.      Yeah, I’ve seen some of the protests. I think it’s a healthy debate. It shows that people are engaged and care about the direction the university is heading in.

So, I just got a call from Elise, and she wants to know if we can come over for dinner next Saturday. She’s bringing the kids, and I think she mentioned something about a boyfriends visit.      Oh, right! I remember. She told me about it during our lunch at the café last week. She’s really excited to have him over. But I should check with her again to make sure the timing works. I told her to not overdo it. You know, she’s always trying to impress people with her cooking. But I think she’s got it in her. She did win that contest at the local fair last year.      That’s right. She got second place. But she still thinks she could have won first. She’s quite competitive, that one.      I can see why she’s so excited about meeting the boyfriends. He’s from Cheshire, so he’s practically local. That’s a relief.      Exactly. Also, he’s a teacher. I think she’s been trying to make a connection ever since she found out about him.      I can imagine. You know how they are. But I think he’s a good guy. I met him once at a family gathering. He was very charming.      Yeah, he was. And he’s got a good sense of humor too. Well, I suppose we should go ahead and let her know we can come over. We could even bring some food to help out.      That’s a good idea. I’ll talk to her and make sure we’re all on the same page.      And maybe we could do something after dinner. Maybe watch a movie or something.

I can't believe we've walked all this way from Woolwich. I’m starting to think I’ve been walking in circles. I thought we were heading straight toward the O2 Arena, but now I’m not even sure where that is anymore. You’d think after living in Edinburgh for twenty years, I’d know my way around London. But the moment I step out of the tube, I’m lost. I’ve only ever been to the O2 once, and it was for a concert. I still don’t know if it’s a stadium or a building. It’s a building, of course. It’s one of those modern structures that looks like it was designed by a robot. You know, like that one in Dubai. I’ve never been to the O2, but I hear the views from the top are amazing. I’ve been thinking about going on holiday with the kids, maybe we could do something like that. That’s a good idea. Though I wonder, would the kids actually want to see the views from the top? They might just want to play on the swings or something. Speaking of which, we should really get a car. I’ve always been a fan of public transport, even if it’s a bit unreliable. Besides, with the way the roads are here, parking is a nightmare. I’d rather walk—though I’d rather have a car too. That’s the thing, though. It’s not just about convenience. It’s about freedom. I mean, what if we wanted to go somewhere spontaneous? Like, what if we suddenly wanted to go to the American Cup or something? You know, that thing where they race boats? The American Cup? That’s the one where the Americans always win. I think it’s held in Australia, though. You’d think they’d hold it somewhere closer. Exactly! What’s the point of a boat race if you have to fly halfway across the world for it? I mean, it’s not even a real race. It’s more like a show.

Can you believe it's raining again? I thought we’d finally get a break from this weather, but no—just when I’m about to go out, it starts drizzling.      I know, it's been like that all week. I tried to take the kids to the park today, but it just got too wet. I ended up staying home with a coffee and watching the rain. Such a shame, really.      Well, at least the rain gives us a chance to get the kids out of the house for a bit. My little one’s been so excited about the children’s sports day next weekend. She’s been asking about it nonstop.      Oh, I remember when my little brother was in his first sports day. He was so proud of himself, even though he tripped over his own feet and ended up in the puddle. It was a disaster, but he’s still the first to tell stories about it.      That sounds like typical sibling stuff. My niece, Zoe, is in the same boat. She’s obsessed with the idea of being a gymnast, but when I tried to take her to the local sports center, she was too scared of the slides.      I know, it’s all about trying new things. Speaking of which, have you seen the new phone app I got? It’s called 'Build a Bear'—you can design your own cuddly toy. My daughter loves it. She just started designing a unicorn.      Oh, I’ve heard of that. I used to buy one for my cousin when she was about five. She still has it, even though it’s got a few stains. It’s like a memory.      I remember when my sister was a kid—she had a ‘Build a Bear’ bear that she named after her favorite cartoon character. She used to take it everywhere.      I tried to build one for my daughter, but I think I messed up the ears. She didn’t mind, though. She just said it looked like a bear with extra eyebrows.      That’s the spirit. I think the kids are more about the experience than the end result. Speaking of, did you hear about the new ‘potty training’ app your daughter’s using? It’s supposed to make it easier.      No, I haven’t. But I’ve been meaning to look into something like that. I’m just so nervous about it.

So, I've been thinking a lot about what I want to do with my life over the next few years. You know, with the house-sitting here in Australia, it's like a fresh start. Maybe it's time I started setting some personal goals.      That’s a great idea. I’ve been meaning to do the same. I think it’s important to have some direction, especially after everything that’s happened with the school year and my family. But I’m not sure where to start.      I’ve been considering expanding my business. I’ve got some ideas for new projects, but I need to figure out how to fund them. I’d love to get some of my friends involved, you know, like those who are starting up their own ventures. We could collaborate or even start something together.      That sounds exciting. I’ve been thinking about taking on more responsibilities at work too. I’m actually looking into a professional development course for teachers. It’s not just about the salary, it’s about growing as a person and being more effective in the classroom.      That’s really admirable. I’ve always admired how you’re always trying to improve. I think it’s important to have that drive, especially when you’re in a profession that impacts so many lives.      Thanks, but I think it’s also about making sure I have a better work-life balance. I’m not sure I want to be at work all the time. Maybe I should consider moving to a different role or even doing something part-time.      I get that. I’ve been thinking about family planning too. We’ve been talking about having kids, but the timing just hasn’t felt right. I want to be in a stable place financially and emotionally before we make that big step.      That makes sense. I think it’s important to make sure we’re both on the same page. I would love to have kids, but I want to make sure I’m not sacrificing too much of my own life for them.      Exactly. We need to plan this carefully. Maybe we can set some goals for the next couple of years and check in on them regularly. It’s all about being proactive, you know?      Agreed. I think we could even create a sort of roadmap. Financial goals, personal development, and maybe even some travel plans.

So, I've been meaning to ask, what do you think about the new accent trends? I swear, every time I go out, it's like a dialect festival! You can tell where someone's from by their first word.      Aye, I know what you mean. I'm from Wigan, and even though I grew up here, sometimes I catch myself slipping into a more "posh" accent when I'm in a formal setting. It's weird, right? Like, you wanna sound smart, but you're also from the North.      That’s the struggle, isn’t it? I’m from Warrington too, and I can do both—drawl and posh. I’ve even used my left-hand man skills to switch accents on the spot. D’you know, I once did a little monologue at a pub quiz, and it was so convincing, people thought I was from London.      Wait, you’re from Leeds, right? How’d you get that down? I’ve tried, but I just sound like I’ve had a fight with a bagpipe. I thought it was just a regional thing, but now I’m not so sure about that.      You can’t blame them. I’ve been in Liverpool and even London, and I know how it feels. The accents up here are like a language in themselves. I once tried ordering a coffee in Liverpool and said, “Wha’ ye want?” and the barista just stared at me like I’d spoken in code.      And that’s what I love about it. It’s like a little bit of folklore in every word. Speaking of folklore—did you hear about that new Pokémon game? They’ve got golems with British accents now. It’s  weird  but catchy.      I tried it last night. I’ve never been a big fan of Pokémon, but the new characters are so expressive. I think they even made a team of regional accents to represent the different regions. It’s like walking into a pub and meeting all your friends.

Well, I’ve been thinking about that garden party we had last summer. You remember when we tried to serve homemade lemonade and it turned out like it had been left in the sun for a week?      Oh, yes! And then you tried to pass it off as  sparkling  lemonade, thinking it was some sort of sophisticated drink. I nearly choked on my salad.      I think you were just trying to impress the neighbors. Remember when you said the lemonade was “a twist on the traditional”?      I think you were trying to outdo the neighbor’s gin and tonic. My uncle still talks about that party. He said it was the most dramatic lemonade he’d ever seen.      Blimey, I’ve learned my lesson. I’m not even going to attempt a drink again this summer. Though I do miss the days when we used to have proper parties. Back when I still had a job and money to burn.      I know, old chap. It’s sad, really. We used to have these big gatherings at the house, with proper food and games. Now we’re all just – what’s the word? –  sitting around  having dinner and talking about politics.      I think it’s the age. I mean, even the politicians are starting to look like they’re in a sitcom. I tried watching the news last night, and it was like a soap opera. So much drama and no real substance.      I couldn’t agree more. I used to love talking politics when I was in college. But now, I just want to talk about football and food. Though, honestly, I still don’t know how you can be a proper football fan without understanding the rules.      You think you know the rules? I’ve seen you miss the most basic passes in the Premier League. You’re just as bad as me.      I do love football, though. Last season, I followed the local team, Norwich City. I even joined their fan club. It’s not about winning; it’s about the community, the passion.      That’s nice. I think I’d like to get into that. Although, I’d probably start with the Premier League because, well, I can’t say I’ve ever watched a local match.      I think that’s the key. It’s not about the game, it’s about the fan culture. And the food, of course.

So, I was just thinking, do you ever miss those days when we used to stay up all night with our mates, just talking about everything? You mean the nights when you got   so   drunk that you actually   tripped over your own feet   when you got home?      Oh, come on, you were there! You were the one who tried to sing "Bohemian Rhapsody" like it was a karaoke song. I still remember you falling flat on your face in the hallway and everyone laughing. I know, but I’m just so burned out. I mean, I still remember when I first came to university, and I was so excited to be here. But now? It feels like I’m just going through the motions. Have you ever thought about where you grew up? Like, what was it like in Falmouth?      Oh, it was so different from here. Everything was just… laid back. That’s classic. You always had that wild streak.      And you, you were always the one trying to be the “big shot” in our street.      Well, I had to be. The chaos, the freedom, the dirt on my shoes and the sense that anything was possible.      Yeah… I think we all miss that. But maybe that’s what makes us who we are.      Yeah. Even if we are still here, and still messing things up.

So, it's been ages, isn't it? I was just thinking about how we haven't caught up properly since the summer. You're looking well, by the way.      Same here! I feel like we've been busy as ever. Now you're running the show?      Ha! I still ask for advice, though. I think I’ve just gotten better at asking the right people. It’s funny how things change.      Totally. I’ve been thinking about my own future lately. I’m trying to figure out what I want to do next. I’ve been considering moving to another city for a new project, but I’m not sure yet.      That sounds like a big decision. Have you thought about where you want to go?      I’ve been looking at London and maybe even Edinburgh. I’ve heard good things about Edinburgh, and I’m finally ready for a change.      Edinburgh is a great choice. I’ve been there a few times, and the vibe is amazing. If you go, let me know—I’d love to visit you.      I would love that. I think I’ll reach out to you once I make a decision. We should really plan a proper catch-up soon.      Absolutely. Let’s grab dinner again, maybe next week? I’m in the mood for something new.      Sounds perfect. I’ll check my schedule and get back to you.      Great. I can’t wait to hear what you decide. And don’t forget, whatever you choose, I’m here for you.      Thanks, I know. It’s good to catch up, and I’m glad we’re finally back on track.      Me too. Let’s make sure we don’t let so much time pass again.

So, I've been thinking about getting a few things online. I was just looking at Amazon and eBay... but honestly, I'm not sure which one is better. I’ve had some bad experiences with people not sending items or sending the wrong ones.      I know what you mean.
