Depends on the seller, but most things arrive within a few days. And if you order on eBay from the UK, you can usually get free delivery. I’ve had some items arrive in two days.      Well, I guess I should give it a try. I’ll start with something small—maybe a book or something like that. It’s better than just buying things I don’t really need.      That’s the way to go.

So, I was just thinking, do you ever remember that time we tried to fix the old fridge? I mean, I thought I was being helpful, but it ended up making more noise than before.      Oh, you mean the one you tried to open with a hammer? I still can’t believe you didn’t notice the door was stuck. You were so determined to prove you could fix things.      Well, I thought I was being practical. It wasn’t like it was a fancy appliance. I mean, what’s the point of having a fridge if you can’t even open it?      I know, I know. You had this whole theory that the problem was the hinges, not the door. I tried to tell you, but you were too busy explaining it to the cat.      Ah, yes, the cat. I still think that was the cleverest thing I did that day. It was looking at me like I was the one who had done the damage.      You were so proud of yourself. You even told the neighbors about it. Remember how they all laughed?      It’s not like I didn’t have a reason. I was just trying to be useful. You know, with all the time I’ve been out of work, I thought maybe I could start learning new things.      I know, and I’m proud of you for trying. It’s not easy being retired and not having a job, is it? I mean, you’ve got this whole life, and you’re still trying to find your place.      Well, I’m not sure where I’m going, but I don’t want to be a burden. I’ve been thinking about maybe doing some gardening. You know, the one in the back. It’s been neglected for years.      That’s a great idea. I’d love to help you with that. You could grow some vegetables, and I could bring the kids over for lunch. It would be a nice way to spend time together.      You’re a good friend, you know that? I don’t know what I’d do without you.      And I wouldn’t want to be without you either. We’ve been through a lot together, and I think we’ll be around for a long time.      Yeah, I think you’re right. I’ve had my ups and downs, but I’m not giving up.

So, what are we doing for Christmas? I’ve been thinking about flying on Christmas Day. The flights are usually cheaper then, and I’ve got a friend who said they got a great deal last year.      I hear you. I’ve been thinking about that too. I’ve got a ticket booked for the 25th, but I’m still figuring out where to go. Maybe I’ll just stay in London. I’ve got a few family members here, and I’m not sure if I want to fly all the way to the countryside. Plus, the airport’s always a zoo on Christmas Day.      Oh, I know, I’ve been there. But maybe they’re just adapting to the urban environment. I remember reading something about how animals are getting more comfortable around people.      I guess that’s the cost of living in cities. But I also think it’s weird to see wildlife so close to home. I mean, I’d be terrified if a deer ran into my car on the way to the airport.      That’s the thing, though. It’s almost like the wildlife is becoming part of our daily lives now. I think we need to be more aware, especially when we’re driving.

So, I've been thinking—do you ever notice how people's accents can tell you so much about where they're from? Oh yeah, that’s always been a thing with me too. I mean, I grew up in a small town in the south, so I was always the one who had to adjust my accent when I went up north for uni. It’s funny how people judge you based on how you sound, even if you’ve been in the same country your whole life.      I think it’s more about the way people use their voices and the cadence. Like, even if someone’s from the same part of England, if they grew up in a different environment, their accent changes. I mean, I work in games, so I’ve heard all sorts of accents from people who’ve lived in different parts of the country, and it’s wild how they all sound so different.      Exactly! Now I sound more like a Londoner, even though I still say “chips” instead of “crisps.”      Oh man, I’ve been trying to do that too. I’d love to be able to say “chips” without sounding like I’m from a different planet. But I still fall back on “crisps” when I’m nervous. It’s like a habit.      I think the key is practice. Maybe we should do a little accent workshop. I’ve got a friend who’s into all that language stuff—he could help. Plus, it’d be fun to see how we sound when we try to mimic each other’s accents.      That’d be hilarious. I could try to sound like you, Speaker_2. I’d be like,  “I’m from the south, so I go to the cinema for a film and I’m always late.”  You’d just laugh, but I’d be serious.      I’d be the first to laugh, seriously. But I’d also be impressed that you could pull off an accent that well.

Hey guys, did you hear about the new album from that indie band we love? They dropped it last week, and it’s absolutely wild.      Oh man, I heard! Okay, so I was talking to the kids about balanceability the other day. You know, when they're trying to do those balance beam exercises at school. Speaking of practice, I heard from one of my classmates that their friend is moving to a new house, and they’re renovating it. They even have a swimming pool now!      Wow, a swimming pool? I wonder if they’re still doing that.      Yes, they are. I heard from a parent that it’s about balancing the water flow to make it look like a real waterfall. It’s part of a new project they’re doing at the school.      That’s cool! I bet it’s really beautiful. I wish we had something like that at home.      You know, I think it’s about balancing things in life too. Like, when you’re trying to succeed at something, you’ve got to keep trying and not give up.      I like that. So, if I try harder, I can do better at school?      Exactly. And don’t forget, we’re all in this together. You don’t have to do it alone.      I have a cat named Whiskers. He’s really good at balancing on the windowsill. I think he’s the best at it!      That’s adorable. You know, National Cat Day in Japan is coming up.

So, I was just telling my cousin about the gym again—the one in Doncaster. So, what do you think of that pizza we had after the Domino Drive? It was proper good, wasn’t it?      Yeah, it was alright, I guess. I’ve been meaning to get a proper cut. I’ve been letting it grow since the last time I went to the hairdresser. It’s started to look a bit like a wild man.      You’re not the only one. Yeah, I’ve seen your hair. It looks like a brush full of hay.

I just made a new batch of tea. You want a cup? It’s just as strong as usual, though I might have added a little more milk this time. Oh, that sounds perfect. Some have great food, others just have great atmosphere. Definitely. I remember when we first moved here, we used to go to that little place on the corner, right? The one with the veggie menu. I think it was the first time I ever ordered a salad instead of a burger. Oh, yes! I remember that. You were so nervous about it, but it was actually really good. And the owner, he’s a bit of a character. Always has some interesting stories about the neighborhood. He definitely does. I still hear him talking about the old days when he first opened the place. I bet he’s been there for over twenty years. Anyway, I think I’m going to order a green salad for lunch today. I’ve been trying to eat more vegetables. That’s great. I’ve been trying to do the same. I’ve even started growing some herbs in my kitchen. It’s a bit of a mess, but it’s fun. I think I’ll try adding some more greens to my meals this week. That’s a good move. I’ve heard that eating more vegetables can do wonders for your health. Plus, it’s better for the environment, right? Less meat, more veg. Absolutely. And I think it’s just about making small changes.

So, I've got a word game trick up my sleeve. If you think of a word that has three syllables and ends with 'tion', I'll tell you a joke about it. Ready?      I’m ready! What’s the word?       Education.  Alright, here’s the joke: Why did the teacher get kicked out of the classroom? Because she kept  educating  the students  in  the  tion  of the wrong path!      Oh, that’s a good one! But hold on,  education  isn’t exactly three syllables. It’s  ed-u-ca-tion —that’s five syllables.      Oh, you’re right! I’m getting confused. Maybe I should stick to  information ? Let me think of another one.      You’re overcomplicating it. Just say “the word’s not there.” That’s a classic. And it’s only one syllable.      Wait, that’s not a word game. That’s a joke. Let’s try the rules again. The game is Articulate, right? So, the object is to describe a word without using it. We’re all pretty good at that. But some words are harder than others.      Yeah, like  carnival . I did “a big party with fireworks and games.” No one knew what I was talking about for five minutes.      I once tried to describe  bureaucracy  as “the system where nobody knows what they’re doing, but everyone has a form.” My cousin laughed so hard she cried.      That’s the spirit! We’re all trying to outdo each other. I think I’m going to go for  celebrity  next. Let me think… “A famous person who always gets the spotlight.”      That’s it! You just got  celebrity  without using the word. You’re getting better at this!      I’m learning! I’ve been teaching and writing, so I’m used to explaining things. Still, I think I need to play more. Maybe I can go back to my hometown and teach a game night.      That’s a great idea. We could all come over. I’ve got some old board games I’ve never used.      And I can bring some snacks. You know, to fuel the games and the jokes.      And I can tell some more stories. I’ve got a whole list. My childhood was full of wild stories.      That sounds like the perfect plan. Let’s set up the games and see who wins. I’ve got a feeling I’ll be the last one standing.

So, I think I’ve just won. I had the queen of spades and... oh, wait, did I say that out loud?      You did. And you also just said the queen of spades. That’s the third time this game. You’re really  not  subtle today.      Maybe it’s because we all know you’re the best at this game, so you don’t even need to pretend you’re trying. You just go for it.      Oh, please. I’ve seen you  win  this game with a hand that’s only got a two and a three. You just keep changing the rules mid-game.      Okay, fine, I might have a bit of an advantage. But I was about to say something about the breakfast, wasn’t I? I mean, we’ve been in this cottage for three days and not once have we actually cooked anything besides cereal.      I know, I know. But it’s not like we have a fridge full of food to work with. And honestly, who has time to cook when we’re playing cards and arguing about the rules?      I think I’ve seen you  argue  about the rules more than I’ve seen you play the game. You’re more interested in the  rules  than the  game , aren’t you?      That’s because the rules are the fun part. The game itself is just a vehicle for us to socialize. Look, I’ve never actually played a game that lasted longer than an hour. But this one’s been going for days. I think we’re all just waiting for someone to give up.      You’re not the only one. I think I might actually be starting to enjoy the  arguments  more than the game itself. It’s like a mini-drama every time someone suggests a rule change.      Oh, I see. So you’re saying the game is  actually  the drama, and the rules are just the setup?      Wait, that’s a good one! You know, I think I’m going to use that as a joke at the next family gathering. It’s like  The Office —only with more cards and less coffee.      Oh, you’re so dramatic. But I’ll admit, I  do  miss the coffee. I think we’re all kind of in denial about the fact that we’ve been here for three days and still haven’t planned a proper meal.

Hey, did you see the latest episode of  Stranger Things ? It was so intense! I couldn’t stop watching it all night.      Oh, I saw it! It was wild. I honestly couldn’t believe how they handled the time travel. But honestly, I’m just glad it’s over. I’m tired of all the suspense.      I didn’t get to watch it yet, but from what I’ve heard, it’s been a huge deal. I’ve been so busy with my apprenticeship stuff. Do you think I should even bother watching it?      Mate, if you don’t watch it, you’re missing out. It’s one of the best shows out there. Plus, it’s got that nostalgic 80s vibe, which is a big hit in our group.      Yeah, it’s a classic. I actually started watching it last month after my friend recommended it. It’s the kind of show that you can’t stop once you start.      Definitely. It’s funny—everyone’s got their own Christmas plans. I’m still trying to figure out where I’m going. My employer said I could take some time off for the holidays, but I still haven’t decided where to go.      That’s so cool. I’m going back home to my parents. It’s always the same old stuff, but I love it. Parents always make sure you have the best Christmas.      Yeah, I’m going to my mum’s too. She’s been shopping for presents all month. I swear, she’s been more excited about Christmas than I’ve ever seen her.      That’s the spirit. I go back to my parents every year. It’s always so festive, even though I’m in a higher professional job. You know, working on navel combat systems and all. It’s weird, but I love the traditions.      I’m not sure I’ve got the same kind of traditions. I’m working at a care home during Christmas.

So, I was walking down the High Street the other day, and I saw this group of cyclists zooming by like they were in a race. I thought, “Oh, what a bunch of madmen!”      I can imagine. I tried cycling to work once, but it felt like I was racing against time. My boss wanted me there by 9 a.m., and I got there at 9:03.      That’s nothing. I once rode my bike to the shops and got stuck in a queue of cars trying to get through a red light. I had to sprint across the road to get the last loaf of bread.      I’ve always preferred driving. You can control the pace and the route. I don’t like the unpredictability of cyclists and pedestrians. You never know when someone’s going to dart out.      I hear you, but I think cycling is better for the environment and for fitness. Plus, it’s cheaper than buying a car and paying for insurance.      I tried to get a car once, but I couldn’t afford it. My dad said, “If you want a car, you’ll have to work for it.” And I just didn’t have the energy.      I know what you mean. I’ve been around the block a few times. When I was younger, I used to ride a bike to work, but then I got a car and never looked back. It’s just easier, you know?      I think I’ll stick with walking most of the time. It’s the healthiest option. I’ve been doing it more lately anyway. I’m trying to get back into shape after university.      That’s smart. I used to walk all the time, but now I just sit on the sofa all day. I’ve got too much to do, honestly.      I suppose we all have our ways. I think walking is the best, but I’d never say no to a nice drive. Especially on a sunny day.      Maybe I should try renting a car for a weekend. It’d be good to get out of the house and see some places.      That sounds like a plan. Just don’t forget to pay the petrol bill, or you’ll be stuck again.      Oh, I wouldn’t dream of it. I’ve got my savings tucked away for that very purpose.      To walking, cycling, and driving – and to not getting stuck in traffic!

So, I've been meaning to ask—what made you both end up in Cambridge for Alumni Day? I mean, I know it's a big place, but I can't imagine someone from Lincoln or Aylesbury just… appearing here out of the blue.      Oh, it's all part of the alumni event. They’ve got these little workshops and panels where people can reconnect with the university. I actually found it really interesting—especially the language panel. It was about how regional dialects in England have evolved over time.      Ah, the dialects—those are fascinating. I’ve spent years studying them. I remember when I was a student, I used to travel across the country and listen to how people spoke. It’s amazing how much variation there is, even within the same country.      You’re a lecturer, aren’t you? I remember seeing your name in the programme. That’s impressive. I’m just a language research co-ordinator, but I’m still pretty passionate about the nuances of speech. Speaking of which—did you know that the way people speak in Wales is completely different from the rest of England?      Yeah, I’ve read a bit about that. But it’s not just Wales. Even within England, there are huge differences. I mean, I grew up in Lincoln, and the way people speak there is so different from someone from Aylesbury. It’s like a mini dialect map in itself.      Exactly. That’s why I love teaching. You can’t just study a language in a textbook—you have to understand the people who speak it. I remember one time, I was in Basque Country, and even though the language there is completely different from Spanish, the people were so warm and welcoming. It was like a different culture, but it felt connected somehow.      That’s interesting. I’ve been to Spain a few times and have always been fascinated by the way people use language there. It’s so expressive. I remember once I was in Barcelona, and someone was talking so fast, I couldn’t understand a word. I thought maybe I was just being too slow, but it turns out, it was just the way they spoke—rapid and melodic.      I think that’s part of the language’s beauty, isn’t it? That connection between language and culture. It’s like when I was visiting Wales, I noticed how the Welsh language is still taught in schools, even though it’s not as widely spoken as English.

So, I've been meaning to ask you, have you seen the latest Facebook post from the cousin who moved to New York? He was always the one with the adventurous spirit. Remember when we were kids and he tried to climb that tree at the back of the farm? He ended up falling and broke his arm. Still, he got through it.      Exactly! He's always been the kind of person who takes risks. Though, I can't help but wonder if he's actually settled in New York. He’s been into a lot of health stuff lately, like yoga and running. I think he’s trying to get back into shape. But honestly, I miss his old self. He used to be the one dragging us out to the countryside for weekend camping trips.      That’s true. I remember one time when we all got lost on the way back from a hike. We ended up sleeping in a field for two nights. But it was the best kind of chaos.      And we still have those ridiculous photos from that trip. My sister even framed one of them. It’s a family treasure.      I’ve been thinking about how quickly things change. My brother just proposed to his girlfriend last week. It’s so exciting, but also kind of overwhelming. I mean, I’m thrilled for them, but I still can't wrap my head around the idea of someone else's life being so different from mine.      That’s the thing, isn’t it? Life moves so fast. I can’t believe you and I have been through so much together, and yet we're still here, talking about old memories.

You know, I’ve been thinking about that coffee machine we bought last year. It’s been giving us more trouble than it’s worth. Every time someone tries to use it, it either doesn’t heat up or the beans just pour out like sand.      I remember the day we first tried it. You were all excited, thinking it would be the best thing since sliced bread. Now I’m not so sure. I’ve had to dump more coffee than I’ve ever drunk.      Yeah, I can’t even remember the last time it made a decent cup. I think we’re just wasting money on it now. My cousin in Manchester said they’re selling their machine for a third of what we paid.      I know. It’s just that we wanted something better for breakfast, you know? But I’m starting to think maybe we should just go back to the old drip method.      Or maybe we could just buy a keurig or something. I’ve seen those in the shops. They’re like, $20, and they make a decent cup.      Or we could just invest in a new machine. But I think that would cost more than we’ve already spent on this one.      Speaking of costs, have you seen what the removal and storage fees are these days? I was looking at the quote the other day, and it’s like a tax on life. I thought being retired would mean I wouldn’t have to deal with stuff like that, but no.      I know. I had to move my stuff from my old place to my new one, and the cost was insane. I just found out that the storage fee for a couple of boxes is more than what I paid for my apartment.      I tried to get a quote for storage too, and it was just a joke. I ended up keeping everything in my shed. At least I’ve got space there.      Politics is even worse. I can’t believe Labour is trying to push for more taxes and regulations. I just want a government that listens to the people, not the lobbyists.      Yeah, it’s frustrating. I think the Labour leadership is losing sight of what they promised. They were supposed to be idealists, not just another party playing politics.      I agree. Idealism is what got us here, but now it’s just a fancy word used to justify more control.

That would be great! I can’t wait to hear about what you’ve been up to. And maybe we can start planning our little trip.      I’d love that.
