Oh, you mean the “Every Good Boy Does Fine” thing?

So, I've been meaning to ask you, have you noticed the Jehovah's Witnesses coming through the village more often lately? I saw them at the corner shop this morning, and I've been curious about their views on things like voting and taxes. I mean, what do they think about the government?      Ah, yes, they've been around quite a bit. I've heard they're pretty strict about certain things, like not eating meat on certain days, and they're very into their own meetings. As for voting and taxes, I think they're pretty much against the government, or at least they don’t partake in political activities. They focus more on community and the things they believe in.      That's interesting. I’ve always found their meetings to be quite welcoming, especially for the older folks in the village. But I agree, they don’t really engage with the political side. I mean, I remember when I was a childminder, I used to take the kids to their meetings once in a while. It was always a quiet, peaceful place.      I remember reading something about them not believing in the state or anything like that. But then again, I’m not exactly sure what their stance is on things like parking at the coast. I mean, I’ve heard tales about the new development near the beach, and the way the parking is set up—some say it's unfair.      I heard the same. And the dentists in the village have been complaining about the amount of people coming in with chipped teeth from the new patio areas. They're not exactly a fan of the new development, I think.      That’s a shame. I always thought the coast was such a beautiful place. We used to go out there on Sundays and have a picnic. I still remember the taste of the fish and chips from that little café on the way. It’s always been a bit of a tradition for us.      Tell me about the village characters, though. I feel like we’ve got some real personalities down here. There's Mrs. Hart, who always knows the gossip, and the old man who keeps chickens in the backyard. Even the birds have a personality.      Oh, you wouldn’t believe the stories that come out of this village! I once heard that the birds are actually named.

So, I've been thinking about the log burner again. I need to get some more logs in before it gets too cold. Maybe I should check out that antique shop they mentioned on the way back from Tokyo? I heard they have some really good firewood there.      I think they do, but I'm not sure if it's the best place to get wood. You might want to go to that new restaurant by the park instead. The owner said they have a great variety of logs, and it’s a nice place to meet up. Plus, the fudge they serve is amazing. You'd probably like it.      Oh, the fudge? I still remember the ones from my childhood. They used to make them in the village store. It’s a shame they didn’t keep the tradition. But I suppose things change. I heard about the new restaurant too — it’s part of a chain, isn’t it? I worry about places like that taking over local spots, especially with outsourcing to India.      I know, it’s all part of the modern age, but it’s hard not to miss the charm of local businesses. Speaking of local, did you hear about the school academies? My neighbor’s daughter is getting ready to start, and she’s really excited. It’s a shame they’re changing the school system so much. I used to teach, and I don’t think it’s the same anymore.      I can only imagine. Our kids are at a primary school here, and the way they’re pushing for more private tutoring is worrying. I mean, what about the budget? If the government is cutting funding, where does that leave the schools? I think about how I used to teach — it was a different time.      Exactly. I’ve been working in administration for years, and it’s crazy how much things have changed. I’ve even seen some projects outsourced to India. I can’t believe they trust them with the data. I was just saying to my wife, we need to be careful with how we handle sensitive information now.      It’s all about efficiency, I suppose. But sometimes, I think efficiency comes at the cost of personal connection. You know, like the old days when we used to have time to chat with our neighbors. These days, people are always in a rush, even when they’re just visiting.

Well, I've been thinking about buying a house again. I mean, it's not like I've got much else to do these days. I’m just not sure if it's worth the bother with the taxes and everything. Do you think it's even worth it at our age?      Honestly, I don't think it is. I mean, if you're not working, you don’t need that extra burden. I just got my pension and I’m barely keeping my head above water. I think it’s better to rent and save the money. Didn’t you hear about the new council tax? It’s gone up again. I’m still paying for a house I haven’t lived in for years.      Oh, I know. I got a letter this morning about the new tax on second homes. It's so unfair. I mean, I had a little place in the Lake District, but I sold it because of the costs. I still feel guilty about it, though. It was my escape from the city. Still, the money was needed for the kids.      I get that, but listen, I’ve been talking to a mate who’s still working and he says the market is better now. Maybe it's time to look again. I've got a relative who's a property developer, and he said there’s some cheap land in the countryside. Maybe I can pick up a place and start something.      You know, I’d say go for it. But don’t get too carried away. You’ve got to be careful with money. I tried that once—got a mortgage, and then the pension got cut because of the financial crisis. Lost everything. Not a good move.      I hear you. But I think part of it is the politics. The government keeps changing the rules, and it's all so confusing. I don’t even know where to start. I mean, do you even know how to apply for a mortgage these days? I was told to use a Sat Nav for the whole process.      You’re not wrong. I’ve seen people use their phones to find a mortgage broker. It’s like everything's going digital. Still, I think it’s best to go slow. I’ve been watching a few programmes on TV about retirement homes. Maybe that’s the answer?

Well, I think the laptop is still under warranty. Let me check the serial number again. I don’t wanna have to pay for this.      Is it the one from work? I remember you said it was a bit slow last week. Maybe we should just try to fix it before we throw it out.      Oh, here’s some leftover sauce. You can use it for the tacos later. Didn’t want it to go to waste.      Thanks, love. That’ll make dinner easier.      OOOOHHHH!      What’s up, little man? You like the laptop?      Yeah!      Oh, I see. You’re trying to fix it by yourself.      He’s watching us like it’s a race. Maybe we should let him try – just don’t let him touch the keyboard.      He’s already done that. You know what happened last time? We had to reformat the whole thing.      Yeah, and we had a  very  sticky out ears incident.      That’s true. He got so excited, he just stood there with his ears sticking out the sides of his head. It was ridiculous.      I remember. You were trying to explain to the neighbor that it wasn’t a new hairstyle.      You were  so  embarrassed.      Yeah, and we had to explain to the kids at the park that it was just a new phase.      I think he’s growing out of the sticky out ears phase. But I still see it sometimes.      Moooon!      Maybe we should just let him have a turn. Just don’t let him overheat it.      I think that’s the plan. We’ll let him try, but only under supervision.      And maybe we can arrange a little rugby session with the neighbors after dinner. You know, to get the kid moving.      That sounds good. I think he’s been cooped up all day.      Speaking of, should we start the dinner? The fajita sauce is ready, and I think the chicken is done.      Yeah, let’s get this meal on the table. And maybe we can let the little one try to fix the laptop with us – just in a safe way.      Deal. But no sticky out ears this time.      I’ll be good!      Alright, let’s get to work. You’re on the team, little man.      Yeah, and if you break anything, we’ll just order a new one.      That’s the plan. Let’s go. Dinner is waiting!      Moooon!

So, I was telling the kids earlier that I think the Loch Ness monster is just a big, fluffy dog that lives in the loch. I mean, it’s got to be something like that, right? No one’s seen it, so it must be hiding.      I don’t think it’s a dog, Mom. I think it’s a giant snake that only comes out at night. Or maybe a dragon?      Yeah, and it eats all the fish and then just floats around, staring at the boats.      Sounds like a real menace. I mean, I’d rather have a dog. At least you can train a dog.      Wait, but I read somewhere that the Loch Ness monster is actually the same as the one in the Lake District. They’re like twins, but separated by a long time and a lot of water.      Twins? How can they be twins if they’re in different lakes?      Oh, I think it’s a myth. But it’s fun to think about, isn’t it? It’s better than just sitting around talking about pizza all the time.      Yeah, I mean, pizza is great, but I’d rather talk about the Loch Ness monster. It’s more exciting.      Wait, Mom, what’s a handstand again? I tried it once and I fell over.      Oh, a handstand is when you stand on your hands, right? Like balancing on your palms and toes. It’s kind of like a yoga pose.      Can I try it? I think I can do it if I practice.      Sure, why not? But be careful. You might fall. If you do, just get someone to catch you.      I’ll fall and you’ll have to catch me, Mom. I’m not that strong.      That’s the spirit. Now, go on, give it a try. And if you don’t like it, we can always talk about fairy gardens instead.      What’s a fairy garden?      It’s a small garden with tiny flowers, little stone paths, and maybe even some tiny lights. It’s like a magic forest in your backyard.      I want one! And I want to put a tiny Loch Ness monster in it too.      That’s the spirit. Now go on, before I change my mind and say we should just order pizza and call it a day.      Okay, but only if we make a fairy garden too.

So, I tried to order a  pomfrit  here, but the waiter said it's not on the menu. I thought it was a local specialty or something.      Oh, it’s a bit of a local thing, but not everyone here knows what it is. It’s like a thick pancake, basically. You have to ask a local to get it right.      Wait, what is a  pomfrit  again? I’ve heard the word before, but I never really got what it was.      It's a traditional dish, actually. From the north of England, I think. Like a thick, fried pancake, sometimes with eggs or cheese inside. It’s a bit of a comfort food for some people.      Comfort food? I mean, it’s definitely not something I would cook at home, but I can see how it’s comforting.      Yeah, it’s one of those things that reminds you of home. Especially in places like Bolton, where it's common.      So, are we going to try it? I mean, if it's not on the menu, maybe we should ask the waiter to prepare it for us?      I’d be nervous about that. You never know what they might do. But if you’re a local, you can always ask. Some places here are more open than others.      Oh, by the way, did you see the weather forecast? It's supposed to be sunny all week. I was hoping for some good swimming weather.      Yeah, the pool here is amazing. I’ve been meaning to take the kids for a dip. They’ve been cooped up in the hotel all day.      We could go tomorrow, right? I’ve been dying to get in the water. I think it’s been the highlight of the trip so far.      Yeah, go for it. But be careful—this place has some of the best beaches in the region. Just don’t get too sunburned.      I’ve been using SPF 50 every day. I’m basically a sunbather now.      You’re 19, so I guess that makes sense. My son used to do the same thing. He was always trying to tan like a lifeguard.      Yeah, I’m like that. I’ve got a tan, but I’m still pale. I think I need to get a tanning bed or something.      You’re already getting the tan you want. Just not the right kind.      Anyway, I’m just saying—I think this place is perfect.

So, I was just telling my wife about the letter I got from that debt-collecting company. I thought it was a scam at first, but it turned out to be real! Got me all confused for a bit.      I’ve had a few of those, too. It’s one of those things that really gets on your nerves. Though I’ve been lucky enough to avoid serious trouble so far.      Oh, I’ve had to deal with that stuff for years. It’s the worst. You think you’re getting a call from your bank, and then you realize it’s just some debt collector trying to push you into paying something you never agreed to.      I had to deal with that for a while. They kept calling me at odd hours, threatening to take me to court, and all that. It was very stressful.      And the worst part is, you don’t even know where the debt came from. One minute you’re just getting your mail, and the next, you’re sitting there with a landline in your hand trying to tell them, “No, sir, I didn’t sign that!”      I remember one time I got a letter saying I owed money to some “PPI” scheme. I thought, “What’s PPI?” And then I realized it was something to do with insurance. Who even knows what that means anymore?      That’s a classic one. PPI was a nightmare. So many people got caught up in it, and then it took years to sort out. I still remember seeing news stories about people standing on the street with cups of coffee trying to get their money back.      I remember reading an article in the local magazine about that. It said something about how people were still trying to claim their money. I thought, “I would have given it up ages ago!”      You know, I still get my mail every week. Some of it’s just old bills with stamps on them. It’s funny how things keep coming.      I’ve actually been thinking about getting a new computer. The one I’ve had is starting to get a bit slow, and I need to do some research for my job.      Yeah, you should. I’ve got a new one, and it’s been a lifesaver. I even use it to stream some of the BBC stuff. Though I still prefer the old TV.

So, I heard you’ve been working at the court for a few years now, Anne. How’s it going? I mean, I’ve been teaching English part-time, but I’ve never been inside a court before. Curious to know what it’s like.      Oh, it’s been a while, but I still enjoy it. It’s not as dramatic as you might think, but you’ve got to be on your toes. I’ve got to be there every day, helping with the flow of the court. It’s mostly routine, but you never know what might come up. You know, like someone showing up late or a witness not cooperating.      That sounds stressful. I mean, I deal with people all the time, but it’s not like I’m in the middle of a legal battle. I’ve been thinking a lot about the justice system lately, especially with all the news about reform. Do you think it’s getting better or worse?      Honestly, I think it’s mixed. There are a lot of good people working hard to make things fairer, but the system is still so inefficient. I remember when I was in school, we had a real debate about the justice system. It’s always been a point of discussion, especially in places like Scotland and England. I think people are starting to realize that it needs more support, more funding, and better resources.      That makes sense. I’ve also been thinking about climate change lately. It’s such an important issue. I mean, I’m not sure how we’re going to fix it without affecting the economy. It’s a tough balance, isn’t it?      Absolutely. I’ve seen how the local council has been trying to cut down on waste and promote recycling. But you know, it’s not just about the government. People need to take responsibility too. I’ve been trying to do my part by using public transport more often. It’s better for the environment and it saves money in the long run.      That’s a good point. I’ve been planning a trip to the south of England this summer. I’ve always wanted to visit the countryside, but with the cost of living, it’s hard to justify the expense. I guess I’ll have to save up a bit more.      You should go. It’s worth it.

So, what do you think makes people really happy? I mean, it's not just about having a lot of money, is it?      I think it's about being with the people you love. My brother and I are always laughing, and we play with the dog. I think that's what makes me happy.      Yeah, but if you had a lot of money, wouldn’t that make you even happier? I heard once that money can buy happiness.      I've heard that too. But I think it's more complicated than that. You can have money, but if you don't have people around you, you might still feel lonely.      Yeah, I guess so. I mean, I would rather have a nice day with my brother than a million pounds.      Wait, but what if you had a million pounds? Then you could buy everything you wanted—games, toys, maybe even a big house with a pool!      A pool? You’d probably swim in it first. But I think having money can bring a lot of stress too, like worrying about how to spend it or what others think of you.      Hmm, maybe. But if you had a lot of money, you could also help others. Like, you could give to charity or buy a house for someone who needs it.      That’s a good point. I think money can be a tool for good, but it's not the only thing that matters. Happiness comes from things like family, friends, and doing things you love.      But if you had money, you could buy all the toys you wanted. I’d have the best collection ever!      Yeah, you’d be the envy of the whole neighborhood! But I’d still rather have you here with me than a million toys.      That's the real secret, isn't it? It's not about material things or money—it's about the people you share your life with.      So, you think we’re happy because we’re together?      Yes, I do. And I don’t think we need a lot of money to be happy. I think we already have everything we need.      Yeah, we do. And we’ll always be together.      I think I’ll start saving up for a pool. Just in case.      You’ll have to ask me first—this is my house, after all.      Deal! But only if you promise to keep me company.

So, I heard you got accepted into the robotics club, Jack. That’s awesome! What’s it like?      It’s pretty cool, honestly! We’re working on building a robot that can help clean up ocean plastic. It’s kind of like a real-life invention, you know? I mean, if we can get a patent for it, maybe we could actually make a difference.      That sounds serious. But how do you even start with something like that? I mean, patents—what’s the process?      It’s not as hard as you think. You just need to come up with a unique idea, document the design, and then submit it to the patent office. But it’s also really competitive. You have to be careful not to copy someone else’s work.      Oh, I see. So it’s like a legal way of protecting your invention?      Exactly! And if you do it right, you could even get investors to back you. I mean, why not? If you’ve got a great idea, maybe you can turn it into a business.      Hmm, interesting. I’ve always thought about starting my own company, but I don’t know where to start. What about China? I heard they’re really into innovation and tech these days.      Yeah, they are. And it’s not just about the tech—they’ve got massive investments in renewable energy, AI, and even things like electric cars. Like, they’re already way ahead in some areas.      So, if I want to be an inventor, should I focus on China or stick to the UK?      That’s a good question. I think it depends on what you’re trying to achieve. If you want to get funding, maybe looking into international markets makes sense. But for now, just focus on your school projects. You never know—your idea might become something big.      I guess. I just worry about getting distracted by all the cool stuff out there. Like, what if I start thinking about inventions I can’t even build with the tools I have?      That’s normal! It’s all about taking small steps. Start with something simple, like a robot that can sort trash, and then work your way up. Who knows, maybe you’ll end up patenting something.      I might just try that. Thanks for the advice, Jack. It’s good to have someone like you around who’s into this stuff.

So, I've been thinking—should we try that new trail they mentioned? I heard it's less crowded and the views are absolutely stunning.      That sounds tempting, but I’m still a bit nervous. I’ve only ever skied on the slopes near the village. What’s the name of that trail again?      Oh, it’s called “The Serpent’s Path.” I think it’s one of the more challenging ones, but the reward is worth it. We could go later today, after lunch.      Well, if you’re sure, I guess I can try. But I’m not promising to make it all the way to the top. My knees still haven’t quite recovered from the last time I tried something too ambitious.      You’ve been skiing with me since we were kids, remember? You’re better than you give yourself credit for. I mean, you did manage to navigate that black diamond last winter, didn’t you?      True, but that was with a guide and a very strong pair of boots. I still have that blister from it.      Let’s not talk about that. Let’s focus on today. Have you already got your boots on?      Yes, actually. I thought I’d be the one dragging you out of bed this morning. You were still snoring when I got up.      That was  not  me! I was just… meditating. Or maybe I was just trying to decide what to wear. Either way, it’s not a good excuse for your lack of enthusiasm.      You’re such a drama queen. But okay, fine. Let’s go. But if I fall, I’m blaming you.      Deal. But first, let’s grab some coffee. I want to talk about the family reunion next week. I think we should invite the kids.      You’re right. We haven’t seen them in ages. It’s been over two years since we last got together. I’ve been thinking about how much they’ve grown.      And how much we’ve changed. But that’s what makes it special, isn’t it? Reconnecting, reminiscing, and just being together.      Exactly. It’s not just about the family, though. It’s about those moments—like this one, sitting here having lunch and planning our day.      Yeah. Life’s too short to waste time on anything but the people we love. Let’s make the most of it, okay?

So, I've been thinking about the badminton racket repair thing. You know, the string breaking problem. I've got some ideas about how to fix it properly, but I need your input.      Right, right, I’ve been thinking about that too. I’ve read a few things online about string tension and materials. But I haven’t tried anything yet. What exactly is the issue?      Well, the strings keep snapping, and it's costing the club a fortune. I was thinking of using stronger materials, like Kevlar or something. But I saw that people also use cable ties to secure the ends. Have you tried that?      I have, actually. I used them to hold the string in place between the grip and the main frame. But I was worried about the weight and whether it would affect the balance of the racket. What do you think?      I think it’s worth a try. Maybe we can test it on a spare racket first. As for the material, I’ve heard that polyethylene threads are more durable than nylon. They last longer and don’t break as easily.      That’s an interesting point. I should check that out. Also, I was wondering about the cost. Are we planning to sell these repair kits to other clubs?      Oh, definitely. I was even thinking of marketing it through the local BBC, maybe even pitching on Dragons’ Den. But first, we need to get the product right.      That’s a bold idea, but I like it. You know, I was in a primary school once and I remember the kids always had the same strings. Maybe the idea could work for both primary and secondary schools.      Exactly. But I’m not sure about that. I think the secondary schools need more durable materials. Though I had a funny experience once at the hairdresser—accidentally cut my ear lobe and a stripe in my hair. I still look like a kid with a stripe on my head.      Oh no! That must have been awkward. I hope you’re not still getting stares. But that’s a good reminder—sometimes things get messed up, but you can always work around it.      Right. So, back to the plan. Maybe we can test the stringing technique, document the results, and then pitch it. And if all goes well, we could start offering it as a service.      Agreed. Now, I think I need to make a list of the materials and pricing.

You know, I’ve been thinking about that painting we saw in the gallery last weekend. That one with the blue and yellow tones—it reminded me of the old coast down by Costessey. Not quite the same, but kind of similar in feeling.      I remember that one. I thought it was quite moving. It’s funny how art can bring back memories, isn’t it? I was just thinking about the old days when we’d go to the local art club. It was a different time, wasn’t it, Jerry?      Yeah, I can imagine. I’ve never been much into galleries, to be honest. My lectures are all about theory and analysis, not the emotional connection. But I do find it fascinating how people can interpret the same piece so differently.      That’s the beauty of it, isn’t it? You can look at a painting and see something entirely different from what the artist intended. I think that’s why I like teaching—it helps me understand different perspectives, even if I don’t always agree.      I think that’s what makes art so special. You can feel it in your soul, even if you can’t explain it. I used to paint a bit when I was younger, but after I retired, I just didn’t have the energy. Maybe I should pick it up again.      That’s a good idea. You know, I’ve been looking for a hobby—something to keep me occupied. Maybe you could teach me? I’ve always wanted to try painting, but never had the chance.      That’s a lovely thought. I could definitely help you get started. I’d be happy to give you some tips, even if I’m not the most experienced. Maybe we could do it together?      I’d be up for that too. It’s always good to learn something new, especially with the weather getting colder and the days shorter. It’d be a nice way to spend the afternoons.      You know, I think I might be ready to go back to it. It’s been a while, but I think I could do it. It might not be like the old days, but it might bring some joy back into my life.      That’s the spirit, Jerry. It’s never too late to start something new. And if we can do it together, that’ll make it even more fun.

So, I just wanted to say, I am  so  over the whole “girls are always so hard to please” thing. I mean, I’m not saying I don’t have my moments, but I swear, it feels like every time I go out, there’s some kind of drama or expectation.      Ugh, totally. I mean, if you think about it, we’re the same age, right? Like, we’re both in our late twenties, but somehow, we’re still getting judged for wanting to have a decent conversation or not being super into the latest Instagram trend.      Exactly! I mean, I don’t even know the people I’m hanging out with half the time. It’s like, “Oh, you’re not fitting in” – but what is the  standard ? I thought the point of being 25 was to figure out who you are, not get called out for being “too” something.      I know, right? And then you have the whole English language thing. Like, we speak English, but it’s like,  why is it so hard to have a sentence without a typo or a slang word?  I’m a mental health nurse, and I have to write reports, and it’s like, “Is this –  ha  – grammatically correct?”      Oh, I feel that. I’m a project coordinator, and I’m always like, “I’m British, I should be able to write full sentences without looking it up.” But no, it’s like we’re all texting so much now, and it’s creeping into real life. Even my boss said I need to stop using “y’all” and just say “you all.”      Oh, I get that. But you know what? I think it’s just the age we’re in. Maybe we’re all just a bit over it. I mean, I’m more concerned about my workload than my grammar. Speaking of which – have you ever  truly  procrastinated something so much that you just… lost it?      Oh, always. Like, I have this big presentation next week, and I’ve been like, “Maybe I’ll start it tomorrow.” But tomorrow is now, and I’m still scrolling through TikTok. I feel like I’m slipping into the  ultimate  adult version of a student.      Don’t worry, I’ve been there. I had this one time where I was supposed to do a client assessment, and I just…  forgot . Like, I literally had to call them and explain that I’d messed up.

So, I was thinking today, do you ever feel like we’re living in a world where common sense is being ignored in favor of what’s technically correct? I mean, take something like drinking. Everyone knows alcohol is bad for you, but somehow people still do it. It’s like the brain knows what’s best, but the body doesn’t listen.      Well, that’s the thing with vices, isn’t it? We all have them, even if we don’t admit it. I mean, I’ve been trying to quit smoking for years. I just finished my third sock. It’s taking forever, but I love the pattern. You know, it’s a bit like the Olympics—meticulous, repetitive, and I can’t wait to see the final product. Whether it’s a new pattern in your knitting, a new piece of art, or a new idea in your research. It’s all connected somehow. Exactly. I think that’s why I like being in Cambridge.

So, I just got a review on Twitter for my café. It was really cringey. Someone wrote, "The coffee here tastes like burnt toast and regret." I’m like, "It’s £3.50, and it’s made with real ingredients." He just said, "You’re charging too much for a piece of bread."

Okay, I've got a few raspberries from the garden. I thought we could try making some raspberry ice cream for dessert tonight. Okay, so I’ve got this baby who’s just started weaning, and it’s a bit of a minefield. I’m trying to introduce solids, but I can’t get her to take anything other than breast milk. So, you know, I was just thinking about how different these hills are from the ones back in London. You don’t really notice them when you're stuck in traffic or something.      Yeah, I can see what you mean. In London, you’re more used to the skyline and concrete. But out here, the hills are like living things—they roll on forever. I mean, the birds, the wind... everything seems to have its own rhythm.      It's such a contrast from the city. I remember when I first moved here, I thought I'd be missing the noise. And the villages, they’re like chapters in that story. Each one has its own history, its own charm. I’d love to visit all of them. And we’ll have plenty of afternoons left to explore. So, what’s next? There’s that little hill we haven’t climbed yet, right?

So, I just saw this film called  The Last Tree —you know, the one with that eco-activist character? Honestly, it was so intense. I couldn’t stop thinking about it after. So, you know, I was just thinking about how different the countryside here in Norfolk is compared to London. It's so peaceful out here, isn’t it? It’s not just about grammar or syntax—it’s about identity. You can tell so much about a person’s background from the way they speak. I was just thinking – have you noticed how the geese in the park are migrating again? I’ve been seeing them every morning, just flying over the rooftops.      Oh, those are the ones that come in the autumn, aren’t they? I used to love watching them. I remember when I was a kid, my gran would take me to the park every weekend to see them. I mean, I thought I’d be doing something more... creative?      Yeah, I get that. I mean, I’m in admin, but I’ve always had this dream of working in a nonprofit or something. You know, doing meaningful work. But it’s hard to break into that kind of field when you’ve got student debt and all.      I know. I’ve been thinking about going back to school for another postgrad in project management. It’s a bit of a risk, but I feel like I need to up my skills. I mean, I’m not in a position to just take a job for the sake of it.      That makes sense. I’ve been looking into volunteering with some local charities too. Maybe I can gain some experience and see if that’s the path for me. It’s not like I have a lot of other options, I mean, with the economy as it is.      Yeah, it’s tough. I mean, I’m in a lower managerial role, so I’m not exactly rich. I know you’re in intermediate, but I feel like we’re both in the same boat. It’s just different directions.      True. I mean, someone has to be the one to start a movement, right? Or at least try. I’m not sure if I have the guts, but I’ve got to try something. I don’t want to end up in a job I don’t care about just because it pays the bills.      That’s brave. I admire that. I mean, it’s not like I haven’t thought about it. I’ve just been so focused on getting through the day. But I think maybe I need to start planning. What if I take a few months off? Just travel or something. That could give me time to figure out what I really want.      That sounds like a good idea. I mean, you don’t get a second chance at youth, right? If I don’t do something now, I might regret it later. I’m not saying I’ll do the same, but it’s worth considering.

So, I just got back from the café, and I saw this guy with his girlfriend. He was totally ignoring her and texting someone else. I’m like,  what a tosser ! Why would you do that? You’re with her, right?      Aw, that’s so annoying. I’ve been there. I had this guy who would flirt with all the girls at the bar. I mean, he was with me, but he’d be staring at someone else like,  “Hey, can you give me a minute?”       Oh no, I’ve seen that too. I mean, I don’t have a boyfriend, but I’ve had friends who’ve been through it. It’s so frustrating. You’re trying to be romantic, and they’re like,  “Not now, I’m busy.”       Yeah, it’s like,  “We’re here together, so why are you replying to messages from someone else?”  I mean, if you’re not into the relationship, maybe you should just say something. But if you are, then you should be present.      Exactly. And it’s not just guys either. I’ve had a friend who was in a relationship where her girlfriend would flirt with other girls. It’s just so confusing. You’re trying to build something, and then it feels like you’re not even in the conversation.      I mean, I’ve had a few one-night stands, but I didn’t have a long-term relationship. I guess jealousy is something that comes with being in a relationship. But I think it’s more about communication. If you’re feeling insecure about something, you should talk about it instead of acting out.      Totally. I know that. But sometimes people don’t want to talk. They just want to ignore the problem. Like,  “Oh, I’m not jealous. I’m just not into it.”  But that’s not helpful. You can’t just shut it down.      And then there’s the whole  “Jealousy is bad”  thing. I mean, it’s not always bad. It can be a sign that you care. But if it’s making you act out, or if it’s causing arguments, then yeah, it’s a problem.      I think it’s about boundaries. If you’re in a relationship, you should both agree on what’s acceptable. And if one person is constantly acting out, that’s a red flag.      Yeah, and if someone’s not willing to work on it, then maybe it’s time to walk away.

So, I just got a text from my sister saying her kids are  still  arguing over what to cook for dinner. I’m like,  this is what happens when you have a family of chefs . Not to mention my own kids— they  wouldn’t know a recipe if it hit them in the face!      I know what you mean. My brother-in-law once tried to cook a roast dinner, and it ended up being a charcoal briquette. I had to call the fire department. But at least we’ve got the kids here now. They’re like little miniature chefs. Though I still can’t figure out why the fridge is always empty.      Hey, did you hear about the hockey match tonight? My mates are playing, and they said it’s going to be a rematch of last year’s final. They’re saying it’s going to be epic.      Yeah, I heard too. My dad’s even thinking about going. He said he’s been dying to see some real action since the last time we watched a game. I mean, we all know he’s still got that old-school player mentality, even though he’s been retired for years.      My son’s been training all week, and he’s really excited about it. He’s been saying he’s going to be the next star of the team. I don’t know if he’s ready for that kind of pressure, but I’m glad he’s into it. But hey, kids these days—juggling sports and school isn’t easy. I used to have to handle both when I was in college. My sister’s got the same kid, and she’s already worried about him getting too much into hockey and not studying.      I think he’s getting enough pressure. Last week, he got a D in his math test, and his mom was  this close  to banning hockey forever. I tried telling her it’s just one test, but she’s not listening. She’s on a mission to make him a straight-A student.      You’re all missing the point. Hockey isn’t just about school. It’s about team spirit, and the kind of friendships you make out there.

So, I just got this really weird message from my cousin Sarah. She said her dog, Biscuit, got into the garden and somehow managed to chew through the whole fence. I mean, how does a dog even do that?      Oh wow, that’s wild. I’ve heard of dogs getting into things, but chewing through an entire fence? That sounds like a full-on disaster. Did she call the council or anything?      No, actually, she was just venting. She said she’s still trying to figure out how to fix it without spending a fortune. I mean, the fence was brand new. She’s been working so hard to keep up with everything since she moved into that new house.      Yeah, I can imagine. I had a similar situation with my brother last year. He bought this little dog, thinking it was a good idea for the garden. But the thing is, this dog’s like a little tornado. It just went off and dug up the whole backyard in one go.      Oh no, that sounds like a nightmare. I guess it’s just the price of having pets, right? But still, I feel for her. I mean, she’s not even fully settled in, and then this happens.      Exactly. I think it’s part of the journey, though. You learn to deal with the chaos. Although, I will say, I never thought I’d be the kind of person who could get into a full-blown debate with a dog about the rules of the garden.      Haha, fair point. I guess we’re all just trying to survive in this world of unpredictable animals and even more unpredictable humans. Speaking of which, I still haven’t seen the last of my old friend Jane. She’s been acting so strangely lately.      Oh, she’s been through a lot. She told me she’s been having some serious anxiety issues. I think it’s all the pressure of working full-time and trying to keep up with her social life. It’s hard, isn’t it?      It really is. I mean, we’re all supposed to be adults now, but honestly, it feels like we’re all just trying to hold it together. I think that’s why we’re all out here, on this road trip, right? To take a break from it all.      Exactly. I think we all need a reminder that life isn’t just about deadlines and responsibilities.

So, I tried to make chicken kievs last night, and they turned out more like chicken bricks than kievs. I think I over-marinated them or something.      That sounds like a disaster. You can’t even make chicken kievs in Ireland, can you? It’s like trying to make sushi with a steak.      Oh, come on, you know it’s just a British dish. We’ve had it in the States too. But I’ve always preferred the ones with a bit of a crust.      Yeah, I know. I just thought it would be easy. But I think I used too much flour or something. The whole thing was just a mess.      Maybe you should just buy them from the deli. I heard they’re called “chicken cutlets” now, or something like that.      Yeah, and I still don’t understand why they’re called kievs. Sounds like some kind of Russian take on a chicken sandwich.      It’s probably because of the British obsession with naming things after places. I remember when we got “stuffed” – it’s just a sandwich, right?      It’s all part of the British tradition of confusing the world with our food. And let’s not even talk about the rugby.      Oh, the rugby. I can’t watch it without getting all fired up. I think I might be going to the match this weekend.      You’re not serious, are you? We’ve had a few weeks of rain and now you want to go to a game?      You’re going to miss your sister’s visit. She’s coming over next week, and she’s bringing a few of those famous English biscuits.      Ugh, I know. But I’ve always wanted to see the game in person. I’ve got a friend who’s got a season ticket.      Yeah, I get it. It’s a tradition. But maybe next time? I’ve got a headache from eating too many biscuits last week.      You’ve been eating way too many biscuits. And I think I’ve got a bit of a headache too.      I’m not surprised. The biscuits are like a language we all speak.      Yeah, and I think I’ve got a few more in my bag. Should I bring them over?      You don’t have to. We’ve got enough to last a month.      Well, if you’re done with the biscuits, I’ll be over in a minute.

So, I just got an email from the seller about the vintage cups and saucers I bid on. They said the shipping will take about a week, so I should have them by the weekend. I was thinking we could set up a little display in the kitchen—maybe for the community market next month.      That sounds great, actually. I’ve been meaning to get some of those vintage items myself. I saw a few on eBay last week, but I was worried about the condition. You know how it can be with second-hand stuff.      Yeah, it’s a bit of a gamble, but I think the seller had good reviews, and the photos looked pretty authentic. I managed to get the set for around £30, which isn’t bad. I’ve always loved the look of those old porcelain sets. I think they’d add a nice touch to the market stall.      Definitely. I’ve been thinking about the market too. I need to wrap up my work leaving do, and I’d love to have something to bring along. The cups and saucers could work well—people always love a bit of charm.      I agree. And besides, we’ve got that buckwheat bread we baked last week. It’s still in the fridge, right? We could use it as part of the market stall. People love that sort of homemade stuff.      Oh, yes! I almost forgot about that. I think it’s going to be perfect with the tea. I was going to make a fresh batch tonight, but maybe we should save some for the market. It’s got that great earthy flavor that people really enjoy.      Exactly. And I’ve been talking to my cousin about setting up a cooking demo. She’s got some great ideas for using buckwheat. Maybe we can tie that in with the vintage display. It could be a real hit.      That’s a solid plan. I was thinking about the community market yesterday, too. The organizers are looking for volunteers to help out with setup and tidying up. I should probably sign up for that.      Yeah, that would be a good idea. We could split the work so we go in together. It’ll be nice to have some time to chat and catch up.      Sounds good. I’ll send you an email with the details. And maybe we can pick up some more vintage items next week.

So, I heard you got a fine for tax evasion again, Dave? You’re really got a talent for slipping through the cracks, don’t you?      Oh, stop it, Ruth. It was a misunderstanding. The accountant said it was a clerical error. But yeah, I got one of those little letters about money laundering— again .      Oh, I bet you didn’t even read it properly, did you? You’re always in a rush to get back to your café and your new vegan latte obsession.      That’s not the point, Jess. You know I’m doing what I can. I’ve got a small business, a few employees, and I’m trying to keep it all afloat. If I didn’t push the boundaries, I’d be out of business.      I can see that. But isn’t that the risk when you’re running your own show? I mean, I’m just a student—still trying to figure out what I want to do. Sometimes I wonder if I’ll ever even have a career like yours.      Yeah, I’m stuck in the same boat. Sixth-form – no clear path, no real job. My parents just expect me to “get a proper job.” But I don’t even know what that means anymore.      You know, when I was your age, I didn’t have a clue either. I went to university, did a postgraduate degree, and then… here I am. A business owner, in the middle of a legal hassle with the bank. It’s not all smooth sailing, but it’s what I chose.      And I have to say, it’s not all bad. You learn a lot. I mean, if I had a stable job and followed the rules, I’d never have got my business off the ground. Sometimes you’ve got to take a few shortcuts to make it.      But what about the fines? I’ve heard stories about people getting caught for money laundering—like, real criminal stuff. That’s not the same as running a small business, is it?      No, it’s not. But the line between what’s legal and what’s not is getting thinner every day. You see, it’s not just about the money—it’s about how it moves, where it comes from, where it goes.      Exactly. I’ve had to do a lot of paperwork, make sure everything is above board.

So, the weather’s been absolutely dreadful this week, hasn’t it? I mean, it’s like it’s still February, even though it’s already June. I can’t believe we’ve had three days of rain in a row.      Lucky for us, it’s not like we’re out there doing anything that requires an umbrella. But still, it's been a real hassle. I’ve been working from home this week, so I got to stay under cover. It was a bit of a relief.      You're lucky, really. I had to drive my kids to school this morning, and the roads were a mess. I almost had an accident. It was like everyone else’s car was also stuck in the same puddle.      That sounds terrifying! I was just in the store this morning, and it was already soaked. I had to park my car and walk through this pool of water just to get in. It’s not the first time, though, and I don’t think it’ll be the last.      You know, I’ve been thinking about that sign language class we were all talking about last week. It’s only a few weeks away now, right? I’m really hoping we can all make it.      Yes, I know. It’s such a good idea. Especially with the new baby coming. I think learning sign language could be really helpful for when we start interacting with the baby.      That’s a great point. I had a cousin who used sign language with their baby, and it helped a lot. It’s also something that can be done by parents and grandparents alike. I think it’s a win-win.      Yeah, and it’s not too hard to learn. I mean, it’s just a few basic signs, right? I’ve been looking up some videos online. I think I’ve got the idea.      I think we should meet up before the class to practice. We could all come over and go through the basics. That way, we’ll all be more confident when the actual class starts.      That sounds like a good plan. I can go over on Thursday. I know you’re free, so maybe you could come as well?      Absolutely. I’ll check my schedule and make sure I’m free. I’ve been meaning to take some time for myself anyway, so this would be a great chance to connect with the group.

So, I just heard someone in the office say “I’ll be with you in a tick.” I thought they were trying to be British, but it’s not even a real phrase!      Oh, come on, that’s classic. I’ve heard that in my hometown. It’s like, “I’ll be with you in a tick,” but you’ve got to be  really  in a hurry.      Yeah, and you know what’s worse? “I’ll be right with you.” That’s not just a phrase—it’s a whole vibe. Like, you’re not just coming, you’re  spending  time with them.      I get that. But honestly, I feel like some of these expressions are just relics. It’s like, do people even use them anymore, or are we just recycling old Anglo-Saxon idioms?      I mean, I grew up in Sweden, and even there, we had our own sayings. I think it’s just a way to make language human. You can’t just say “I’m coming,” you’ve got to give it some flair.      Exactly. And it’s not just the phrases—it’s the way people speak. Like, you have to know what dialect you’re in. I mean, I’m from England, but I hear people from the South say things like “biscuit” instead of “cookie.”      And I’ve been in the UK for a while, but I still pick up on the accents. I can tell when someone’s from London, or from the North, or even from somewhere like Aylesbury. It’s like a code.      Oh, I’m from Aylesbury. And honestly, I think it gives you an edge. I mean, I’ve met people from all over the world who just don’t know how to use the right word in the right context.      That’s why I’m here, right? To learn the ins and outs of British English. It’s like a whole new language for me, even though I speak English.      And your accent is so different. I can tell you’re not from here, but I love it. It gives the conversation a nice mix.      Yeah, and I think that’s the beauty of it. You’ve got people from all over, bringing different influences. It’s like a melting pot of accents and expressions.      To the British language, and the people who make it so much fun.

So, I've been thinking—should we start looking for a venue for the rally tomorrow? The more people we can get, the better. I mean, we’re going to Mongolia, right? It's not like we can just pull this off from our flat in Warrington.      Yeah, I know. But we need to get the logistics sorted first. Have you heard back from the organizers about the visa application? I tried to call them last night, but they were all booked up.      I haven’t heard back yet, but I’m going to email them again this morning. I’m worried because we need to submit the forms by the end of the week. And if we don’t, we might miss the deadline.      That’s what I’m afraid of. I think the embassy is really strict about these things. I remember reading online that they require a detailed itinerary and proof of funds. You know, like a bank statement or something.      Yeah, I know. I was thinking, maybe we should start raising some money for the trip. We’ve got that donation page up on Gumtree, right? It’s getting a few hits, but not enough.      Definitely. I’ve already put up a few ads on Gumtree, but they’re not getting much traction. Maybe we should try to reach out to some local businesses or universities. You know, our uni might be able to help.      I was just thinking about that. I had a friend from my degree who works at a community center. Maybe we could ask them if they can spread the word. Plus, we need to get our passport photos done. I can’t just use the ones from my last trip to India.      Exactly. I’m going to book an appointment at the local photo booth tomorrow. I heard they’re pretty quick and cheap. You want to come with me? It’ll be easier to get the photos done together.      Sure, that sounds good. I’ve been putting it off, but I figure I might as well get it over with. And maybe we can set up the charity page properly while we’re there.      Agreed. If we can get the passport photos done and the charity page up to speed, we’ll be on our way. It’s going to be a bit of a whirlwind, but I think we’ve got this.

I can't believe I ended up in A&E last night. I think I broke my arm or something. I was just trying to run after my friend who had a panic attack, and I tripped over a stray cat.      Oh no, really? That’s rough. Was it that bad? I heard you were out all night. Did you get a good sleep?      Not really. I just got home at like 3 a.m. and was so exhausted. I tried to sleep, but my arm was killing me. I even had to call my mum to come over and make sure I wasn’t in worse shape.      Wow, that sounds like a disaster. I’m so sorry. I hope you’re okay. You should’ve called an ambulance, though. I mean, if you were really hurt, you could’ve gotten proper help.      I know, I know. I just thought it was a sprain. But apparently, it’s a crack. I’ve got to see the physio tomorrow. I can’t even lift my coffee cup without hurting.      That’s rough. I mean, I still can’t believe you went on that trip. I thought you were just going to meet up for a drink. But I guess you were worried because you thought she was in trouble.      Yeah, I was. I mean, she’s been really stressed lately. She's been seeing a therapist and everything. But I think she just needed someone to be there for her.      That’s sweet of you. I wish more people would do that. I mean, it’s about time we stopped being so self-centered. Sometimes, the people around us are the ones who need support.      I know. It just feels like university life is so draining, you know? Between studying, friends, and all the chaos, it’s hard to keep up.      Definitely. I’ve been so tired lately. I’m still recovering from that party last week. I think I drank three times the amount of alcohol I ever have before.      Oh no, did you throw up? Because I did. And I still feel like I’m going to. I think I’m going to start going to the gym more. It’s the only thing that makes me feel like I’m actually doing something.      Yeah, I’d love to start going to the gym, but I’ve been too tired. I think I’m going to take a break from everything for a bit.

So, did you see the way the whole family came together for the anniversary party last night? It was like a big Yorkshire family reunion. I was just so proud to see everyone, especially the kids.      Yeah, it was pretty cool. I mean, I didn’t get to meet half of them, but the ones I did see were really into it. My cousin Tom even brought his dog along. I thought he was serious about that dog show thing.      Oh, Tom’s a good kid. He’s got a real way with animals, don’t you think? I saw him walking the dog around the garden, and it was like he and the pup were having a conversation. You could tell they were bonded.      For sure. And then there was my aunt Dotty, she was just in her element. She had that little table set up with all the old photos, and she was telling stories about when she was a kid. It was like being transported back in time.      She still has that energy, even though she’s getting on in years. I remember when she was teaching in the village school. She was a bit of a legend, wasn’t she? Her lessons on the history of York were legendary, if I do say so myself.      She still talks about it all the time. She even told me about the time she got into a bit of a tangle with the local council over a traffic sign. They wanted to put one up on the main street, but she argued that it was unnecessary. Turns out, she was right.      Oh, she’s got that fire in her. You know, I was thinking about the whole thing last night. It really made me appreciate how much the family has changed over the years. But at the same time, it felt like we were all still the same, just older and wiser.      Yeah, I guess that’s the thing about family. No matter how far apart we are, or how much time passes, we’re always connected. It was a great reminder of that.      Absolutely. I was just thinking, maybe we should set up a tradition of having an annual family gathering. Don’t you think? It’s something we could all look forward to.      I’d like that. Maybe we can even start planning the next one. It could be something like a picnic in the park or a trip to the countryside.

Dad, I just put my water bottle in the cooler bag, and it’s like it got turned upside down mid-air. I’m so confused.      You didn’t do anything wrong, lass. I remember when you were little, you tried to fill your water bottle with the garden hose and it just poured all over the floor. You were a mess.      Yeah, and you were so upset, thinking I’d broken the whole hose. I was just trying to chase the cat!      You were always chasing something, weren’t you? Even now, you’re always trying to keep up with me.      Well, I’m 16 now, Dad. I’m not a kid anymore. I just had an exam, and I’m going to start sixth form next term. I’ve been thinking about moving house in a couple of years.      Yeah, I heard you were thinking about taking over the old shop. You know, that’s not too bad. You’ve got a good head on your shoulders.      It’s not just the shop. I’m thinking of moving somewhere with more space – maybe near the coast. I’d like to live closer to the sea.      That’s a good idea. You’ve always liked the sea. Remember when you were little, and we’d go to the seaside in Blackpool? You were so excited about the ice creams and the sand.      I still love the sea, but I think I’d like to see more of the world. Maybe travel to Japan or even Norway to see the northern lights.      Japan sounds amazing. I’ve always wanted to go, but I’ve never had the time. You might get to see that. Just remember to take your pen – you know, for the forms and everything.      Yeah, I had a pen in my bag. I also got a new notebook from Holland and Barrett – I’ve been thinking about studying Latin.      That’s a good move. You’ll need it if you’re going to be a lawyer or a doctor, like I was.      I might not be a lawyer. I’m thinking of studying languages. Maybe Hungarian?      Oh, you’ll be the only one in the whole town who can speak Hungarian. But go for it, lass. You’ve got the brains for it.      Thanks, Dad. I just hope I can keep up with you.      You’ll be fine.

So, I've been thinking about the new software we're supposed to be using for the transcription work. It's supposed to make things faster, but honestly, I’m not sure I like the way it's structured. It feels a bit too rigid, like it’s forcing us into a format that doesn’t quite fit the way we usually do things.      I hear you. I tried a test run last week, and I felt the same way. The interface is confusing, and there are so many steps to go through before you even get to the actual transcription. It’s like they made it too complicated for people who just want to get the job done.      I can understand that. My son, who’s in IT, said the same thing about the new system they’re using at the school. He thought it was a bit of a mess at first, but after a while, it started making sense. Maybe we just need some time to get used to it.      I didn’t have the chance to look at it, but I’ve heard the same complaints. I always prefer working with things I’m familiar with, even if they’re not the latest and greatest. Change can be tricky, especially when it’s not clearly explained.      That’s true. I’m not against progress, but I do think there needs to be more support and training when introducing new tools. Especially if we’re already juggling a lot of other tasks.      Yeah, I think that’s a good point. I’ve got a few colleagues who are really struggling with the transition. It’s not just about the software—it’s about the learning curve and how we adapt to it.      I remember when I first became a headmistress. There was so much change in the education system, and it took time to adjust. But once you do, it can actually be quite beneficial. It’s just about finding the right balance.      I guess that’s what it comes down to. We all want to do the best job we can, but if the tools are not right for the job, it can be frustrating. I’d be happy to help run a workshop or something if the team wants to get more comfortable with it.      That sounds like a great idea. We could all benefit from a bit of hands-on training.

Okay, I've got a list of things I need to do for Mother’s Day, but I’m not quite sure how to fit them all in.      That sounds stressful! What are you planning?      I’m helping Mom with her garden. She’s been wanting to plant some flowers for a while.      Oh, that’s a great idea! I was thinking of doing something similar, maybe taking her to Forest School. I heard it’s a nice way to spend time outdoors and get some fresh air.      Forest School? Like, the one where you go into the woods and build things?      Yes, exactly! It’s an educational program for children, but I thought maybe we could do something similar, just for fun. It’s a chance to get away from the city and be close to nature, which Mom really enjoys.      Can I come too? I love being outside, even if it's just in the garden.      Of course! We can all go together. I can drive, and we can bring some snacks and a picnic blanket.      What about a little gift? Mom would love that.      That’s a good point. I was going to get her a book, maybe something about gardening or nature.      I know! There’s this joke about Mother’s Day. Let me think... Why don’t skeletons fight each other?      Because they don’t have the guts!      Oh! That’s a classic. I love that one.      I have another one. Why don’t eggs tell jokes?      Because they might crack up!      Brilliant! You’re both getting better at these.      I’m trying to remember more idioms too. Like, “the early bird catches the worm.”      Exactly! It’s a great way to make things more interesting. I think you’re both learning a lot by helping with the garden and planning the trip.      I feel like I’m getting more grown up every day.      You’re doing great, buddy. It’s all about learning and having fun with the family.      So, to recap: Forest School, a gift, and some food. That’s the plan?      Yep! And a few jokes to keep things light. Mother’s Day is going to be awesome.      I can’t wait! I’m going to help Mom plant some flowers.      I’ll bring the snacks.      Perfect. Let’s get ready and make sure Mom has the best day ever!      Agreed! Let’s go!

So, I just got a call from Linda — she’s been feeling really unwell, and it turns out she’s been diagnosed with cancer. I’m so worried about her. I know she’s been having these fatigue symptoms for a while, but she kept putting it off.      Oh no, that’s terrible. I’m really sorry to hear that. I hope she’s getting the right care and support now. Cancer’s so unpredictable, isn’t it? It can hit anyone at any time.      It really can. And it’s not just the physical part — I’ve noticed she’s been more withdrawn lately. She’s been having trouble sleeping, and she’s stressed about work and the kids. I think she’s dealing with a lot more than just the illness.      Yes, mental health is just as important, if not more so. I remember when my dad was diagnosed with prostate cancer a few years back — he was in denial for a long time. It took some time for him to accept it, and even longer for him to start treatment.      That sounds really tough. But I’ve also seen how strong people can be when they’re facing something like this. I’ve been trying to be there for Linda, but I know she needs more than just my support. She needs professional help, and she needs the family around her.      Absolutely. And it’s not just about the patient — the family is affected too. I’ve been thinking about how my mom is coping with my brother’s chronic illness. She’s managing, but it’s wearing her down. I wish there was more support out there for people in these situations.      I know. It’s hard to balance everything — work, family, and your own mental health. I’ve been trying to take some time off to be with Linda, but I also have my own clients to look after. It’s a real juggling act.      I can only imagine. You’re doing a great job being there for her. I think it’s important to not ignore your own needs too. If you’re feeling overwhelmed, you should reach out for help. You don’t have to do this alone.      Thanks, I appreciate that. I know I’m not alone in this, and I’m lucky to have friends like you who understand what it’s like.

Hey, you've got a weird expression on your face. Are you okay? You look like you've seen a ghost or something.      Oh, I’m fine. Just thinking about that lecture we had yesterday about South Korean festivals. It was so interesting. I couldn’t stop thinking about how different it is from our own traditions.      Yeah, I know. I’ve been thinking about that too. I mean, I’ve studied linguistics, so I get how language shapes culture and how festivals are like a mirror of that. But it’s still fascinating to see how something like the Lunar New Year is so deeply embedded in their society.      Exactly. It’s not just about the celebration; it’s about the entire system of family, respect, and hierarchy. I feel like I’ve been studying the same thing in my English classes about how our own festivals, like Christmas, are more about community and family, but not in the same way.      Right, and that’s why I think language is so important—especially when it comes to understanding other cultures. I mean, I teach English, so I’m always trying to explain the nuances, like how we say “I’m going to the store” versus “I’m going shopping,” which can have different connotations.      That’s why I’m glad I’m studying to be a teacher too. I want to help people understand not just the language, but also the culture behind it. Though I’m still trying to decide whether to go into language teaching or something else.      You should stick with it. I mean, your curiosity is already there. And I know you’re good at it. Plus, talking about different cultures is what makes teaching so fun.      Thanks. I think I’m going to start planning some lessons on different festivals. Maybe even compare them to British ones. It could be a cool project.      That sounds awesome. Let me know if you need help with the research or if you want to do a joint presentation. I’ve got some articles on the role of language in cultural identity that you might find useful.      I would love that. Thanks, I’ll reach out later. And hey, don’t forget we’re having dinner tonight. You need to stop studying all the time and actually cook something.      Okay, okay. I’ll try. Just give me a few minutes to finish this article on Chinese festivals, and then I’ll come help you with the dinner.

So, I just got this really weird present for Secret Santa. A box of flavoured vodka. I don’t even know how it got there. I’m not sure I can drink it, but I guess I’ll try it. What about you guys?      Oh no, that sounds terrifying. I got a box of glitter pens. I was like, “What even is this?” But they were super high quality. I used them on my laptop and my keyboard, and now it’s like a glitter dump. I can’t even clean it off.      That sounds like a nightmare. I got a pair of boxers that were so tight, I couldn’t even put them on. I had to ask my flatmate for help, and she just laughed. It was ridiculous.      Oh, I got a set of sports kit tops. It was like a whole collection of different sports. I tried to wear them to class, but I looked like a confused athlete. And the ones for cricket? They were way too big.      I feel you. I had to wear one of those “I ♥ Art History” T-shirts to a lecture once. I got so many weird looks. But hey, it was fun.      Speaking of fun, remember that time we got tickets to the Sugarhouse nightclub? We were so excited, but we ended up getting lost on the way. We accidentally ended up in a karaoke bar. It was the worst.      I still remember that. We tried to follow the signs, but they were all in some weird dialect. I think it was like Yorkshire. I couldn’t even understand half of it.      Yeah, I think the problem was that we were too drunk to read the map. We ended up there and then barely made it back.      That’s the thing about being students. We’re always trying to have fun, but we end up in the most ridiculous situations. Speaking of which, I tried to play Heads Up with my flatmates the other day, and I ended up doing a terrible impression of Jack Whitehall.      That sounds like a disaster. I tried to do an impression of Sheldon from  The Big Bang Theory  once, and I got completely lost.      I think I’m going to try to do an impression of Twilight’s Edward Cullen. I can’t wait to see how that goes.      I think we all have to start a group called “The Improv Club.”

So, I was just thinking about that weekend trip we took to the Lake District. You remember when we got stuck in the rain and had to sleep in that tiny cabin?      Oh, how could I forget? I still have the photo of us both in those ridiculous raincoats, looking like two lost tourists. I swear the cabin was smaller than my aunt’s bathroom.      Yeah, and the only thing that saved us was the fact that we had a fire going. I think it was the first time I ever felt so warm in my life.      You were freezing, though. I remember you shivering so hard, you looked like a wet cat. You kept asking if the fire was going to go out, like it was going to save us from something.      I think I was just really nervous. I mean, we were miles from anywhere, and the weather was just… wrong. I kept checking my phone, hoping for a signal, but we had no bars.      That’s when I pulled out my emergency kit, remember? I had a thermos, a blanket, even a couple of energy bars. It was like I’d been preparing for something like that my whole life.      You always do that. You’re the one who brings the survival gear, and I’m the one who forgets my own keys. It’s like we're the two halves of a survivalist team.      Hey, you did bring the extra socks, though. That was a win.      Yeah, and I even remembered to pack the waterproof jacket. Look, I wasn’t all that useless.      Exactly. You just needed a little nudge from me. Maybe next time you’ll be the one with the survival kit.      Maybe, but I’d rather you be the one who knows how to start a fire with just a piece of cloth and some sticks. I’m not sure I’d ever figure that out.      You’ll learn. Just like you’ll learn how to not keep checking your phone in the middle of the wilderness.      Touché. But seriously, that trip taught me a lot. I mean, surviving a few hours in the woods with you is almost like a mini survival course.      Yeah, and you made it through. I think that counts as a success.      Definitely. It’s just like we’re built for each other—me for the panic, and you for the calm.

You know, I’ve been feeling a bit off lately. Not sure if it’s the cold or just getting older, but I’ve got this constant ache in my knee. It’s been bothering me all week.      I’ve been feeling the same, really. I think it’s the weather. The cold wind from the north has been really harsh lately. I’ve been staying under the blanket more than I used to. You know how it is, getting older and the body doesn’t handle the cold as well.      I’ve been keeping warm, but I can still feel the chill. I’ve been thinking about getting a new heater for the flat. I’ve heard those new smart thermostats are a bit more efficient now.      Yeah, I’ve been thinking about that too. I’ve even looked into buying one online. But honestly, I’m not sure if I can deal with all that tech stuff. My phone is still a mystery to me, let alone a smart thermostat.      I know what you mean. I still can’t tell the difference between my old TV and my new one. I remember when we first got the digital box. It took me ages to figure out how to change the channels.      I did the same. I used to call it ‘the magic box’ for a while. I still get confused when it comes to the remote. You just press the button and hope it works.      It’s not that hard. I had to learn it for my lectures. I mean, I walk into the lecture hall with a laptop and a projector, and I have to adjust the settings. It’s not that different from the TV, really.      I’d say you’re more tech-savvy than I am. You know, I was thinking about getting a new phone. I’ve been waiting for a new model. I’ve been using the same one since 2017. It’s starting to slow down.      You’re lucky you can afford a new one. I’ve been holding on to mine for years. I think I might just upgrade to a tablet instead. I can use that for reading and watching videos. It’s more comfortable for my hands.      I think I’ll stick with mine for now. I like the simplicity of it. I’ve got my phone for emergencies. You know, I just need to call someone when the weather gets too bad, or when my knee starts acting up.

Hey, girls, it's been ages! I’ve been meaning to catch up with you all. How have you been?      I’ve been good, thanks! Just been super busy with work. You know how it is, managing sales and all. How about you, Speck?      I’ve been okay, but honestly, it’s been a bit of a blur lately. I’ve been working on this big project at the studio, and it’s been taking up all my time. But I'm surviving, I guess.      Yeah, same here. I’ve been juggling art deadlines and trying to get my head around this new software. Honestly, it’s been a bit overwhelming, but I’m pushing through.      Well, I’m glad you’re all still around. I’ve been thinking about you all, and I wanted to catch up. Let’s talk about something fun—your weddings! I mean, don’t get me wrong, I'm not trying to push you into anything, but I’ve heard so many stories about your friends getting married.      Oh, you don’t need to push! We’re all in our early twenties, and we’re not even thinking about marriage yet. But I have to say, I’ve been thinking about it a bit, like, maybe in a few years. You know, once I’m more settled in my career.      I’m not even sure if I want kids yet. I mean, I love the idea of a family, but I’d rather focus on my art and my career first. What about you, Speck?      Honestly, I’m about the same. I think the idea of having kids is cool, but I’m not ready yet. I think I’d like to see where my life goes first. But I can see how some people might want to jump into it right away.      I get it. I think a lot of us are just figuring it out. I mean, I’m still single, and I’m not in a rush. I’d rather focus on my admin job and maybe even go back to school for a bit. Still, it’s amazing how quickly time passes, isn’t it?      You’re not alone in that. I think we’re all just trying to figure out who we are and what we want. It’s a journey, and it’s okay to take your time.      Exactly.

You know, I’ve been trying to get my head around this new tablet I got. It’s all about the apps, isn’t it? I can’t even remember what “apps” are, honestly. I mean, I’ve got a phone, but it’s like it’s got a life of its own now.      Oh, don’t you worry, love. I remember when I was your age, I used to think a phone was just for making calls. Now it’s like a mini computer in your hand. I still can’t work out how to share photos with my grandkids, though. I keep sending the wrong ones by accident.      You’re not alone, really. I’ve had to teach my kids how to use these things. It’s like a whole new language, isn’t it? I remember when I was a teacher, I used to say “computers are just tools,” but now they’re everywhere, even in the classroom.      I suppose it’s all part of growing up, isn’t it? Back in my day, you didn’t need a tablet to keep in touch. You just had a letter. I remember when I got married, my wife and I wrote every single letter. No postage stamps, just ink and paper.      Yes, I remember that. You used to get those big envelopes, and you’d have to wait for weeks. I still miss that. It felt more personal. I mean, you had to think about what you were saying. Now, it’s all instant messages and notifications.      I think there’s something to be said for the slower pace. I’ve been trying to get back to that with my own kids. I’ve started teaching them how to write letters again. It’s a nice way to slow down, even if it’s not practical.      I agree. I’ve been getting into horses too, you know. I’ve got this old stable in the village. I keep a few ponies. It’s the only thing that keeps me going these days. I like the quiet, the routine.      That’s lovely! I’ve always wanted to get back into horses. I used to ride when I was younger, but after the accident, I couldn’t. Still, it’s good to have something to look forward to.      Yeah, hobbies are important, especially when money’s tight. You know, I’ve been thinking about taking up something like that.

You know, I’ve been thinking a lot about how language changes. It’s fascinating how people from different regions of England still find ways to understand each other, even with all these accents and dialects.      Oh, I’ve heard that all my life. I used to think I was from Essex, but I bet you could tell I’m from the south just by listening to me talk. I mean, I remember when I was a managing director, I had to give presentations in London. You’d never guess where I was from based on how I spoke.      That’s the beauty of it, isn’t it? Being a language teacher, I get to see how people adapt. It’s like a living thing—evolving, changing, and still holding on to the roots. I often find that older generations retain more traditional ways of speaking, while younger people are more likely to mix in slang or use technology-based communication.      I suppose that’s true. I still use a lot of the same phrases my father used, like “cheerio” or “top of the morning to you.” But I also know that if I tried to speak like that today, people might just laugh. Though I do find it funny how some younger people still say “y’know” or “like” a lot.      Oh, I’ve heard that one too. I always tell my students that “like” is a verb, and it’s been around a while—just like “gonna” or “wanna.” Anyway, I’ve been meaning to ask, how have your hobbies changed with age?      Honestly, they’ve slowed down a bit. I used to be into sailing and gardening, but now I just enjoy sitting out with a book and a cup of tea. I even started taking up knitting. It’s surprising how much you can do when you’re retired—especially if you’ve got time on your hands.      That’s lovely. I always thought knitting was a bit tedious, but I’ve been trying it with my kids. It’s a great way to bond and pass on skills. I bet you’re making some beautiful things.      I’m not sure about beautiful, but I can say I’ve learned to be patient. It’s a big difference from managing a business, where things move quickly. I think I’m finally learning to slow down and enjoy the process.

So, I just got back from my weekend trip with my boyfriend. We had such a good time, but honestly, I’m still not sure if this is the right path for us.      Oh no, are you breaking up? That’s so sudden. What happened?      Not exactly breaking up, but I’ve been thinking a lot about our future. He’s got a job in Manchester, and I’m still in London. I mean, we’re seeing each other, but it’s not really working out.      That’s rough. But you know what? If you’re not sure, it’s better to figure it out now rather than later. You don’t want to waste time on something that’s not right.      I know, but it’s hard. I love him, but the distance is killing me. I was thinking about going out for breakfast on Friday—maybe I’ll just go with a friend instead.      Wait, Friday? That’s Valentine’s Day, isn’t it? I thought you were going out with him.      I was, but honestly, I didn’t feel like celebrating. It felt like we were going through the motions. I just wanted to have a good time with someone else.      That makes sense. You don’t have to do anything you don’t want to. And honestly, if you're not feeling it, it’s okay to take a break.      Yeah, I guess. I just hope I don’t regret it later.      You won’t. You’re still young, and you’ve got time. Also, about movies—did you see the new one? I heard it’s amazing.      No, sorry—I was too busy thinking about things. But I might go to the cinema this weekend. Maybe with someone else.      That sounds better. And don’t worry, if you need advice, I’m always here.
