Also, I saw your accent the other day—don’t worry, it’s totally London.      Thanks! I’m not sure about mine, though. I think I’ve picked up some Midlands bits from you.      Oh, I’m so proud! You’re like my little accent experiment.      You’re the one who taught me to say “brolly” instead of “umbrella.”      Exactly! And I still say “chips” over “crisps.” I’m not sorry.      No, me neither. It’s weird, but I like it.      Good. Now, let’s go grab some food before it’s gone.

So, I just got my first major project approved — a mixed-use development in East London. It’s going to be a bit of a shot in the dark, but I’m hopeful. The council is pushing for more affordable housing, and I think this could help.      That sounds exciting, but don’t you worry about the politics? I mean, with the current government's policies on housing, it’s like trying to build a house in a storm.      It’s not easy, but I think we’re in a better place than before. Although, I still can’t believe how many people are being priced out of London. I mean, even my parents can’t afford to move back to Watford anymore.      Yeah, I know what you mean. My cousin who lived in Nottingham moved to Manchester just to save money. But even there, rent is going up like crazy. I think it’s all about capitalism — everyone wants a cut, but no one’s willing to share.      Exactly. And it’s not just about money. There’s a real sense of alienation in the city. I mean, we’re not even in the same class anymore. You’ve got people like me, working in the creative industries, and then people like you — freelancing, trying to make ends meet.      True. I’ve had some really tough times, but I’ve also seen the upside. Being a freelance journalist gives me a lot of freedom, but it also means I’m constantly juggling projects and clients. Sometimes I wish I had a more stable job, like a proper office and a predictable income.      I can relate. I have a pretty stable job, but the pressure is still there. And then there’s the whole politics angle. I think part of the problem is the government’s handle on things — it’s like they’re not even trying to fix the system.      I agree. And on the racism front, it’s getting worse. I’ve seen way too many stories about discrimination in housing and employment. It’s sad to see how people from different backgrounds are treated.      It’s really frustrating. I think we need more community support and better policies. Maybe we can go back to my place later, and I’ll show you my drawings for the project.      That sounds good. I’d love to see what you’ve got planned.

So, I've been thinking about the nursery again, and I’m just so nervous about starting it. I mean, I know it’s the right thing to do, but I can’t help but wonder if we’re doing everything right.      I get that—it’s totally normal to feel that way. I remember when I started thinking about nursery for my little brother, I was completely overwhelmed. But honestly, once you get past the initial nerves, it’s actually easier than you think.      Thanks, I needed to hear that. But, I’m also trying to figure out when to go back to work. I don’t want to miss out on too much with the baby, but I also need to get back on my feet financially.      That’s such a tough call. I’ve been there too. I had to make the same decision with my first job. I think the key is to look at what you can manage without stress. Maybe you could start part-time, or even do remote work from home for a few days a week?      That’s a good idea. I’ve been talking to a few people about it. I’m also starting to think about holidays—when we can actually take a break from the baby. I remember how much fun we had when I was your age, just hanging out with friends or going on trips.      You're not wrong—time flies. I’m already looking forward to that first big holiday. Maybe we can plan a trip to the coast? I’ve always wanted to go to the Yorkshire coast. Or maybe even a weekend in London?      That sounds perfect. I’ve been thinking about the same things. Oh, and I’ve been trying to get used to the baby weening. It’s so hard, but I’m trying not to take it too personally.      I know, it’s so emotional. But I think it’s a sign that the baby is starting to adjust, and we’re starting to get some peace. It’s not easy, but it’s also a necessary part of growing up.      Yeah, I suppose you’re right. It’s like a new chapter. I go through all these emotions, but I keep reminding myself how far we’ve come.      That’s exactly it. And I’m here for you every step of the way.

Well, I think that’s the last thing we’ll be discussing tonight. We’ve got more important matters to talk about. Did you hear about the incident at the shop last night?      I heard something about it. They said it was a robbery, but I’m not sure if it’s true. I tried to call the police, but they were too busy. I should probably give a statement if they ask.      Wait, you were there? What exactly happened?      Yeah, I was working late. Someone came in, smashed the glass door, and grabbed a few items. It was pretty scary. I didn’t get a good look at the person, but the security camera might have caught them.      That’s a relief. At least there’s footage. I’m just worried about what the police will ask. Should I be prepared?      They’ll probably want to know what you saw, what you heard, and if you noticed anything unusual. You might want to write down the details and keep them safe.      Yeah, I’d do that too. I remember my cousin had a similar situation at the café, and they really wanted the details. It’s important to be clear and calm when you talk to them.      I just got an email about the EE phone bill. It’s way over the limit. I’m not sure how that happened. Did you get a similar bill, Speaker_2?      I did. I think it’s because of some automatic renewal for a service I no longer use. I should call them and cancel it. But it’s late, and I don’t want to deal with it tonight.      You could leave it for tomorrow. But don’t forget about it. Those bills can add up quickly. I’ve had to deal with that before. Let me know if you need help sorting it out.      Speaking of things to do, what are the plans for the week? I need to figure out my schedule for next week. I’ve got some shifts coming up, and I need to make sure I’m not overbooked.      I’ve got a meeting with the team on Monday. I was thinking of taking a short break, maybe a weekend trip. We could all go together. It’s been a while since we’ve done anything like that.      That sounds like a good idea. I’d like to get out of the house for a bit.

So, I heard you mentioned Spartacus the other day. Are you a fan of the TV show? I mean, the one with the gladiators and all?      Oh, yeah! I totally am. Though honestly, I think the original one with the Roman history stuff was way better. I mean, it’s not just about the fights—it’s about the politics and the rebellion. You ever watch that?      I did! I mean, I didn’t think it was that interesting at first. But then I got into the backstory of the people in Rome. Like, how the slaves were treated, and how much power the patricians had over the plebeians. It was pretty eye-opening.      Definitely! I remember one episode where they showed the early deaths of the main characters. It was so sad. Like, how quickly things can change in Roman society. You ever think about how much of that history is just stories passed down?      Yeah, I guess that’s part of why I love the TV show. It makes all that ancient history feel real. Though I still can’t wrap my head around how people back then could survive with so little food. I mean, today we’ve got bread, chickpeas, nuts, and all sorts of spices. Back then?      Right? I mean, even now, we’re still using some of those same spices and herbs. You know what I found interesting? I was in a market in Cyprus last week and saw a mortar and pestle. It was like they still use it for grinding spices—just like the Romans did.      That’s wild. I had a mortar and pestle at home, actually. My mum always used it for making sauces. It’s kind of a nostalgia thing. Maybe I should start using it again. I’ve been thinking about making some homemade bread lately. My sister’s got this bread machine, but I’d rather make it with a real oven.      You should! I mean, it’s way better for your health. Plus, the smell of fresh bread in the morning is something else. I’ve been trying a new recipe with chickpeas and herbs. My granddad used to make it with a mortar and pestle. He said it’s the best way to get the flavors out.      That’s cool. I might have to try that. You know what else I’m into these days? Musicians.

Hey, have you seen the new music teacher at school? I heard she's the one who started the wind-band.      No, I haven’t. Is she good? I mean, we’ve had a few teachers, and some of them were pretty terrible.      She’s actually really good. I think she’s from London, but she’s been at the school for a few months now. She’s got this amazing way of making even the most basic instruments sound amazing.      That sounds cool. I want to join the band. I’ve been practicing the flute at home. I’m pretty decent, I think.      You should totally try out. I’m still waiting to hear back about the audition, but I’m nervous. I’m not sure I’m good enough.      You’re definitely good enough. You’ve been working so hard. Plus, I heard the band is going to perform at the school fair next month. It’s going to be awesome.      Yeah, I hope so. Oh, and I’m still really nervous about the English test. I think it’s going to be on Friday.      Same. I’ve been studying so much, but I’m still not sure I’ve got everything down. I was thinking maybe we should study together?      That sounds like a good idea. I mean, if you’re not too busy with the band practice.      No, I’m free this afternoon. We could meet at the library. I’ve got some notes I can share, and maybe we can quiz each other.      Perfect. Oh, and I almost forgot—did you hear about the art lessons? They’re starting to do a new project about famous British artists.      Oh, that’s cool. I love art. I think I’m going to do something with the paintings of Turner. I’ve always liked the way he uses light.      That’s a great choice. I think I’m going to do something with Picasso. Even though he’s not British, I like how he mixes different styles.      That’s a good one too. I just hope the teacher doesn’t get too strict with us.      I hope so too. Speaking of teachers, have you been to any of the French lessons lately?      Yeah, I did last week. It was pretty hard, but the teacher’s pretty patient. I think I’m starting to get the hang of it.

So, I've been meaning to ask you, have you seen the new café down by the station? It’s got a great vibe, and the coffee isn’t half bad. I was thinking we might grab a bite there next week.      Actually, I went there last weekend with my mates. The food was decent, but the service was a bit slow. I had the fish and chips, and it was pretty good—though the portion was a bit small for the price.      I'm not sure I'd pay that much for fish and chips. I mean, I like to eat it, but I also like to save money. I've been trying to cut back on my spending lately. Just trying to make ends meet.      I hear you. I’ve been doing the same. It’s tough being in the lower managerial bracket, you know. You’re still expected to have a bit of disposable income, but in reality, it’s not there.      Yeah, I know. I’m still in school, but even here, there are some costs. My mum helps out with some stuff, but it’s not like I can afford everything.      It’s funny, isn’t it? I used to be a teacher, and I always told my students that education was an investment. But now, I don’t even have enough for my own basic needs.      That’s a shame. I remember when I was teaching, I always made sure to save a bit each month. Even if it was just a few pounds, it helped. Now I’m trying to make sure I don’t fall into the same hole.      I can relate. I’ve been saving a little bit from my part-time job at the library. It’s not a lot, but it’s something. I’m hoping that when I finish school, I can get a better job.      That’s the spirit. I tried to get back into teaching a few years ago, but it was hard to find work. I ended up quitting and just living off what I had. It took a while to get back on my feet.      I go through the same thing sometimes. It’s not easy, but I try to stay positive. I think it’s important to have goals, even if they’re small.      I agree. I’ve been thinking about doing some kind of apprenticeship or something to get into a better job.

So, I was telling my dad earlier that I think my kids are more like me than my husband. But he said, “That’s not possible! You’re both lecturers!”      I bet he says that every time. He’s got that “I know everything” look. But honestly, I think it’s about genes more than anything. My mum always said I had her nose and your dad had his stubbornness.      I can tell you that. My sister’s got the same stubbornness as my dad. I swear, she’s just a little version of him. And the nose? Oh, that’s from me. But honestly, I think it’s all luck. Some people are just born with the right look.      I think it’s more about how you carry it. My husband’s taller than I am, but he’s got the same awkwardness I do when I try to be the centre of attention.      That’s true. I still can’t get over how tall he is. I mean, we’re both in the same size clothes, but he looks like he’s in a different universe.      Yeah, but it’s not just about looks. I think the way you act is more telling. My parents are both very strong-willed, and I’m just like them. Though I’d say I’m more like my mother in that way.      I think it’s about the upbringing. My kids are starting to show their personalities, and I can see bits of me and my husband in them. My youngest even does that “I’m not listening” thing my husband used to do.      Speaking of which, have you heard about the new gym opening in Norwich? I thought I’d try it, but I’m not sure if I’m ready to go.      I tried that once. Got halfway through my first session and realized I couldn’t lift anything. I think I scared the instructor.      I would’ve run out. I’m not into that kind of thing. I think I’d rather do jigsaws. There’s no pressure in a jigsaw.      Yeah, but jigsaws take time. I’ve been trying to do one for hours, and I still haven’t finished. I think it’s a metaphor for life, really.      I think we’re all just stuck in our own versions of the jigsaw. It’s not about finishing fast, it’s about enjoying the process.

So, I've been trying to get Moodle to work properly for the new module I'm running. It’s got to be the most frustrating thing I’ve ever dealt with. I thought it would be straightforward since I've used it before, but now it's like it's designed to confuse me.      I can understand that. I had the same problems last week when I tried to set up a new course. Moodle can be a bit of a headache, especially if you're not used to its interface. But once you figure it out, it's pretty powerful.      Yeah, but I keep getting these errors when I try to upload the files. I don’t know if it’s the file format, the server settings, or something else. It’s like there’s a hidden layer of complexity I’m not seeing.      That’s probably the problem. Moodle can be really picky about things like file types, permissions, and even the order in which you upload content. I remember spending hours trying to get a video to load, only to realize I had the wrong format.      Oh no, I’ve been doing that too. I thought I had everything set up properly, but then the system just gives me a generic error message. It’s like it doesn’t want to tell me what’s wrong.      It’s not that it doesn’t want to tell you—it’s just that it’s not very user-friendly in that way. I found a forum thread that helped me out a bit, though. They mentioned checking the file extensions and making sure they’re compatible with the system.      Oh, I should have done that. I was so focused on the content itself that I didn’t think about the technical side. I guess part of the challenge is knowing which parts to troubleshoot.      Exactly. It’s like teaching—it’s not just about the material, but also about the tools you use to deliver it. Sometimes, the tools are just as important as the content itself.      Well, I suppose I’ll have to keep experimenting. If I can just get the files to upload without errors, I can start building the course structure. I really want this module to run smoothly, especially since it’s a new one.      You’ll get there. I remember when I first started using Moodle—I was so confused, but now I can’t imagine teaching without it.

So, I just got home from the airport, and I am still trying to adjust. Jetlag is a real pain. I swear, I was up at 3 a.m. and now I’m exhausted, but it’s 9 p.m. and I can’t sleep.      You poor thing. I remember how it felt when I first started traveling for work. It’s like your body is fighting you all the time. How long were you abroad?      Three days in Barcelona. We had to meet with a colleague for a research conference, and the whole time I was just trying to keep up with the time difference. I kept telling myself it’s only a few days, and now I’m home, and I’m still not fully back on track.      I feel you. I was just in Manchester for a conference last week, and I’ve been trying to get back into the rhythm of things. Speaking of rhythms, I saw a dramatic performance last night. It was amazing, actually. You’d love it—very emotional, full of suspense.      Oh, I’d love to go. But with the jetlag, I’m worried I’ll fall asleep halfway through. I mean, I’ve got a baby on the way, and I’m already feeling the strain of being a new parent. I barely have time to breathe, let alone go to a play.      I understand completely. When I had my first child, I was just surviving. But now that I’ve had my second, I’ve learned to make time for things that make me happy. You shouldn’t let the baby’s schedule take over everything. We should plan something soon—maybe next weekend?      That sounds good. We can check out the local theatre. I’ll ask Sarah if she’s available. She’s been wanting to see something new. And if I’m still up at 3 a.m., I’ll probably be up at 6 a.m. anyway. It’s all part of the package, I suppose.      Exactly. Life with a baby is a balancing act, but it’s worth it. You’ll have so many memories. And trust me, a play will be the perfect way to unwind. Just go easy on yourself, okay?      I will. Thanks for the reminder. I need to remember that I’m not alone in this. It’s tough, but it’s also special.      Always. And don’t forget, I’m right here.

So, I've been meaning to ask you, how do you manage to keep in touch with so many friends across the world? I mean, I’m more of a local kind of guy, stuck in Liverpool and all that. Not that I don’t like it—actually, I do—but it’s hard to keep up with everyone, especially with the visa stuff and all that.      It’s not that hard if you have the right connections. I mean, I've had to move around quite a bit myself. Between my work as an interpreter and translator, I’ve been in the UK for over a decade now. It’s not just about speaking the language, it's about knowing the right people and understanding the nuances of the culture. Plus, living in a multicultural environment like the UK makes it easier to maintain relationships.      That’s true. But I still find it difficult when it comes to getting a visa. I’ve been trying to visit my cousin in Berlin, and the process has been so bureaucratic. I mean, do you think the political climate has made it harder for people like us?      Oh, definitely. The politics of oil and the way different countries handle visas have changed a lot over the years. Take Libya, for example. Ten years ago, it was much easier to move around. But now, with all the instability and the influence of groups like the Wahabi, things are more complicated. It’s not just about the countries you come from, it’s also about what someone believes in.      That’s a bit scary, honestly. I mean, I’d never have thought the religion would play such a big role in where you can live or travel. It feels like everything is connected now—politics, migration, religion. It’s a bit overwhelming.      I know what you mean. But it’s also a reflection of the times. Young people today are more aware of these issues than ever before. They’re more open to different cultures, but also more cautious. I’ve seen it in my work. People are more selective about who they trust and where they go.      I guess that’s why I’ve been thinking about moving house. I’m in a bit of a rut, you know? I go to lectures on English literature, but I’d love to be in a place where I can explore more.

So, I just got the last of the lamb out of the oven—it’s just about perfect. The skin’s got that nice, crisp crackle, and the meat is still juicy inside.      That looks amazing. I’ve been craving roast lamb all week. I wonder if it’s worth the effort, though? I mean, with the way the weather’s been, I’ve been thinking more about indoor activities.      Oh, don’t be daft, George. You know as well as I do that the best thing about winter is roast lamb, and the worst is the cold. Besides, this is Scotland, not some tropical island. You’re lucky to have a fire burning at all.      True, but I think it’s the combination of the lamb and the TV in the dining room that makes it all the more worth it. I was about to switch it on. I’ve been watching this documentary about the history of the Scottish tablet—how it’s been around for centuries, even before the Romans came.      A Scottish tablet? I thought that was a thing from the Highlands. I’ve heard stories about those big, heavy stone tablets used by the clans for records. It’s fascinating, honestly. I remember reading about it in one of those history books I picked up at the library.      Oh, you’re talking about the  clachan ? Yes, they were used for marking territory and even for writing in the old Scottish script. But I think the tablet you’re referring to is more of a modern invention. You know, the ones people use for skimming through emails and news.      Oh, you mean the tablet with the screen? I thought you were talking about the stone. I’ve been meaning to get one of those for work. It would make transcribing so much easier, especially when I have to work late.      I can see why. I’ve been thinking about going on a cruise for my birthday next year. I’ve always wanted to see the world, but the idea of being stuck on a ship for a week with a bunch of strangers sounds both exciting and terrifying.      That’s a great idea. I’ve been on a few cruises myself. You get to see different parts of the world, and the food is usually excellent. But I’ll warn you—once you start, you can’t stop.

You know, I’ve been thinking about the whole house situation again. I mean, we’re all living together, but is it even legal? I mean, sure, we’re friends, but we’re not exactly family. What if someone gets sick or something?      Oh, come on, we’ve been through this before. It’s not like we’re living in a council flat or anything. We just split the bills and keep the place clean. Besides, it’s not like we’re doing anything illegal. We’re just, you know, being responsible adults.      I get where you’re coming from, Rob. It’s just that sometimes I feel like we’re all just passing the buck. I mean, I’m not even sure what my parents think about this. I told them I was staying with a friend, but they’re asking when I’m going to “get a proper job” or something.      Yeah, I hear that a lot. My mum’s always like, “You’re not a student forever.” But I’m not even in a proper job. I’m just a TA for now. I’m trying to get into a master’s program, but it’s not easy. I mean, I’m not even sure I can afford it.      Mate, you’re not the only one. I’ve got a degree, and I still can’t find work. I just end up binge-watching shows on Netflix and eating takeaway every night. I’m not even sure what I want to do anymore. I mean, I used to think I’d be doing something more meaningful, like working with kids or something.      I know, I know. Life doesn’t work out the way we plan. But we’re still here, right? And we’re still supporting each other. That’s what matters. I mean, I’m not even sure if I’ll be able to afford my own flat when I finish uni. We’re all in the same boat, in a way.      Yeah, I guess that’s the thing. We all came from different places, but we’re stuck here in this flat, trying to make it work. I mean, I’m from Germany, but I still feel like I don’t belong here sometimes. I can’t even speak the language properly, even though I’ve been here for almost two years.      You’re not the only one.

Okay, so I’ve got this baking lesson coming up for the kids, and I need to plan something that’s engaging and educational. I was thinking maybe we could make cupcakes with a fun twist. What do you think?      Cupcakes! That sounds like a great idea. I love cupcakes. But wait, does the lesson have to be about baking, or can we do something else?      Well, the lesson is about baking, but it’s also a half birthday celebration for Mum. So we’re combining the two. We can make cupcakes and then have a little party with the kids.      Can I help decorate the cupcakes? I can do the sprinkles and the icing!      Absolutely! You’ll be the decorator extraordinaire. But first, I need to make sure the recipe is right. I was thinking of using a frosting that doesn’t need to be refrigerated, so it’s easier to handle in the classroom.      What’s the recipe again? I might help you measure the ingredients.      It’s a basic cupcake mix with some vanilla extract. We’ll add a little lemon zest for flavor. Oh, and I found a book in Morrisons about baking with kids. It’s got all the tips and tricks for making it fun.      Cool! I like books. Do you think we can read the book together while we make the cupcakes?      That sounds like a good idea. It’ll keep the kids entertained and educated at the same time. Also, I was thinking about telling a joke during the lesson to keep things light. Do you have any good ones?      I know one about a tomato and a potato. The tomato asked the potato, “Do you know why I’m red?” And the potato said, “Because you’re a  mash !”      That’s a classic! I’ll add that to the lesson. It’s always good to have a few jokes up your sleeve.      I know another one! Why don’t skeletons fight each other? Because they don’t have the  guts !      Oh, go on! You’re getting better at this. That was great! I think the kids are going to love this. We’re going to make sure the lesson is both educational and fun. Let’s get started on the cupcakes!      I’ll mix the batter. You can put the cupcakes in the oven.      Perfect. And I’ll be over here helping the kids with the frosting.

So, I was just on Facebook the other day, and I saw this post about electric cars. It’s got to be the most ridiculous thing I’ve ever seen. I mean, sure, they’re good for the environment, but honestly, they’re not practical for people like us. You can’t just drive one around the countryside without charging it every few miles.      I agree, but I think that’s just because we’re not used to them yet. I mean, think about how quickly the tech is advancing. My brother just bought a hybrid, and he says it’s way better than his old diesel. It’s quiet, efficient, and he doesn’t get fined for idling anymore.      Yeah, I get that, but I still think the charging infrastructure is a mess. I tried to find a charging point the other week, and it was like looking for a needle in a haystack. I ended up using a petrol station just to get a bit of juice in the car. It’s not worth the hassle.      True, but I think it’s going to get better. I read somewhere that the government is investing a lot in expanding the network. Plus, the cost of electricity is way cheaper than petrol. If you’re driving a lot, it actually saves money in the long run. Plus, the tax incentives are pretty sweet.      I suppose, but I still feel like the transition is too fast. I don’t know if I can trust the technology. I mean, my dad’s got a diesel, and it’s been running fine for years. I don’t want to be stuck with a car that breaks down because it’s not properly maintained.      Fair point. But the thing is, the cars today are way more reliable than they used to be. I know that sounds like an old man’s mantra, but I’ve seen the stats. The average lifespan of a car is increasing every year. And with all the software updates they’re pushing out, it’s like they’re constantly improving them.      Hmm, maybe you’re right. I guess I just need to give it a bit more thought. But I do have to say, I’d be really nervous about switching. I like the idea of not having to worry about running out of fuel in the middle of nowhere.

So, I've been working my arse off all week. I had to do a load of stock shifts at the shop, and then there was this presentation for my course. I've been so tired, I've barely had time to eat properly.      Yup, I can’t even imagine. I’ve been stuck in lectures all week too. But at least I’ve got this film on. It’s  Cloudy With a Chance of Meatballs , right? I think it’s one of those ones where the whole town is covered in food. Didn’t you want to watch it with me?      Yeah, I did. I was going to, but then work got in the way. My manager was being a right pain. I think I’ve got a bit of a problem with my appetite these days. I just don’t feel like eating anything. Maybe it’s the stress.      Have you tried eating something healthy? I mean, don’t get me wrong, I love junk food, but I’ve been trying to eat more veggies lately. I mean, it’s not like we’re in a place where food is scarce, is it? We’re in Warwickshire, not somewhere like... well, I don’t know, a famine zone or something.      Haha, I know, but sometimes it just feels like everything’s too much. You know, work, studies, and trying to figure out how to operate this stupid TV remote. I’ve been trying to change the channel for the last 20 minutes, and it’s like the remote’s made of sabotage.      Oh, I know that feeling! I’ve spent ages trying to get the settings right. I think the remote’s from the 90s. But hey, what’s the point of having a smart TV if you can’t figure out how to use it? My sister tried to explain it to me once, and I just said, “Just press the button that says ‘Play’.”      Exactly! I think I need a break. Maybe we should talk about something else. Like... how has the way we communicate changed over the years? I feel like everyone’s always on their phones now, and it’s like the real conversation is missing.      Yeah, I feel that too. I mean, I’m still figuring out how to have a real conversation with my friends. Sometimes, we just text each other and never really talk properly.

So, I've been meaning to ask you, how do you feel about the current state of politics in the UK? I mean, with all the changes over the years, it's hard to say what's really working.      Well, as a Liverpool lad, I've seen my fair share of political shifts. I remember the New Labour days under Tony Blair. It was all about making things better for everyone, right? But now, it feels like the country's going in circles. It's like someone's got a compass that's broken.      You're not wrong. I think the key is that people want change, but no one seems to know exactly what they want. It's like everyone's shouting, but no one's listening. Speaking of which, do you still follow football like you used to?      Oh, I still do, but not as much as I used to. I used to watch every match with my mates in the café. Now, it's more of a background thing. But when the Liverpool team does well, it brings the whole place to life, you know?      That's true. Football has this way of uniting people, even in times of political division. I've always thought of it as a way to bridge gaps – even though I'm a lecturer, and you're a taxi driver, we both still have that shared love for the game.      Exactly! I think that's why it's so powerful. When the team plays well, you can forget about the political mess for a while. It's like the world stops and everyone just enjoys the moment.      That’s the beauty of sport, isn’t it? It's not just about the game; it's about the culture and the community. I mean, I was born in Salzkotten, Germany, but I've lived in England for most of my life. Sometimes I can't help but feel that the political climate here is a bit too divisive, especially when it comes to things like immigration or national identity.      I hear you. But I also think people are starting to realize that we're all in this together. I mean, you don't have to be British or German to care about the country's future. It's about what's best for the people, not just the politicians.      You might be right. I think we’re at a crossroads, and it's up to us to decide which direction we take.

So, I've been listening to these BNC recordings again. I know it's supposed to be British National Corpus, right? Anyway, it's like, completely different from how people actually speak now. I mean, it's so formal and stuff, like, what even is that?      Honestly, I feel the same. I was just on LinkedIn the other day and saw this post from a linguist saying that the BNC is outdated. I mean, it's from the 90s or something. We've evolved, haven't we? Didn’t even know the BNC was that old.      Oh, I think it’s from the late 90s to early 2000s. I remember reading somewhere that it includes written and spoken English from across the UK, but it's not really reflective of the way we communicate today, especially with social media and all that. I feel like we use so many more slang terms and emojis now.      Exactly! And don’t even get me started on how people use abbreviations like “LOL” and “brb.” It's like a whole different language. I mean, I've tried to use some of that in my work, but my editor friend – I think she’s got a name tag or something?      Hey, that’s me! Anna. You two are talking about me? I’m the one who told you to never use “brb” in a professional context. You’re both still using it. And you know what? It’s not professional. It’s lazy.      You’re right. I’ve been trying to cut it out, but it slips in so often. I think I need to start using more proper language, like “be right back” or “I’ll be back shortly.” It’s so hard, though, when you’re used to texting like that.      And don’t even get me started on flying. I’m still scared of it. I’ve never gone abroad, but I’ve always wanted to visit the Maldives. I mean, the water is so blue, and the whales are big and beautiful. I keep telling myself I’ll go, but I can’t even get on a plane.      You know what’s weird? I’ve been to Spain a few times, and I don’t even have a fear of flying. Maybe it’s because I’ve been on flights so much. Oh, and I had a pug last year. You should’ve seen it.

So, I’ve been thinking about getting a tattoo. Not sure yet—what do you think, Jo?      Oh, you’ve been wanting one? I thought you were still in the “no permanent markings” phase. What’s it gonna be?      Yeah, I’ve been delaying it for ages, but with the summer coming, I figured I’d finally do something for myself. Maybe a small one—something meaningful. Maybe a symbol or something from my grandparents’ old house?      That sounds nice. You know, I’ve been thinking about getting a small one too. Maybe something related to my late father. My mom keeps saying I should do it before I’m too old. But I’m not sure.      I get it. It’s a big decision, but once you do it, you can’t really take it back. Maybe you should get a small one first, you know, to test the waters.      Yeah, I guess. It’s just that I’ve been so busy with work and the house renovation that I haven’t had time to think about it. Speaking of which, did you hear about the new intern we got?      Yeah, she’s amazing. Very eager and organized. I think she’s gonna be a great help with the renovation. But did you know the whole house is getting a complete redo? I mean, we’re turning it into a proper home.      Yeah, it’s going to be a massive transformation. I still can’t believe we’re doing it. But it’s going to be worth it in the long run. I was just talking to my sister about it earlier. She said she’s excited to see it all come together.      Speaking of which, have you thought about Christmas plans? I know we’ve been meaning to do something special this year.      I was actually thinking about that. My brother is coming down from Manchester, and I was hoping we could have a small gathering at the house. Maybe even get a tree. It’d be nice to have some real Christmas spirit again.      That sounds great. I’d like that. Maybe we can go out for dinner before the big day. I’ve been meaning to try that new restaurant in Shoreditch. I heard their Christmas menu is amazing.      I’d love that. Let me check the menu online. Oh, and I think we should send a card to my parents.

So, I just got this really cute pair of denim jeans from that online store. You know, the ones with the subtle distressing? I’ve been dying to try them out, but I’m worried they might not be comfortable for the yoga class I have tomorrow.      Oh, I get it—denim can be stiff at first, but once you break them in, they’re great for movement. I actually wore mine to a Pilates class last week, and they were perfect. Plus, they’re so versatile. You can pair them with a sweater or a t-shirt depending on the weather.      That does sound good. I love how they can easily transition from day to night. But I’m also thinking about food tonight. The weather’s been so damp, and I’m craving something hearty. Do you feel like making a slow-cooked stew?      Absolutely! I’ve been wanting to try that new recipe I saw online for a creamy leek and potato stew. It’s supposed to be really comforting. I could even use some of those herbs from the garden we planted last summer.      That sounds amazing. I’ve been meaning to start a herb garden too. I’ve got a few basil and thyme plants in pots on the window sill. I just need to figure out how to care for them properly.      Oh, don’t worry—basil and thyme are pretty low maintenance. Just make sure they get enough sunlight and water them when the soil feels dry. I read somewhere that they actually thrive when you occasionally let them go a bit thirsty.      Interesting. I’ll give that a shot. Speaking of plants, did you hear about the trip to Spain we were talking about last month? I’m really excited to visit Seville and try that famous tapas culture.      I know! I’ve been researching the best spots to eat in Seville. I think I found a great little tapas bar near the cathedral. Oh, and I’ve been saving up for a quick trip to Barcelona too—maybe next summer.      That sounds like a plan. I’ve been thinking about going to Barcelona for a solo trip. Just to get some time to myself and go to the beach. Maybe I’ll even take some language classes there—there are a few schools that offer Spanish courses in the city.      That could be really beneficial.

So, I was just thinking about our old university mates. Remember when we used to meet up every Friday for drinks and just chat? It’s funny how time flies.      Absolutely, I still remember that. I think the highlight was when we all agreed to meet at the student bar and then ended up getting kicked out for arguing about the best theory of history.      Oh, right, that one! We were all so passionate. And you were the one who got us all into debating whether the Industrial Revolution was a good or bad thing.      I still think it was mostly bad, but I’ll give you that we had some good laughs. It’s just weird how some of those people have completely fallen off the radar. I mean, some of them are still in academia, and others have gone into completely different fields.      Yeah, it’s funny how life takes people in different directions. I’ve been thinking about reaching out to a few of them to see if they’d like to meet up again. It would be nice to catch up and exchange some ideas.      That sounds like a great idea. I’ve been meaning to get in touch with a few people too. I was just thinking about that last week – how we all got so caught up in our work and started losing touch.      I know, it’s such a shame. I’ve also been meaning to email some old friends. I think one of them is in London now, and they’ve been doing some interesting work with community projects.      That’s cool. I actually had a colleague mention something about a similar initiative. I should check with them about it.      You know what’s even more annoying? I was trying to take care of my toe nails last night and got them all messed up. I’ve been meaning to go to the nail salon, but I keep putting it off.      Oh no, you poor thing! I told you about my toe nails last week. They’ve been getting worse by the day. I think I’m going to have to schedule an appointment soon.      I told you! You go first. I’ll wait for you. If I go first, I’ll just end up making a mess of everything.      Exactly. It’s all about planning ahead. I’ve been meaning to do it for weeks now, but I’m always too busy grading papers or preparing for lectures.

So, I heard you mentioned you're going to be in Birmingham for the weekend. How’s work been lately? You’re a company director now—how’s that going?      It's been pretty intense, honestly. I’ve been managing a few new projects, and the pressure’s high. But it’s rewarding, you know? I mean, I enjoy the challenge. How about you? Still teaching languages?      Yeah, I’m still teaching, but I’ve started doing some workshops for adults. It’s different from the usual school stuff. I get to work with people who are really passionate about languages, even if they’re not students. It’s refreshing.      That sounds interesting. I’ve always admired how you make languages feel like a journey rather than just a subject. Speaking of journeys, I’ve been thinking about traveling. Maybe take a trip to the Lake District or something. I’ve been wanting to get out of the city for a while.      That sounds perfect. I’ve been to the Lake District once, and it’s absolutely beautiful. You should definitely go. I heard there’s some great hiking trails and a really welcoming community. Oh, and did you catch the new film on Netflix?      No, I haven’t. I’m still catching up on some older movies. I’ve been trying to catch up on some classic British films—there’s something about them that just feels nostalgic.      I agree. I think there’s a reason so many of our films are so popular internationally. They have that unique storytelling and cultural depth. Speaking of culture, I’ve been hearing a lot about conspiracy theories lately. Some of them are about climate change, and I’ve started to wonder—are we overreacting or is there a kernel of truth in some of them?      That’s a tough one. I think some of the theories are just sensationalism, but others have some merit. I remember reading about a few that mentioned how certain industries might have a stake in keeping people in the dark. It’s strange how much information can be hidden.      Yeah, it’s a bit unsettling. But I also think people should be informed. I mean, if you’re going to believe in anything, it should be based on facts, not just rumors. Speaking of beliefs, have you ever thought about getting married again?      Honestly, I’ve been thinking about it more lately.

Dad, can we stop at that little village ahead? I saw a red and white caravan with a big sign saying “Jamaica Inn.” I’ve read that book a million times! It’s got all those creepy woods and the haunted inn—  like   the Wizard of Oz but way darker!      Oh, you’re still into that? I remember when you were six and would sit in the garden, pretending you were the witch from   Alice in Wonderland  . You’d run around with a stick, yelling, “Off with their heads!”      Yeah, but I  was  into Alice and Sherlock Holmes too! I still have that old book with the   Morse code   on the back cover. I used to try to send messages to my mates in school using it.      I still have that old radio from when I was a kid. It’s broken, but I remember how we used to send telegrams. You could send a few words for a pound! I even sent one once—”Have a good time, Dad”—but it turned into “Have a grief time, Dad” because of the   braille   machine messing up the code.      That’s not funny! Wait, are we near the   wind turbines  ? I saw one on the side of the road. They’re so big! Like giant butterflies trying to fly.      Yeah, they’re everywhere around here. Some people think they ruin the   scenery  , but I like how they make the wind spin. You know, it’s about   clean energy   now.      Oh! There’s a   beach   up ahead! I can’t wait to run in the sand and find a   seashell  ! Dad, can we stop here? I want to take a picture of the   flowers   by the sea.      Alright, but we’ll have to check the fuel first. I don’t want to run out in the middle of nowhere. You know how those   houses   are built along the coast—narrow and windy.      Yeah, but the   chocolate   shop in the village will be worth it! I’m telling you, the   text   on the sign said “Best chocolate in the county.” I’ll take a piece to share with the   birds   over there.      You’ve got a wild imagination. But I love it. You remind me of my own   fairy tales   from when I was your age.      You were the one who told me about the   telegraph   and how it used to send messages across the world.

So, I've been thinking about our trip to the seaside. I was just reading about that guy who swam the Channel, you know, the one from the 1920s? He was mad, wasn’t he? I mean, I’d rather just go to Blackpool and get a good fish and chips than try to swim across the English Channel.      Aye, I’ve heard about that. He was one of those pioneers, I suppose. But you know, back in the day, people didn’t have the same excuses as now. You don’t even need a wetsuit to swim across the Channel these days, do you? Though I wouldn’t try it for the world.      It’s not just the Channel, though. I’ve heard about people swimming from the Isle of Wight to the mainland. I think it was about 20 miles. I’d probably collapse before I even got half way.      You’re not wrong, mate. I’d be so out of my depth, I’d probably end up getting stuck in a current or something. Though I have to say, I’ve always been a bit obsessed with the idea of doing it. Maybe when I’m 50, I’ll try.      Aye, I’d say 50’s a bit young. You’ve got to be in good shape and have a bit of experience. I’ve heard that the biggest danger isn’t the water — it’s the sharks.      Yeah, I think the sharks are a real concern. But then again, the politicians are the ones who should be worried about the water quality. I mean, I don’t know about you, but I can’t even taste the water from my local tap without filtering it.      That’s true. I’ve heard that some areas of the UK have worse water than others. I think it’s something to do with the geography. I was just thinking about the primary school trip we did to the local reservoir. We had to wear those silly yellow raincoats and everything.      Aye, I remember that. My teacher took us to the reservoir too, but we had to walk all the way there on the mud. It was a proper adventure.      And I bet you were all excited about it, weren’t you? I mean, I can’t even remember the last time I went to a reservoir. I think I’m more of a cinema person.

So, I've been thinking about our old house in Enfield. You know, the one with that weird weaver fish decoration in the living room. It was a bit of a conversation starter, but I can't help but miss it. Did you ever think we'd be living in Bedford now?      Oh, I remember that weaver fish! It was definitely a talking point at family gatherings. I think it was your grandfather's idea—something about it being a reminder of the sea, or maybe just a quirky decoration. Anyway, I've been compiling a list of things we need to move from the old house. It's mostly furniture, but I also need to include some sentimental items.      Yeah, I was going to mention that. I've been going through the old photos and memories, and it's been a bit emotional. I mean, thinking back, we’ve been through so much. When you and I first moved in together, I was in my early twenties, and you were in your fifties. I can’t believe we've been together for that long.      Time flies, doesn’t it? You know, I’ve been feeling a bit of jet lag since I returned from my trip to Japan last week. I was in Tokyo for a conference, and the time difference really got to me. I think it's making me a bit forgetful. Have you noticed that? Sometimes I misplace things or forget names.      A bit, actually. I've been dealing with my own kind of jet lag lately too. I went to Barcelona for a language workshop, and it took me a couple of days to adjust. I even had a funny moment at the airport where I thought the flight was to Madrid instead of Barcelona. But I'm over it now.      That's barely a week ago. You're going to be the one telling  me  about jet lag soon. Anyway, I was thinking about marriage. We've been together for over twenty years, and it's still amazing. I think we should plan a little celebration to mark the occasion. Maybe a dinner at our favorite restaurant?      That sounds like a great idea. We should set a date. I've been meaning to cook that Italian dish you love, but I keep getting distracted by other things. Let's make it a weekend thing, okay?

So, I was just thinking about that garden we've been trying to tackle. I mean, the plants are growing like weeds now, but I still can't get the roses to bloom properly. I keep wondering if it's the soil or the lack of sun.      Yeah, I remember the one you tried planting last summer. It looked like it was going to be a miracle, but then it just... withered. Still, I guess that’s part of the learning curve. You can’t just expect a garden to be perfect overnight, especially with the weather being as unpredictable as it is.      I guess that's true. It's like trying to figure out how to style my hair without looking like a hot mess. I mean, I've been experimenting with different cuts, but every time I try something new, it ends up looking worse than before. I feel like I need a personal stylist, or at least a mirror that’s more honest.      You’d think with your degree and your job, you’d have mastered the art of looking put together. But seriously, your hair looks fine. I think you’re just being too hard on yourself. You know, I’ve been reading about the NHS staffing crisis lately – it’s been a huge deal, hasn’t it? It’s like they’re trying to fix everything at once, but the system’s just too stretched.      Oh, it’s definitely been a mess. I mean, I've had to wait over an hour just to see a GP, and that's if I even get through the waiting room. I heard they’re talking about A-Level reforms now, too. I don’t even know what the point is. It’s like they’re trying to make it harder for students to get into university, but then again, maybe that’s just how it is these days.      I heard about that too. It’s all about alignment with university courses, but I don’t know if that’s helping. It’s like they’re just trying to make everything match up with what’s happening in the job market. But honestly, I think the petrol crisis is the real problem right now. The prices are through the roof, and it’s making life so much more expensive.      Yeah, I know. I’ve been trying to cut down on how much I drive, but it’s not easy.

So, I heard you all were talking about the Black Death in class? Honestly, I thought it was some kind of exam topic for history. I mean, what’s the point of studying that? It’s like we’re all living in the same world now, yet we still have to remember how people died in the 14th century.      Oh, you’ve got it all wrong. It’s not just about dying. It’s about how it reshaped society. You know, the way the labor shortage changed the economy. It’s like studying the root of modern capitalism, in a way.      Yeah, and think about the feminist angles. A lot of women actually stepped up during the plague because so many men died. It was their time to take over and run things. Pretty cool, if you think about it.      I mean, if you’re into that kind of thing, you could say the Black Death was the first feminist movement. But I’m more interested in how it’s affecting our university fees. We’re all paying loads for courses that don’t even guarantee a job. It’s like the Black Death, but with paperwork and debt.      You’re comparing university to a plague? I’m not sure I like that analogy. But I get what you’re saying. We’re all just surviving, trying to make it through the system. And honestly, I don’t even know what I want to do. I’m stuck between a job that pays the bills and one that actually makes me happy.      I know exactly what you mean. I’ve been thinking about switching to a different course, but the finance is just too tight. I’ve got student loans, rent, and then there’s the pressure to do well. It’s exhausting.      I feel you. But maybe we should take a step back. Let’s talk about something more fun. Like, how are we going to deal with the smoking ban at university? I’ve been trying to quit, but it’s so hard when you’re in the common room with all those people lighting up.      Ugh, I tried that too. It’s like trying to stop eating chocolate. I just want a cigarette. And honestly, I’m not sure what the alternative is. I mean, I can’t afford a vape, and I don’t want to be a full-time herbal tea sipping Buddhist.

So, I just wanted to say, I think I need to start phasing out some of my friends. It’s not that I don’t like them, but lately I’ve been feeling like I just don’t want to see them anymore. It’s like I’m not connecting with them the way I used to.      Oh, I get that. I’ve been thinking about this too. It’s kind of like when you lose touch with someone from your past, right? You used to be super close, but now it’s just not the same.      Exactly. And it’s not like I’m angry or anything. It’s more like, I just don’t feel like putting in the effort anymore. It’s hard to explain, but it’s like a sort of emotional fatigue.      I think I’ve been there too. Sometimes you just outgrow people. Like, we’re at different stages of life now. I mean, I used to hang out with this group of people every weekend, but now I’m so busy with work and my own stuff, I just don’t have the time or energy.      Right, and it’s not like I can just stop seeing them all of a sudden. I mean, it’s a gradual thing. I’ve been thinking about how to approach it without hurting their feelings.      Yeah, that’s the tricky part. You don’t want to seem like you’re rejecting them, but you also don’t want to keep pretending everything’s the same. I’ve tried saying things like, “I really value our friendship, but I think I need to focus on other things right now.”      That sounds about right. I think I’ll try that. Maybe just start by saying I’m not as available as I used to be. I know it’s not a direct way, but it’s honest.      And maybe you can make it about your own needs. Like, “I really miss our friendship, but I’ve been feeling like I need to focus on myself for a while.” It’s about being clear but not overly dramatic.      Yeah, that makes sense. I think that’s the key—being honest but kind. I don’t want to lose them as friends, but I also can’t keep pretending I’m into it.      Exactly. And maybe it’s a good opportunity to reconnect with people who actually  want  to be there for you now.

So, I’ve been thinking about university days a lot lately. Remember when we first met in the library? I was so nervous about my first year, and you were already studying art, like, seriously?      Oh, you were the one who accidentally spilled coffee on my thesis draft. I was so upset, and you just laughed and said, “Well, that’s a start!” I still have that stained copy in my attic.      Yeah, I remember. Didn’t even apologize. But honestly, those days were wild. I mean, who’d have thought I’d end up studying philosophy, and you’d become an artist? My lectures are all about existentialism, and you’re painting murals in Nottingham.      It’s funny how life takes you in different directions. I always thought I’d end up in London, but then I ended up in Vienna, and then I met you. You know, I still have that old sketchbook from university, and I’ve been going through it, trying to remember what inspired me back then.      You should show me sometime. I’d love to see it. I’ve been reading this book about the Bauhaus movement lately, and I feel like you’ve got that same kind of energy.      You know what’s interesting? When I was in Vienna, I used to walk past the same galleries you go to now. I remember seeing your brother’s first exhibit there—what was it called? “Pieces of London.”      Oh, right! I still remember that. My dad was so proud. But you know, I’m planning a trip to Vienna next year. I’ve been dying to see the places you used to live and work. Maybe I can visit your old studio?      That would be amazing! I’d love to show you around. I’ve been waiting for someone to come back to Vienna with fresh eyes. Let’s plan it.      I’ll start looking into flights. I’ve got a few months before I graduate, so it should work. I’ll bring some of my philosophy notes too—maybe you can help me interpret them?      Only if you promise to let me paint something. You know how I get when I’m inspired.      Deal. But only if you let me see your old sketchbook first.      You’re on. Let’s make it a trip to remember.      To family, art, and a few more adventures.

So, I just had a really weird moment at the supermarket. I was trying to buy some protein powder for my gym session, and this guy came up to me and said, “You sure you’re not a woman?” Like, what? I didn’t even know what he was talking about. I was just looking at the label.      Oh no, that’s so frustrating. It’s like people still think that men are the only ones who go to the gym. I mean, I was in a gym once and a guy walked up to me and asked me if I was a  real  woman. I just stared at him and said, “Excuse me?” and walked away.      It’s so strange, isn’t it? I think it’s this ridiculous stereotype that only men who are into fitness are “real” men. But then again, if women are into fitness, they’re just…  girls  or something. Like, it’s not a real thing.      Exactly! And it’s not just in the gym. I’ve noticed it in everyday life too. Like, when I’m driving, I get people looking at me as if I’m not serious about something. Like, “Why is a woman driving a car?” or, “Why is she taking the lead on this project?”      That’s so much more subtle, but no less annoying. It’s like, why does gender have to define everything? I mean, I’m in a campervan with you, and I’m not just a “girl” looking for a ride— I’m  the one who planned the route and got us here.      Yeah, and I’m the one who taught English for a living. But even then, people still think I’m not “qualified” because I’m a woman. It’s exhausting.      I know. And I’ve been unemployed for years. I feel like people just assume I’m not capable of anything. It’s like the moment I stopped working, I was just…  out .      That’s so unfair. I mean, we’re both intelligent, hardworking, and capable. But society just  has  to put us in boxes.      I think it’s getting better, though. I see more women in leadership roles now, and more men who are open about their interests. But it’s still a long way to go.      I hope so. I think we’re starting to break through some of those barriers.

You know, I found these beautiful hand-thrown mugs in a market in Hebden Bridge the other week. They’re from a local potter—really unique designs, with a little bit of texture. I couldn’t resist bringing them back home.      Oh, I remember the one you brought over last time. I still use that one for my morning tea. It’s got that earthy look to it, like it’s been through a lot.      Didn’t it? I think it’s been through a few cups of tea and a couple of power cuts. Remember when the fridge broke last winter? We managed to keep the milk cool by putting it in a bowl of water in the back of the freezer.      Oh, I remember that. And the spiders? They were everywhere. I thought I’d never get a good night’s sleep again.      You couldn’t have known the spiders would be so bold. I swear, they were trying to scare me out of the house. But seriously, your garden looks lovely this time of year. The roses are in full bloom.      Yeah, they’re coming back to life. I’ve been trying to get the old bench out of the shed to put in the corner. I think it’s time for a bit of decorating. Maybe even a few flowers in the window boxes.      I’ve been thinking about the local festival coming up. I heard it’s going to be bigger than last year. Some of the people I know from school are going to be there.      Oh, I remember when that festival started. I used to take the kids there all the time. It’s amazing how time flies.      It’s funny how things change. I was thinking the other day about that accident in your kitchen last year. You said you slipped and broke a plate.      Yes, and I took the blame for it for weeks. I thought I’d never live it down. But you know what? It wasn’t your fault at all.      I know, I know. You were just tired and the floor was wet. I still remember the look on your face when you saw the broken plate.      And I still remember the silence that followed. I thought the whole house was going to fall apart.      To the quiet moments and the loud ones too.      And to the spiders, the power cuts, and the mugs.

Hey, mum, I was just thinking about our holiday. I really want to go somewhere with the beach, you know, like somewhere with white sand and waves. I’ve been looking up places online, and I think we could go to Cornwall or the Isle of Wight.      Oh, I like the idea of Cornwall. I remember when I was younger, we used to go there a few times. It’s such a beautiful place, and the seaside is always so peaceful. But, are you sure you want to go with me? You know how I get when I’m planning things.      Lad, you don’t need to worry. I’d go anywhere with you. But what’s the plan for the kids? I left my guitar at home, so if we’re going somewhere with a bit of music in the air, I’m all in.      Dad, you always say that. But seriously, I think we should take the kids too. Maybe we can go to Brighton. There’s the beach, the culture, and it’s not too far from here. Plus, I’ve got a few friends who said they’d like to come along.      That sounds fun, but I’m not sure about taking the kids. I know they love the beach, but I also know they get tired quickly. Maybe we should stick to a place where we can have a slower pace. What about the Lake District? It’s scenic, and there are lots of places to walk.      The Lake District? That’s a good idea. It’s peaceful, and it’s got great views. Plus, I can take my guitar and play some tunes by the lakeside. But wait, are we going to have any friends coming with us? I need to know if I should pack my stuff.      Yeah, actually, I’ve been talking to my friend Emily about it. She’s planning to go on a trip with her family, and she’s asking if we want to join them. We could all meet up and travel together.      Hmm, that might work. But I need to check the dates. I have a few shifts at the shop, and I can’t afford to miss too many.      I’ll help you with that, love. I can take notes or something. And if we’re going to be together, I’ll make sure we have a good time.

Hey, did you see that movie we watched last night?  10 Things I Hate About You ? It was so cheesy, but I kinda liked it. I mean, it was a romantic comedy, and it was… okay.      Yeah, I thought it was pretty good. The dialogue was a bit over the top, but the chemistry between the actors was real. Plus, I mean, Shakespeare? They actually adapted  The Taming of the Shrew  into a modern setting. That’s pretty clever.      Oh, right! I almost forgot about that. I guess it’s kind of like a modern take on a classic. But I still can’t get over how everyone kept saying “pardon me” like it was the 1800s. It was so funny, though. I mean, the way they dressed and talked was so different from today.      Total anachronism! But honestly, it’s the kind of movie that’s perfect to watch when you’re in the mood for something light and not too serious. Like, maybe we should watch more of those? I mean, if we’re going to be stuck at ANON’s house for the weekend…      Yeah, maybe. Although I’m already thinking about school stuff. I have this presentation due tomorrow about climate change. I’m so stressed.      You're not the only one! I’m stuck on this biology project. I have no idea what I’m doing. I tried to look it up, but all the info is so complicated.      I feel you. Maybe we can work on it together? I mean, if we have the time. But I still need to finish my presentation. I’ve already spent like three hours on it.      Honestly, I think I’ll just wing it. I mean, it’s not like it’s graded. Wait, no, it is. My teacher said it counts for 30% of our final grade. That’s not good.      Ugh, I’m so bad at school sometimes. I just can’t focus. I’m so tired. I wish we could just go to London for the weekend instead of doing homework.      I know! I’m really looking forward to the trip next week. I’ve been planning it for weeks. We’re going to see the Tower of London, maybe go to a museum or two, and eat at that café near Covent Garden where they have the best food.      That sounds amazing. I can’t wait.

You know, I was just looking at Facebook this morning. There's this old friend of mine from Costessey, he's posted all these photos of himself in a café in London. I don’t know why he's so obsessed with showing off.      I remember him from when he used to run that little shop on the high street. I bet he still does, though. He’s got that kind of stubbornness.      I think he might have moved to London to be closer to his daughter. I saw a post from her too—she works in finance. Facebook’s full of people trying to keep up with the Joneses, isn’t it?      I suppose it is, but I find it fascinating how people use it to share both the mundane and the extraordinary. I still can’t figure out why people post pictures of their breakfasts.      I once saw a post where someone had a picture of their toast with a caption that said, “My breakfast today: A slice of bread and a cup of tea. It’s not fancy, but it’s good.” I laughed so hard I nearly spilled my tea.      That’s the kind of thing that makes me miss the old days. Back when people didn’t have to show off. You didn’t need to post a photo of your food. You just ate it.      It’s amazing how much has changed. I still remember when I was a child, and being able to sit down with the whole family and have a proper meal was considered a treat. Nowadays, people are always rushing, always watching their time.      I think it's also about how we perceive value. In the past, time was measured in hours and minutes. Now, it's all about metrics and likes.      I suppose that’s part of the problem. It’s as if we’ve lost the ability to just be with people without needing to document it.      I’ve noticed that too. I even go out of my way to avoid my phone sometimes.      I’ve got a friend who’s a bit of an OCD sufferer. He’s always cleaning, arranging things in a certain way, and he gets really anxious if things aren’t just right. It’s like Facebook—everything has to be perfect.      I think that’s part of the pressure we put on ourselves.

So, I've been thinking about our trip to Germany last year. You remember how we got lost in Dresden, right? I swear, the GPS said one thing, and the locals were telling us another!      Oh, I remember! You were so determined to follow the GPS that you ended up walking for an hour through some cobblestone streets. I think I actually got more lost than you did.      Wait, didn't we meet this old man who spoke perfect English? He took us to the best schnitzel place in town. That was a good moment, even if we were still lost.      Yeah, and you almost got us kicked out of the restaurant because you were too busy taking selfies with the locals. I told you, we should’ve focused on eating and not the photo op!      You’re not the only one who got distracted by photos. I still have that picture of me trying to eat a bratwurst with my hands like a tourist. It’s one of those things I’ll never live down.      Speaking of photos, did you know that the locals in Germany actually have different accents depending on where they’re from? I remember one of my coworkers told me that the people in the south have a different way of speaking than those in the north.      Oh, I’ve heard about that too. There’s a big difference in dialects. I used to work in Hamburg, and the way people spoke was so different from what I was used to back in London.      And you know what’s even more interesting? They have these different regional languages. I think they call it "Hochdeutsch" or something like that. I’ve never been able to master that.      I think it’s called "Standard German." But I still can’t understand anything if they switch to that. I prefer the local dialects—they sound more like singing.      You’re not wrong. There’s a kind of musicality to it. I used to listen to a lot of German folk music, and the way they speak sounds like a song.      I go to Germany every year for work. It’s always so interesting to hear the accents and dialects change between cities. I’ve even picked up a bit of German. It’s not great, but it helps me when I’m in the shop buying bread or something.

So, how’s the new gig going? You mentioned you were doing something different this week. It’s going alright, I guess. I’m more into doing some cooking now, but I still manage to jam with some local musicians on weekends. I even joined a little drum circle in Exeter. Got a bit of a rhythm going on. That’s cool. I’ve been trying to get back into music myself. I’ve got this old drum kit in my flat that I’ve been wanting to dust off. I’ve been thinking about starting a band again. Just need to find some people who are into the same stuff. That sounds like a plan. You know, I’ve been in a few bands before, but I’ve been more focused on the kitchen lately. But I still play the drums in my free time. I think it’s good to keep that connection, you know? It helps with the flow when I’m cooking. Definitely. I remember when I was in school, we used to play at local pubs and cafes. One of my mates was a drummer, and we used to book gigs on a whim. I think that’s what I miss now. It’s easier to get lost in routine when you’re a student. Yeah, I get that. I’ve been thinking about taking a break from the kitchen for a while and maybe going into a music internship. I did apply for one at a local venue in Devon, but I’m not sure if I’ll get it. It’s a bit of a toss-up. That’s a good move. I’d say go for it. If you’ve got the passion, you should be doing it. I’ve been applying for internships too, but I’m still trying to figure out what direction I want to go in. Maybe something in music tech or production? That’s interesting. I’ve been thinking about studying music production online. It’s something I’ve always wanted to do, but the timing never worked out. With the apprenticeship I’ve got, I can at least get some hands-on experience. That’s a solid plan. I think I’ll take a similar approach. I’ve got a few workshops coming up, and I’m hoping to meet some people who go in the same direction.

Well, I suppose we should get something to eat. We’ve been walking around the city for an hour, and I’m starving.      Yeah, I’m with you. I’ve been dying for a coffee, though. I was in a rush this morning and didn’t have time to grab one.      That’s understandable. I think they serve that new latte here. It’s got a nice foam top.      Didn’t you just get the free coffee with your loyalty card?      Oh, right, I’d forgotten about that. I’m glad you reminded me. I’m still trying to figure out what the benefits are. I mean, what’s the point of a loyalty card if you’re not getting anything for it?      Fair point. I think it’s just a way for the café to keep customers coming back. I’ve heard that the owner is trying to expand—maybe even do a domino drive or something.      Hmm, sounds like they’re planning something big. I’ve been meaning to check out the business structure of local cafés. I’ve got a bit of time on my hands now that I’ve finished my term at school.      Yeah, I’ve been thinking about that too. I’m considering doing an apprenticeship in a café, maybe something with a focus on sustainability. I’ve seen a lot of places talk about their eco-friendly practices.      That’s interesting. I used to work in the education sector, but I’ve always been curious about how small businesses operate. Speaking of which, have you heard about the new transport plans for Newcastle?      Not really. I think the city is still trying to work out the best way to manage traffic. I’ve been meaning to ask my dad about it. He’s been involved in some local business ventures.      That’s great. I think it’s important to support the local economy, especially with all the changes happening in the city. Speaking of changes, have you thought about where you’re going this summer?      I’m still figuring that out. I was thinking about going to Durham. I heard the weather is nice there, and I want to see the castle.      That’s a good plan. I used to go there when I was younger. It’s always a peaceful place to visit. Just make sure to pack a sleeping bag—probably the weather there won’t be too bad.

Hey, mate, how’ve you been? It’s been ages since we last saw each other. I’ve got to say, I’m thrilled to see you here in my new flat.      Hey, man! I’ve been good, just busy with work and trying to get my head around this new city. I’ve got to admit, I’m still getting used to the cost of living here. A lot more than I expected.      Yeah, I know, it’s a bit of a shock. I remember when I first moved to Sussex—it felt like I was paying double for everything. Still does, honestly.      True, but I guess that’s the price of living in a place like this. I’ve been thinking about how much I miss the cost of living in Manchester. At least the rent wasn’t an issue there. So, I was just thinking about the whole cancer thing. I mean, it's such a tough subject, isn’t it? I can’t even begin to imagine what it’s like for someone who’s going through it. I know we’ve all had our share of health struggles, but this… it’s so different.      Absolutely, it’s heavy. I was actually talking to my sister last week about it. She’s been doing this awareness campaign at work, and she’s had some interesting conversations. She mentioned how people are so hesitant to talk about cancer when it’s someone close. You know, like, they avoid it, or they don’t know what to say.      Hmm, I can see that. I mean, it’s a scary topic. I think part of the problem is the stigma around it. Like, people fear it, but they don’t want to admit it. I remember when my mother was diagnosed. It was hard to be around her, you know? You want to be supportive, but you don’t want to overstep or say the wrong thing.      Exactly. I think that’s why it’s so important to just be there, even if you don’t know what to say. I’ve been trying to remind myself that sometimes silence can be okay. But I also know that sometimes people just need someone to listen.      I completely agree. I’ve been trying to be more open about my own mental health too. It’s not always easy, but I think it helps. I remember when I was going through that tough time with my dad, and I didn’t want to burden anyone. But he always said, “Talk to me, even if it’s not about the problem.”      That’s beautiful. I think that’s the key—being open, not just about the disease, but about the whole experience. I’ve been thinking about my own mom, too. She’s been dealing with some chronic issues, and it’s been hard to see her struggle. You just want to fix it, but you can’t.      I know. It’s one of the hardest parts of being close to someone—knowing you can’t always fix the problem. But I think it’s also about being there for them, even when you can’t do anything. It’s not about solving it, it’s about being present.

So, what’s the deal with you two and your obsession with tennis? I swear, every weekend you’re either hitting a ball or talking about coaching!      Yeah, we’re pretty serious about it, Dad. Sounds like you’ve got the right mindset. Didn’t you mention something about wanting to do apprenticeships after school? That could be a good path. I remember when I was your age, I was trying to figure out what I wanted to do. I ended up in marketing, and it’s been a good ride. But honestly, it took me a while to get there.      So, did you ever think about going into something like that? Like, starting your own business?      I did, but I was too scared to take the leap. You go through a lot of stuff before you figure it out. But the key is to stay open-minded and not be afraid to try new things.      I think I’m starting to get it. My coach says I’ve got potential, and I’ve got the drive to make something of it. Maybe I’ll even start my own academy one day.      That’s the spirit, mate. And if you ever need a hand with the business side of things, you know who to ask.

So, I just got the confirmation that our trip to Lancaster is all set. I can’t believe we’re actually going to visit the coast again. Yeah, I’ve heard about that too. I think I read somewhere that the fish is sourced fresh from local markets and they use the traditional deep-frying method. Absolutely. I think we’re both lucky to have our families and friends around us.

So, I was just telling my mates about the gig last night. That band  The Hollow Echo —they’re local, you know? I’ve been dying to see them live since they started playing at the underground venue in the old warehouse.      Yeah, I heard about that. I was actually there too.
