She said it’s a bit different—more experimental, but still retains that emotional core. I’m curious to check it out. I’ve been meaning to get back into music more. I’ve been so focused on my studies, I haven’t really had time to explore anything outside of that.      I know what you mean. Between uni and part-time work, it’s a struggle. But I’ve been trying to make time for my hobbies. I’ve been painting again, actually. I started doing some abstract stuff, and it’s been a good escape.      That’s cool! I’ve always wanted to try painting, but I’m scared I’ll just make a mess.      Well, you can’t make a mess if you’re trying. Plus, it’s all about the process. You don’t have to be perfect.      Yeah, I guess you’re right. Maybe I’ll pick up some brushes this weekend.      To new hobbies, and bands that make you feel alive.      To that! And to surviving university.

So, I think we’ve all agreed that the way we’re playing Pandemic is a bit too much like a game of ‘who’s the best at keeping the virus at bay.’ I mean, we’ve been fighting this thing for two hours now, and we’re still in the red zone.      You’re absolutely right. I feel like I’m the only one actually doing anything. I’ve been researching all the outbreaks and trying to find the right combination of actions. But every time I think I’ve got a handle on it, the virus just mutates again.      You know, I think part of the problem is we’re all playing too aggressively. I’ve been trying to focus more on building up the research labs instead of just rushing to cure everything. I mean, I’m a chef, not a game expert, but I know that you can’t fix a problem by just throwing more ingredients at it.      I think that’s exactly it. I remember once, in a similar group, we all went for the cure too early and ended up with no labs left. We lost the game because we didn’t think strategically. It’s like trying to make a perfect soufflé—every move has to be precise.      That’s a very apt analogy, actually. I mean, I’ve spent most of my life working with people in need, and I’ve always believed that preparation and planning are key. If we’d just taken a step back and thought about how the virus spreads, maybe we wouldn’t be in this mess.      And speaking of thinking, I’m not sure if I’m even allowed to make moves anymore. I’m feeling a bit out of my depth here. But honestly, I think I’m starting to get the hang of it. I’ve barely noticed the board, but I’ve been trying to be a ‘support worker’ for the rest of you.      You know what? I think you’re doing better than you think. Everyone has a role, even if it’s just holding the board together.      I keep thinking about the time we played this game with the kids last year. They had no idea what they were doing, but they still had more fun than we do now. Maybe we’re trying too hard?      That’s a good point.

Okay, so I was thinking—what if we plan a little birthday celebration for the twins? The CBeebies pantomime is on at the weekend, and I know they both love it. Maybe we can make it a special day with some stories and a little party?      That sounds like a great idea, Mummy! I love the CBeebies stories so much. Especially the one with the talking animals. I remember the one where the bear had to solve a mystery. It was so funny!      Yeah, that was awesome! And the time when the hare got stuck in the mud and had to climb up a tree. I laughed so hard, I almost fell off my chair!      Oh, I remember that one too. And I think the CBeebies pantomime this year features a similar story. It’s called  Where’s Wally?  I think—yes, that’s right. They’ve been doing a series of stories about him and his friends.      I hope they include the red balloon! I love the part where Wally blows up a balloon and it floats away. It always makes me feel happy and safe.      Absolutely—it’s one of my favorite parts too. I was thinking, maybe we can dress up as characters from the show. It would be so much fun. I’ve got some old costumes from when I was a kid, and I can make them fit the kids.      Can I be the grumpy bear? I like being grumpy. It makes me feel powerful!      You can be the grumpy bear! And I’ll be the wise old owl. I think we’ll all look so silly, but it’ll be great. And if we can get some of the family to join in, that would be even better.      Can Grandpa come too? He loves the stories, and he’s been trying to remember the endings of all the CBeebies tales.      Of course he can! I love that saying. And it’s a perfect message for the twins—patience and kindness.

So, I’ve been thinking about moving out of the flat. I’ve had enough of the damp in the kitchen, and I’m not sure I want to be stuck here for another year.      Oh, really? I thought you were happy here. You’ve only been living here for a few months.      Yeah, I know, but I’m starting to feel like I need a bit more space. Plus, I’ve been looking at some properties in Oxford. It’s not too far, and the rent is reasonable.      Oxford? That’s not too bad. But I’ve heard it’s pricey. I mean, I’m not rich, but I can’t afford a deposit on a place there.      I know, I’ve been thinking about moving too, but I’ve been holding off because of the job. I’ve been on a few apps too, but I’m not sure I want to be in a relationship right now. I’m still trying to figure out what I want out of life.      That’s okay. It’s not like you have to be in a relationship to be happy. I mean, I’ve been doing a lot of socializing with friends, and it’s been really nice. Though I miss the weekend dinners with my mum.      Yeah, I’ve been thinking about how much I miss my family too. It’s funny how moving cities can make you realize how much you’ve taken your family for granted.      Definitively. Whether it’s moving, changing jobs, or just taking a break from dating, it’s all part of the journey.

So, I've been thinking about our old childhood toys. Remember the one we used to play with—those giant plastic dinosaurs? I still have one in my garage, covered in dust.      Oh, I remember those! I had one that looked like it could actually roar. I used to pretend it was a T-Rex and terrorize my younger brother. He used to run around the house screaming, “Dinosaurs are coming!”      That sounds like fun. I had a teddy bear that my mum used to dress up, but I think it’s still in the attic. My dad used to tell me stories about it when I was a kid.      That’s sweet. I still talk to my mum about things like that. She always says, “You know, I used to think your brother was an alien.”      Oh, I love that! My mum still says I used to speak in riddles and only she could understand me. It’s funny how our childhood memories shape the way we talk now.      I guess dialects and accents are like a part of our identity. I sometimes think my way of speaking is influenced by growing up in Essex. Do you think our dialects have affected the way we work?      Absolutely. I’ve noticed that in my job as an account manager, I use a more formal tone, but at home, I speak exactly how I did when I was a kid. I think it’s a mix of professional language and familial warmth.      Yeah, and being in a managerial role, I’ve had to develop a more polished way of speaking. But I still use a lot of the phrases I learned from my mum and dad. It’s part of who I am.      That’s interesting. I’ve always thought about language in terms of work and home. As an accountant, I have to be precise and clear, but at home, I’m more casual. I even started learning some Spanish to talk to my uncle who’s from Spain. He’s been helping me with the language over the years.      That’s amazing. I’ve always wanted to learn another language, but I never got around to it. I think it’s a shame not to, especially living in England with so many different cultures.      I agree. I’ve been trying to improve my French, mostly for work, but I’m not very good at it.

So, I've just got back from a little trip to the Lake District. It was absolutely beautiful. I got to go hiking with some friends, and we stayed in this small cottage by the lake.      That sounds lovely. Did you get to do any of the classic hikes there? Like the one up to Scafel Pike?      I did! It was a tough one, but the views were worth it. The sun was out, and the air was so fresh. We even saw a red squirrel on the way up.      Oh, I love the Lake District. I’ve been there a few times with my family. My mum always says that the best time to go is in the autumn when the leaves are changing.      Yeah, and I think the autumn is when the trails are less crowded. I went there last year, and it was just me and a few other hikers.      I’ve always wanted to go. I mean, I’ve been to the countryside before, but the Lake District is one of those places you hear about in stories.      It's like a mix of nature and history. There are these old stone walls everywhere, and the fells – those big hills – are just so majestic.      Speaking of nature, I’ve been meaning to take up hiking more. I’m not the most athletic, but I want to get out more and get some exercise.      You should definitely try it. I’d be happy to go with you. I’m not great at it either, but it’s a great way to clear your head.      That’s a great idea. I’ve been trying to get my friends to go hiking more. We even have a group chat for it.      I might have to join in. I just need to get a pair of decent hiking boots. I’ve had these old ones for years, and they’re not really up to the task.      You’ll need a good pair of boots. I’ve got a few that I’m not using anymore. Maybe I can lend you some?      That sounds like a good move. We could all go on a hike together. It’s a great way to get out and about.      I love that idea. We could plan a trip to the Lake District, or maybe somewhere a bit closer, like the Peak District.      I’m up for that.

Morning, lads. Did you two get any sleep last night? I was up until 2 a.m. trying to fix the boiler. It’s like it’s been given a new lease of life, or something.      Oh, I bet that was a nightmare. I was up too, but only because my cat decided to do a midnight patrol. I swear, that thing is more of a dog than a cat now.      I got up at 6 a.m. to make coffee. I thought I’d be the first one up, but it turns out the cat has a schedule too. It’s like it’s been trained by a military officer.      You know, I think the boiler might be getting revenge for the time I left it to run on auto during the flood last winter. I still have the leaky patch on the wall in the bathroom.      I heard you were working late on that project with the local council. How did it go?      It went okay. We got the plans approved, but it’s going to be a bit of a logistical nightmare. They want the pipeline rerouted through a park to avoid the residential area.      That sounds like a mess. But it’s good that you’re getting the job done. I was reading an article last night about how engineers are being asked to balance utility and nature more than ever.      Yeah, it’s a tightrope walk. I suppose that’s the life. But I’m glad I got through the proposal. I was worried I’d have to start looking elsewhere.      You’re not going to have to do that. You’re one of the best in the field. Just don’t let the boiler get to you. I’ve been meaning to ask—did you ever learn to fix it yourself?      I tried. I got halfway through the manual, and then I realized I was just making things worse. I think it’s time to call in the professionals.      You could always get one of those smart home systems. You know, the kind that monitors the boiler and sends you notifications? I’ve been thinking about getting one myself.      That’s a good idea. I’ve been meaning to get a smart thermostat too. I think I’ll go check out the specs today.      You should. And while you’re out, could you pick up some fresh produce?

So, Reg, you’re really going to be away for a while? I mean, Saudi Arabia? That’s got to be a big change from Peterborough, right?      Yeah, it is. I mean, I’ve never even been outside the UK before. But it’s for a good reason—working with the government on some infrastructure project. They’re really pushing for development in that region.      That sounds intense. I mean, I can’t even imagine working in a place like that. You’ll be living in a foreign country, dealing with different customs, different languages. What’s the plan for your family?      Well, I’d say it’s going to be tough, but it’s also a chance to see the world. Reg’s got a good job, so he’s not going alone. He’s got a partner and two kids. They’re moving with him.      Oh, that’s a big step. Moving to a different country with your family, especially with kids. I mean, I’m still figuring out where I want to live, let alone move across the world.      It’s definitely a decision that takes time. I’ve been thinking about it for months. But it’s about opportunity. You know, the money, the experience, the chance to be part of something bigger.      It’s not just about the money, though. I mean, you’ve got to think about the people you leave behind. I’ve got a few mates from work, and I don’t know if I’ll be able to see them again.      That’s the thing about it, mate. You have to make sacrifices. But Reg’s not just going for the job—he’s going for the future. And he’s got family that supports him.      Maybe I should start thinking about my own future. I mean, I’m at the stage where I’m looking for something more. Maybe a different job, a different city, even a different country. I’ve been reading about how good the healthcare system is in Germany.      Yeah, I heard that too. But the problem is, you don’t just move countries and expect everything to work out. There’s a lot of red tape, especially with jobs. I mean, I had to go through a whole application process just to get this role.      It’s not just the jobs. There’s the culture, the language, the way people live.

So, I've been meaning to ask you, how do you manage your skincare routine when you’re traveling? I’ve been trying to keep up with it, but I’m not sure if I’m doing it right.      Oh, I get that. I used to be pretty strict about my routine, but now I’m more laid-back. I think it depends on where you are. In Stockholm, I’ve been using some of the local products, like those herbal toners from the apothecary. They’re amazing for sensitive skin.      That’s interesting. I’ve actually been reading up on holistic skincare and how it connects to the environment. I mean, when you’re surrounded by so much greenery, like in the botanical gardens, you start to think about how the plants affect your skin. Have you noticed any changes?      Honestly, I have. I’ve been more mindful about what I’m putting on my skin and what I eat. I’ve started incorporating more herbal infusions into my skincare. My wife, she’s a teacher, and she’s always encouraging me to listen to my body. She says your skin is like a mirror—what you put in, you get out.      That’s a beautiful way to put it. I’ve often told my students that understanding your body’s signals is key. I’ve been trying to get into a better routine myself. I’ve been doing some research on the principles of biodynamic skincare. It’s fascinating how the natural cycles of the Earth affect our own cycles.      Exactly! And it’s not just skincare—there’s so much more to it. I work in communications, so I’m always thinking about how our surroundings shape our well-being. The gardens here in Stockholm are incredible. I’ve been telling my friends how the scent of the plants affects my mood. It’s like a natural therapy.      I’ve been trying to incorporate more green spaces into my life too. I’ve been walking through these gardens every morning. It’s amazing how it clears your head. I’ve even started thinking about how I could bring some of this into my business. Maybe a wellness retreat for entrepreneurs?      That’s a great idea. I think it’s more important than ever for people in high-stress jobs to prioritize self-care. I’ve been advising my students to take breaks and reconnect with nature.

So, I've been thinking about our accents lately. I mean, you can tell where people are from just by the way they speak. You know, like down here in Kent, we all have that sort of flat, soft sound to our speech, right? It's almost like we all sound like we're on a beach or something.      Aye, I've noticed that too. I’ve been in London for years, and every time I come back home, I can pick out a Kent accent a mile away. It's got that slight lilt, don’t you think? You can tell someone’s from here even if they're not saying much.      I agree. It’s like a badge of honour, isn’t it? I mean, growing up in Harlow, I could tell if someone was from Essex or Kent just by their accent. It’s part of who we are, isn’t it?      Yeah, but I’ve also noticed that people who move around a lot, like me, end up with a mix of accents. I grew up in Chatham, but I’ve lived in London, Manchester, even a bit in Devon. It's like my accent is a patchwork quilt now.      That's interesting. I feel like my accent has changed a bit because I've been studying in the city. Now I speak more like the people I meet there, but I still catch myself slipping back into my old way of speaking sometimes. It’s so weird.      You know, I think that's the thing about accents. They can change with time and place, but they always come back. I’ve been retired for a few years now, but I still sound the same as I did when I was working. It's like it's ingrained in you.      Exactly. I’ve always thought that accents are part of your identity, especially when you're at home. You can't really escape them, can you? I mean, even if you move away, you still talk like you grew up here.      I guess that’s why I’ve been thinking about going back to Kent. I miss the way things were. The weather, the people, even the way we speak. It’s like a comfort zone.      I could go with that. I mean, I grew up here, and even though I live in the city now, I’d miss those days of riding my bike around the countryside, listening to the sounds of the sea, and just being part of the community.

So, I've been thinking about our Halloween party this year. I was just telling the boys that I’d like to go with a theme—maybe something more original than last year's "Monster Mash."      Yeah, the Monster Mash was a bit cliché. I mean, it’s not like we’re kids anymore. But I was wondering—do you think we should have a baked Alaska for dessert? I remember reading that it’s a showstopper.      Oh, you’re right. Baked Alaska is always a hit. But I’m not sure how to get the perfect flake. I mean, I’ve tried, but the meringue tends to collapse.      You just need to be patient. I’ve seen some videos online where they use a special technique—like grating the cheese first. Wait, you’re not going to use cheese in the baked Alaska, are you?      No, no, not in the meringue. I was just thinking about grating some cheese for the party snacks. Maybe some cheddar or something.      Cheddar’s good. I love it on crackers. But seriously, I was also thinking about something else. Have you ever considered recruiting some kids for the Halloween party? I mean, maybe some younger ones who can help set up.      I have considered that. But I’m not sure how to approach it. I mean, not everyone wants to be involved. Plus, there are those age-of-consent issues. Some people might not be comfortable with the idea.      I get that. It’s a sensitive topic. I mean, I’ve heard stories from friends who were involved in similar things and it wasn’t always positive. But I think we’re in a better place now, right?      You’re absolutely right. We’ve come a long way. I remember when I was your age, things were so different. I think we need to be mindful of how we approach these conversations, especially with younger people.      Exactly. And while we’re on the topic, I’ve been thinking about something else. Remember that time we had to explain the history of the Halloween party to our parents? They didn’t understand why we wanted to do it.      Oh, I remember. It was funny. They thought we were just having a party, not realizing the amount of planning that goes into it. But I think it’s changed a lot over the years.      Yeah, it’s a testament to how things have evolved.

Morning, love. I’ve just had a cup of real Yorkshire tea, proper and strong, not that muck they serve down here. How’s your sleep? Still having trouble with the sun coming through that window?      Oh, I’m still getting used to the sun here. It’s so bright compared to Japan! Though I have to say, I love the mornings here. The air’s so fresh, and it’s not as cold as it was when we first moved here. You remember when we had that snowstorm last winter? You were stuck in the car for three hours, and I was trying to get the fridge to work!      Oh, I remember. I was so grateful to finally get home, even if it was late and I had a head like a drum. I was about to give up on ever getting back to Shipley. But you were still there for me, weren’t you?      Of course I was. I would never have left you in the lurch. Speaking of which, I’ve been thinking about visiting New York. I read this article about a flight school there, and I’m seriously considering taking flying lessons. Have you ever thought about it?      I’ve thought about it a few times, but I’m not sure if I have the patience for it. I’ve always preferred the ground. Though I did have a friend in London who got a pilot’s license. It took him years, but he’s now flying private jets for a living.      That’s impressive! I’ve been meaning to look into it. I’m finally feeling like I can do something for myself, you know? And with the new job at the university, I think I have the time. Plus, I’ve got the money, thanks to the grant from the education council.      That’s great to hear. You’ve always been so driven. I still can’t believe we met in Japan. We were both just fresh out of our PhDs, and here we are, over a decade later, still talking about the same things.      It’s amazing how time flies. I still remember our first night in Tokyo, walking around Shibuya, just the two of us. It felt like the world was on our shoulders, but we were so excited. I can’t wait to see what’s next.      And I can’t wait to see you fly, love.

So, I was running late this morning, and I thought I had 30 minutes to get to the coffee shop. But by the time I got out of my flat, I was already 15 minutes late. I had to sprint down the street like I was in a race.      Oh no, that sounds like one of those days where everything goes wrong. I remember a time when I was late for a meeting and got stuck in a traffic jam, but then the bus came and I ended up getting there just in time.      You know, I think that’s part of growing up. It’s like the older you get, the more you learn to manage time, but sometimes you still fall into the trap of thinking you’ve got more time than you do.      That’s funny. I once had an A Level exam and thought I had an hour to get there, but I got distracted by a YouTube video and ended up missing the start by 20 minutes. My teacher was so upset.      That’s like the origin of the word “late” – it’s not just about being delayed, it’s about the consequences of that delay.      I think that’s also why we have the phrase “late for everything.” It’s like, if you’re late once, you’re automatically late for everything else.      I’m not sure that’s entirely true. I was late once for a job interview, and the interviewer was a bit annoyed, but he still gave me a chance. Still, I shouldn’t have been late.      Exactly! You can’t let one misstep define you. I mean, I still remember the time I was late for my first day at university because I got lost on the way. But I made it in time for the welcome speech.      And that’s probably why I’m studying English Literature. It’s all about the power of words and how they shape our understanding of the world. I think the origin of words is fascinating. Like, how “scramble” and “scrabble” are related.      I agree. I think the origin of “Scrabble” is from the word “scramble,” which is interesting. It’s like the game is a scramble of letters, and the winners are the ones who can find the best words.      Hey, I think I’m about to win this game. I’ve got a “quarantine” and a “florist” on the board.

I've been thinking a lot lately, you know. I've had a few years of being out of work and it's been a tough road. You ever feel like you're just waiting for something to happen, but nothing does? Oh, I know what you mean. I used to be a childminder, you know, and then I retired. But even after that, I found myself not really knowing what to do with my days. I mean, I used to be busy with the kids, but now it's just me and the house. It's like the whole world just slows down. Yeah, I guess it does. I've always been a bit of a hands-on person. I like to do things, but when I first retired, I didn't have much to do. I tried gardening, but I can't stand the weeds. And I tried to take up painting, but I just can't get the hang of it. Haha, I know what you mean. I tried knitting, you know, for the grandchildren. But I just couldn't keep up with the patterns. I ended up making a scarf that looked more like a bundle of wool than anything else. I think they liked it, though. Well, maybe it's not about making things perfect. Maybe it's about just enjoying the process, you know? I've been thinking about the old days, when I used to work and have a routine. Even if it wasn't the most exciting job, it kept me busy. I suppose that's the thing, isn't it? When you're working, you have a purpose. Even if it's just looking after kids all day, it gives you a sense of doing something. Now I'm just trying to figure out what to do with my time. I know. I think I've been trying to find a new purpose, but I'm not sure where to start. I've been going to the local community center now, just to see if there's anything going on. It's a bit of a stretch, but I'm not sure what else to do. That's a good idea. Maybe there's something there you could get into. You never know, you might find a new passion or a new way to spend your days. And if not, at least you're out and about instead of just sitting at home all day.

So, I've been thinking about the new app that tracks your fitness goals. You know, the one that syncs with your phone and gives you daily challenges. I’ve been trying it out, but I can't get the calorie count right. It's driving me mad.      Oh, I tried that too. It’s one of those apps that uses your GPS to estimate how many calories you’ve burned. I think it's more of a game than a real tracker. It's fun, but it’s not always accurate.      Yeah, I’ve heard that too. I still use a basic fitness band, but I think it's the same principle. Still, it's good to have a goal, even if you’re not sure how accurate it is.      Exactly. I’ve been trying to lose a few pounds, and it’s giving me a bit of motivation. But then I think about all the food I’ve eaten at the holiday. I mean, we had so much good stuff.      Oh, I know. We had a proper meal every day—some of it even with the local produce from the market. It was like a food festival.      And the fish from the local market was amazing. I swear, it tasted like it was caught that morning.      Speaking of food, have you heard about the new train station that’s due to open soon? I think it’s going to change things around here.      Yeah, I remember reading about it in the local paper. It’s been delayed for a while, but they say it’s going to be a big boost for the area. Better transport means more tourists, which means more business for the local shops.      I think it’s going to be a game-changer. It’s been such a long time since the last station was upgraded. The locals have been waiting for it.      I wonder if it’ll make it easier for people like me to get around. You know, I’ve always been a bit of a stickler for convenience. Not that I’m not enjoying the holiday, but I’d love to have the option to travel more easily.      I can imagine. You’re not the only one who’d benefit. The local schools and businesses will be able to get more people in and out. It feels like the area’s finally getting the recognition it deserves.

So, I just got back from this weekend trip to Cardiff. I had this awesome stag weekend with some course mates, and I thought I’d tell you about it.      Oh, a stag weekend? You didn’t do anything too crazy, did you?      Not really, but it was still crazy enough. We stayed at this Airbnb near the castle, and we spent most of the time just drinking and talking about old university stuff. One of the guys even started a debate about whether Shakespeare should be taught in schools.      That’s the sort of thing you get into at seminars, isn’t it? I remember one of our professors talking about  Hamlet  and how it’s still relevant today.      Exactly! And then, to make it even better, we caught a movie in the evening. We went to this new cinema that opened up near the city, and we saw  The Lie  – a British film. It was pretty good, but I thought the ending was a bit too slow.      I’ve heard of that one. I think it’s got some pretty intense themes. Like, did it make you think about real-life lies and stuff?      Definitely. And then we got back to the Airbnb and decided to play some games. We had this old PlayStation 4, and we tried to play  Valorant  for the whole night. It was a mess, but it was fun.      That’s the sort of thing students do, right? Between studying, football, and gaming. Speaking of football, have you seen the Premier League recently? I’ve been watching a lot of matches on my phone.      Yeah, I’ve been watching too. I think Manchester City are going to win it again this year. I mean, it’s obvious, but still. My brother’s a huge fan, and he’s been going to matches every week. He even said he’s thinking about doing a stag weekend with his mates next year.      That’s cool. I can’t wait to go to a game with you. I think it’s been ages since we last went.      Yeah, we should do that. Maybe go to a match in Manchester? It’s not too far from here.      Sounds like a plan. I’ll let you know when I’m free.      Deal. And maybe we could catch up on some books too. I’ve been reading a lot of poetry lately, and I think it’s helping me with my essays.

Hey, it's good to see you again, Em. How have you been? I’ve been busy with work and trying to get my head around this new project I’m co-ordinating. It's been a bit of a rollercoaster, but I think things are settling now.      I know, I’ve felt the same! Work has been hectic too. I’ve been working on a marketing campaign for Pearson, and honestly, it’s been a bit of a nightmare. But hey, you know what they say—every cloud has a silver lining. How’s your health? You’ve been looking a bit peaked lately.      Thanks, I’ve been okay, but I’ve been struggling with a bit of insomnia. I’m trying to figure out what’s going on, but I’m not sure if it's just stress or something more. I’ve been meaning to talk to you about it. Do you think it’s just work pressure, or should I be worried?      I can’t say for sure, but I think it’s definitely work-related. You know, you’ve always been a bit of a workaholic. But seriously, you need to take care of yourself. Have you thought about changing your schedule or getting some time off? You deserve it.      Yeah, I know. I’ve been thinking about it. I’m actually considering taking a short break next month. Maybe a weekend trip somewhere. I’m not sure where yet, but I want to get out of the office for a bit.      That sounds amazing! You’d be a great fit for a road trip through the countryside. I’ve been meaning to take a break too, but I’m always pulled back into work. Speaking of which, have you heard from Alex lately? I thought you two were pretty close.      Honestly, I haven’t. I tried to reach out a few times, but he hasn’t responded. I guess life gets in the way. I think he’s still in Oxford, though. You know how he is—he’s got that  ex-boyfriend  energy sometimes.      Oh, I know. I still remember the time you two were dating. You were so happy back then. Anyway, have you thought about your future plans? I heard you’re planning to move back to London soon.      Yeah, I’ve been thinking about that. I’ve got a few opportunities there, and I think it’s time to take the next step.

So, I was just telling my mum about the one time I tried to grow a vegetable garden and ended up with a complete disaster. I thought I was being all serious, planting tomatoes and carrots, but I didn’t even know the difference between a seed and a seedling.      Sounds like you had a bit of a green thumb gone wrong. But I’ve been trying to grow some herbs in my flat. I’ve got rosemary and thyme, but they’re not doing too well. I keep thinking I’m doing it right, but they’re just sitting there like they’re judging me.      That’s the worst. I think the secret is to not overthink it. When I first tried growing plants, I was obsessed with the soil, the pH levels, the amount of sunlight—like I was about to start a PhD on plant science. But then I just switched to houseplants and it was easier.      Yeah, I guess once you stop trying to be a botanist, it’s easier. Although, I have to say, I’ve been trying to grow a few more things since I got a new apartment. My roommates are always asking for ingredients for cooking, so maybe I should start growing some herbs.      That’s a good idea. You know, I’ve been thinking about starting a small garden in the back of the house. My parents have always said I’m not a proper gardener, but I want to do it properly this time. Maybe I’ll start with some tomatoes and herbs.      I’d help you, but I might end up the one who ends up with dead plants. I’ve already killed a basil plant that was supposed to be the star of my kitchen. I still have the pot. It’s just sitting there, like it’s waiting for me to fix it.      I’ve got one of those too. My mum sent me a fern once as a joke, and I thought it was a real plant. It was just a dead stick. I kept watering it and putting it in the sun. Now I’ve got a goomba of a plant that I can’t even tell if it’s alive or not.      You know what I’ve been doing? I’ve been trying to make some proper tea with the right amount of milk and sugar.

So, how was your weekend, Dave? I heard you had a bit of a busy time with the kids.      Oh, it was alright, thank you. A bit hectic, though. My wife’s cousin is a footballer, and her son is about eight. He’s always asking if he can go to training with the team. I reckon he’s got more ball skills than I do.      Haha, funny you say that. My nephew is a snooker player, and he’s got that same sort of energy. He’s always talking about tournaments and the players. I even caught him trying to knock down a few balls in the garden last week.      That’s something. I think I’d rather be knocking down a few weeds in the garden, though. I’ve been trying to get my roses back in bloom. It’s a bit of a nightmare with the weather this year.      Well, the weather’s been a bit of a drag everywhere, isn’t it? I’ve been trying to get my students’ work marked, and it’s been slow going. You know how it is with deadlines and everything.      I can only imagine. I’ve been doing the same. It’s a bit of a balancing act between marking and actually getting some work done. I’ve even considered applying for a part-time position in the police force or the armed forces. It might be a good change of pace.      You know, I’ve thought about that too. I was in the army back in my day, and it’s something I still find interesting. Though I’ve got a bit of a soft spot for academia. Still, it’s good to keep the mind active.      Absolutely. I think it’s important to keep things fresh. You never know, maybe one day we’ll both be guest lecturers at some military academy.      Not if I have anything to say about it. I’d rather stay in the lecture hall than in a barracks. Though I’ll admit, the discipline is something to be admired.      Fair enough. I think I’ll stick to the garden and the marking for now. Unless I get a sudden urge to change my career.      Well, don’t go changing your mind too soon. We’ve got enough to do without you vanishing off to the forces.      Relax, old man. I was just joking.

Okay, I've got a few things to discuss before we get too deep into the day. First off, I need to figure out who’s going to be at the birthday party for my brother. I know Sally is coming from Liverpool, and Tom from Bristol, but I haven't heard from Rob yet.      Mum, I can call Rob for you. He said he’d be free, but I should double-check just in case. I mean, it’s his brother’s birthday, so he probably wouldn’t miss it.      That’s true. But I don’t want to assume. Still, it’s better to be safe than sorry. Also, I’ve been trying to get the venue confirmed. The one near the park is still available, right?      Yeah, Mum, the park venue is still on. I called them this morning, and they’re all set for Saturday. The caterer has a menu in place too. I even got a discount for booking early.      Great, that’s a relief. I was worried we might have to move it to another location if the park one fell through. Anyway, I need to talk about the Christening too. I’ve got the invitations printed, but I haven’t sent them out yet.      Can I help with that? I’m pretty good with emails and making sure everything goes through on time. Plus, I can keep track of who’s RSVP’d.      That would be a big help, sweetheart. I’m so grateful you’re all so organized. I think the Christening is going to be more formal than the birthday, so I wanted to make sure we have the right guests.      Mum, you’re not going to be the only one organizing everything, you know. I can help with the guest list too. Maybe we can split the work? I’ll handle the invitations, and you can focus on the catering and venue details.      That sounds like a plan. I’ll start sending out the invitations first thing tomorrow. Oh, and I need to check with the church about the schedule. The priest said they’re happy with the date, but I need to go over the details again.      I can help you with that too. I’ll go with you to the church if you want. It’s only a few minutes away, and I’d like to see the place where the Christening will take place.

You know, I’ve been thinking about our holiday to New York. It’s been a while since we went on that trip after my sister’s wedding.      Yes, that was such a good time. Remember when we got lost in Manhattan and ended up at that little café on the Lower East Side? The coffee was amazing, and the guy behind the counter had the most interesting stories.      Oh, I remember! You were so excited about the stories that you completely forgot about the time. You were supposed to meet us at the hotel, but you were still talking to the barista.      Grandma, can we go to New York too? I want to see the Statue of Liberty and ride the subway!      Of course, sweetheart. We’ll plan something special for you. But first, we need to figure out when we can all go.      I was thinking we could go at the end of July. My shift at the store is pretty light then, and I’ve got some vacation days coming.      That sounds good. I’ll check with my colleagues to see if they can cover my workload. And I’ll confirm with my brother-in-law about the hotel.      Can I bring my teddy bear? I want to have it with me the whole time!      Of course, love. You can take all your toys. That’s what holidays are for, right?      Exactly. And we can take some time to relax. I’ve been wanting to try that new café in the city. The reviews were incredible.      I should also check the weather. The forecast shows it might be a bit rainy in July, so we should pack an umbrella.      Look, it’s starting to rain!      Yep, and it’s getting colder too. I think it might be the start of the autumn weather.      Well, that’s a sign that summer is almost over. But it also means that the holidays are right around the corner.      Grandma, I drew a picture of New York! Look, there’s the Empire State Building and the big bridge!      That’s wonderful, sweetheart. You’ll have the best adventure of your life.      And I can’t wait to share those memories with you, love.      I love you, Grandma. I can’t wait for the trip!      We’ll make sure it’s the best trip ever, my darling.      And I’ll even bring some souvenirs for you.

So, I've been trying to get my paperwork sorted for the research grant, but it's been a bit of a nightmare. I mean, the forms just don’t make sense. I think I might have missed something in the submission guidelines.      Oh, I know what you mean. I spent the whole weekend going back and forth with the system. They keep changing the deadlines, and the online portal is constantly crashing. I just wish they’d make it easier for students like us.      It’s frustrating, isn’t it? I called the support line yesterday, and the person I spoke to was really unhelpful. They said I needed to “clarify my application further,” but I already did. I mean, I’ve read the guidelines three times. What more do they want?      That’s exactly the problem. It feels like they’re expecting you to interpret the requirements, not just follow them. I remember when I was in my first year, the paperwork was so simple, you didn’t have to think too much. Now, it’s like you need a PhD in bureaucracy just to get a grant.      You’re not wrong. It’s like they’re testing our ability to navigate the system, not our actual research. I think the best thing you can do is just keep checking the guidelines again. Maybe break it down into sections and make sure each part is covered. Also, maybe ask someone else to review it—like your supervisor or a peer.      Yeah, I was thinking about that. I’ve got a study group meeting tomorrow, and I could definitely use another pair of eyes. I don’t want to waste this opportunity. It’s a big deal for my project.      Definitely. And don’t forget to keep a copy of everything you send. You never know when you might need to prove you did it. Even if they do mess up the process, at least you’ll have the records.      Thanks, mate. That actually helps. I was starting to feel like I was going around in circles. I’ll line up the documents and go through them again today.      No problem. If you need any help with the writing or the formatting, just let me know.

So, I was just thinking about my dream last night. It was weird, honestly. I was in a field, and there were these giant white dogs running around. I didn’t even know I wanted a dog, but I felt this pull toward one. I woke up still thinking about it.      That’s interesting. I had a dream the other day where I was on a beach, and I won the lottery. I remember feeling so relieved, like all my problems were gone. I was just sitting there, counting the money, and it felt so good. But then I woke up and realized it was just a dream.      Oh, I get that. I think dreams are a way for our brains to process things. Maybe my dream about the dogs is linked to this conversation we were having earlier about wanting to get a dog. I’ve been thinking about it for weeks now, you know? I feel like I need one.      Yeah, I’ve been wanting a dog too. I keep telling my brother, “We should get a puppy.” But he says he’s not ready. He’s still working on his thesis, and I don’t want to add another responsibility. But I think I’d love to have a dog. I imagine how it would be to have someone who follows you around all the time.      I think it would be fun. I like animals, especially dogs. I just wish I could talk to them. I mean, I know they can understand some things, but it would be cool if they could talk back.      That would be amazing. I’d love to have a dog that could talk. I mean, I’m a teacher, so I’d have to make sure they didn’t disrupt the class. But still, it would be so much fun. Maybe I could name them after famous authors or something.      You’re not the only one. I was talking to my colleague last week, and he said he’s been dreaming about getting a dog too. He said he used to have one, but he lost it when he moved to a new city. He’s been thinking about it ever since.      I’ve been thinking about it too. I remember when I was at the park with the kids, one of them had a little puppy, and it was so cute. I thought, “I wish I had one.”

So, I just got off the phone with the hospital. They said they managed to get ahold of my uncle and he’s stable. Although, he’s still in A&E, so we’re not out of the woods yet.      That’s good to hear. I hope they’re treating him properly. I mean, he was in a bad accident, wasn’t he? You said he hit his head?      Yeah, he was walking home from the pub and got hit by a car. The guy was drunk, apparently. He’s got a concussion and some bruising, but nothing too serious, apparently. Still, it’s scary to think about.      I know, it’s terrifying. I can’t imagine what it’s like to be in that kind of situation. I mean, I’ve had a few minor injuries, but nothing like that. Wait, did he get taken to the nearest hospital?      Yes, it was a local one. They said they had a specialist on call, so that helped. I’m just worried about the long-term effects. You know, if there’s anything he might be hiding.      I get that. I mean, it’s not just the immediate injury. There’s always the risk of something sneaking up later. Did they run any tests?      They did a CT scan and some blood work. Everything seems okay, but he’s still got a headache and is feeling dizzy. The doctor said it’s just part of the recovery.      Well, that’s a relief. I hope he’s resting properly. Maybe you should have someone stay with him while he recovers. You know, just to keep an eye on him.      I’m thinking about it. My cousin is coming over later, so that’ll help. But I still feel like I should be there more. It’s just the whole thing with work and all.      I understand. You’ve got to balance everything. But don’t push yourself too hard. If you need a hand, just say the word. We’re all here for you.      Thanks, that means a lot. I’m just glad he’s okay. I know how lucky we are. It could’ve been so much worse.      Absolutely. It’s a reminder to stay safe, you know? We can’t take anything for granted.      Yeah, definitely. I’m just hoping he makes a full recovery. I can’t imagine going through that without him.

So, I've been thinking about starting a small business. You know, something that combines my teaching experience with a bit of practicality. Maybe a tutoring service for kids, but not just the usual stuff. I thought about offering mentoring to young entrepreneurs, like a sort of after-school program.      That sounds interesting, mate. I mean, I’ve always thought about starting something like that. You’ve got the education, and you’ve got the social connections. But you’d need to get the right people involved. You’d have to think about how you’d market it, and how you’d keep the kids engaged.      Exactly, and I was thinking of using some of the tech that kids are used to. Like, an app or a website where they can log their progress, set goals, and even get feedback in real-time. But then again, it’s a bit of a long shot, isn’t it? I mean, with all the competition out there.      Not necessarily. You’ve got a unique angle. You’re not just teaching them facts—you’re helping them develop skills. And with the way the world is moving, creativity and problem-solving are more important than ever. Plus, you’ve got the contacts. I remember when you used to run that after-school club back in Brighton. The kids loved it.      Yeah, I know. And I still have a few contacts from back then. Maybe I can reach out to some of them. Oh, and I’ve been keeping up with the news lately. You know, the international stuff. It’s a bit of a mess, but there’s been some interesting developments.      Tell me about it. I’ve been watching the tech sector, and it’s really changing fast. There’s this new initiative in London about upskilling young people in digital skills. It’s a government-funded program, but they’re looking for partners. Maybe you could tie into that. You’d get funding, support, and a ready-made audience.      That’s good to hear. I’ve been thinking about how to make this sustainable. It can’t just be a one-off thing. I need a plan, a team, and some resources. I’ve been talking to my friend Dave about it. He’s got a bit of a knack for digital stuff, and he’s been looking for a project to get back into.

So, I was just thinking, we need to get a proper meal before we head back. I’m starving, and the pub’s menu is a bit confusing. Do you know what’s recommended here?      Yeah, honestly, I’ve had it before. The fish and chips are decent, but I’d say the steak and kidney pie is the real winner. It’s hearty and perfect for an evening like this. A bit too rich for some, but I’m not one to complain.      That sounds good. I was going to go for the fish, but I’m not sure if they use frozen stuff. Maybe I’ll just go with the pie. What about you?      I’ll go with the pie. I’m still recovering from the week, and I need something substantial. You know, I was just thinking about the Happy Valley show—did you watch the last episode?      I did! I found it so compelling. The way they portrayed the relationships and the dynamics in the workplace was spot on. I mean, isn’t it funny how the characters are so much like us? I can’t get over the way the cat kept appearing in the background. It was like a character in its own right.      Absolutely. I think the cat is a metaphor for the estate itself, you know? It’s always lurking around, watching everything. I’ve been telling my sister about it. She’s a fan, and she’s planning to catch up on the series this weekend.      That’s a good idea. She’s been meaning to watch it for ages. Speaking of which, I was looking at the décor of the pub today. The owners must have a real eye for design. The walls are lined with local artwork, and the lighting is so warm.      Definitely. I think it’s one of the best pubs in Woolwich. The owner’s got a real passion for history. He told me about how this place used to be a meeting point for soldiers before the war. It’s a shame you can’t really see the past anymore, but the atmosphere still feels like it’s holding on to some of that.      It’s amazing how places like this can still tell a story. I think the coat by the entrance is really on point too. It’s not just a coat—it’s a statement.

So, what’s the deal with that weather we had last week, eh? I swear, it was like a giant kid throwing a tantrum. One minute it’s sunny, the next it’s pouring like a waterfall.      Aye, that’s the kind of weather we get in Edinburgh, isn’t it? One minute you’re sippin’ a dram on the patio, and the next, you’re shivering under a blanket. I tried to take some photos of the castle the other day, but the sky was so grey, it looked like it was crying.      Aye, I remember that. You know, I was out hiking on Arthur’s Seat with a few lads, and the sky turned black real quick. We had to take shelter under a tree. It was like the heavens were about to open up. I’ve never seen such a dramatic shift in weather like that.      That’s the thing about Scotland. You can’t predict the weather, and that’s part of the charm. I’ve been trying to get into photography for a while now. It’s a hobby of mine, actually. I’ve got a camera that I picked up secondhand, and I’ve been snapping shots of the city at different times of the day.      Really? What kind of shots are you takin’? I’ve always wanted to get into it, but I just don’t have the patience. I’ve got a friend who’s into it, and he said it’s like looking at the world through a different lens.      It is, honestly. I’ve been taking a lot of street photos lately, especially around the Old Town. The light there is just magical in the early morning. I even snapped a few shots of the castle reflected in the waters of the river. It was like a dream.      That sounds amazing. Do you ever get disappointed when the weather isn’t co-operative? I mean, if you’re out taking photos, you’d want the skies to be clear.      Truth be told, I’ve learned to embrace the weather. If it’s overcast, I’ll just take some indoor shots or focus on the details. Photography’s all about perspective, isn’t it? You can make the most of any situation.      Aye, that’s a fair point. I suppose that’s why we Scots are so adaptable. We’ve been through more weather changes than most people.

Okay, I've got a few things to do this week. I was thinking about the nursery arrangements—do you have a plan for next week? I need to make sure everything's sorted before the baby arrives.      Honestly, I’ve been a bit overwhelmed with it all. I’ve been trying to contact the nursery a few times, but they’re always on hold. I was going to go in person tomorrow, but I’m worried about the waiting time. Oh, and I was supposed to meet with the midwife on Tuesday, but I haven’t confirmed the time yet.      You should definitely go in person. I know it’s a bit nerve-wracking, but they’ll be able to help you get everything set up. I can come with you if you want. You don’t have to do this alone.      That would be great. I’d feel more comfortable if you were there. I’ve been so stressed about the baby coming and not knowing what to expect. I mean, I’ve read all the books, but nothing prepares you for the real thing.      I know what you mean. I remember when I was pregnant with you, I was so anxious. But it’s all part of the journey. Speaking of which, have you been looking at baby names yet? I heard you were considering something with a nature theme.      Oh, yeah, I’ve been thinking about it. I love the idea of a nature-themed name. Maybe something like Willow or Ash? I like the idea of something meaningful. Also, I was thinking about starting a baby journal. Do you think that’s a good idea?      Absolutely. A baby journal is such a lovely way to document everything. I still have mine from when you were born. I can show it to you sometime. Oh, and I’ve been watching some baby shows on TV lately. I think the one about parenting in lockdown is really insightful.      I’ve been meaning to watch that. I’ve been too busy with work to sit down and relax. I’ve been trying to balance teaching and preparing for the baby. It’s been exhausting, but I know it’s worth it.      You’re doing amazing. I’m so proud of you. Let’s make sure we take some time for ourselves this week. Maybe we can go for a walk or something.

So, I just got a text from my sister saying her new dress is so tight it’s making her feel like she’s got a corset on! I don’t know how she manages to walk in that thing.      Oh, I’ve seen that kind of thing before. My cousin got one of those “statement” dresses for her wedding, and she said it was like wearing a sandwich press.      I know what you mean. My mum was obsessed with that “slimming” dress she bought online last year. She wore it to a family dinner, and I swear, the whole table was looking at her like she’d been turned into a stick figure.      I’m not sure about that. But I do think clothes can really affect how we feel about ourselves. I’ve been trying to get into more casual workwear this year. Less formal stuff, more comfort.      Yeah, I get that. I’m still in a labourer job, so I need to be practical. But I’ve been trying to dress a bit smarter for when I go out with friends. It’s a bit of a struggle.      Mate, you don’t need to dress smarter. Just be yourself. I mean, I’m in a production controller role, and I’ve been working from home a lot. I wear what I want, and I don’t get judged.      I guess that’s the thing—different jobs have different expectations. I’ve got a conference and events job, so I do have to dress a bit more professionally. But sometimes I just want to wear my old jeans and a hoodie.      I get it. I mean, I’ve got a girlfriend, and she says I need to “dress up” for dates. But honestly, I don’t think a suit makes me any more attractive.      Yeah, and I’ve seen how some people go all out for a date and still end up looking like they’ve been dragged through a washing machine.      True. I think it’s more about confidence than clothing. I mean, even in my job, I dress smartly, but I feel most at home when I’m in something I’ve made or bought second-hand.      That’s a good point. I’ve been trying to buy more sustainable stuff, even if it’s not the most fashionable.      You’re lucky, you’ve got a graduate degree.

Well, I’ve been trying to get that old tea set out of the cupboard for ages, but I can’t seem to find the right tea. I think it’s been in there since the 70s, for goodness’ sake!      Oh, I know what you mean. I’ve got a cup of tea in my cupboards that’s been there since I was a child. I think it’s still got a few leaves in it. It’s like a time capsule!      You know, I remember my mother used to make this really strong black tea with a bit of milk and a splash of brandy. It was like a ritual. Every afternoon, after school, it was tea time. I can still taste it in my head.      Oh, I remember that too. My gran used to make a pot that could fill half the kitchen. She’d say, “If you want to keep your bones strong, you’ve got to drink your tea, love.” I used to think she was a bit eccentric, but now I see the wisdom in it.      I think the best tea is always the one you brew in a proper teapot. I remember my nan had one with a little porcelain handle, and it was like a treasure. I still have it, actually. It’s been in the attic for years, but I might bring it down for a bit.      That sounds like a real treasure. I remember my mum had a china teapot too, but it got broken in a fall. I still feel awful about it. I had to buy a plastic one after that. No touch of elegance, I’m afraid.      I think the key is to have a good cup of tea. It doesn’t have to be fancy, but it has to be warm. A bit of conversation, a bit of time. That’s what makes tea special, isn’t it?      Absolutely. It’s not just about the tea itself, it’s about the company. I’ve always found that when you’re with the right people, even a simple cup of tea becomes a celebration.      I suppose that’s the beauty of it. It brings people together, doesn’t it? No matter how old we are, we can still find joy in a cup of tea.      And it’s always a good excuse to sit down and chat. I mean, what else are we going to do?

So, I was at the pub last night, and this guy was talking about his kid’s circumcision. I nearly choked on my pint. I said, “That’s a sensitive topic, isn’t it?” He said, “Oh, it’s a cultural thing. We do it in our family, and it’s normal.” I just stared at him. I mean, I’ve never heard of a Brit doing that. I thought it was more of a Middle Eastern thing.      Yeah, I’ve heard of it too. But it’s still so strange. I mean, I’ve got a brother who’s a doctor, and he said it’s only done in some cultures now. My mum still talks about how she watched her brother’s circumcision when she was a kid. It was like a big family event.      Yeah, it’s weird, but I guess it’s a part of culture for some people. I mean, I’ve never thought about it much, but I can see the importance of it for families who follow certain traditions. Though I still can’t wrap my head around it.      Honestly, I’ve never even thought about it. I mean, when I was growing up in London, we never talked about it. My parents were very modest, and they never brought it up. It’s not something you discuss at dinner.      I suppose that’s the thing about London—everything’s a bit more reserved. But then again, I think some people still do it. I mean, I’ve heard of some friends who’ve had it done, but it’s not about to happen to me.      I think you’re safe. I know that my ex had a kid, and he was against it entirely. My sister-in-law tried to convince him, but he just said, “No way. I’m not getting involved in any of that.”      Sounds like a good stance. I mean, as long as people are informed and it’s done safely, I guess. But I can’t imagine having to do that to my kid.      Exactly. I think it’s a personal choice, but I just can’t see myself being part of it. I mean, I’ve had some weird family traditions, but that’s one I won’t be embracing.      To not having to have a circumcision, then.      To that.      And to not having to explain it to anyone.

Hey, you're back early! I thought you were going to be away for another week. Did you have a good time?      Yeah, it was actually pretty chill. I didn’t do much except relax and catch up with some old friends. Just like you said, it was a real break.      I know, I was so jealous. I’ve been stuck here with all these chores and work deadlines. I feel like I haven’t even had a proper weekend.      I know, I get it. You’ve been working your head off, haven’t you? I mean, I saw you yesterday when you were in the kitchen. You were like a robot, just moving from one task to another.      Oh, you saw that? I was just trying to get the house in order before the weekend. But honestly, I’m tired of the same old routine. I miss the days when we used to cook together and just have fun.      I miss that too. It’s funny how the things you take for granted can be the most important. Anyway, did you hear from Jess last week? I think she still has that ex from university.      Yeah, she mentioned him a couple of times. I think he still calls her, even though she’s moved on. It’s annoying, honestly. You know how she is—she’s always saying how much she’s grown, but she still lingers on the past.      I know, but I think she’s just trying to get over it. I mean, she’s a mental health nurse, so she knows a lot about overcoming things. I think she’s just using the job to help herself.      That’s true. I guess she’s got a lot on her plate. Speaking of which, do you have any plans for the weekend?      I was thinking of going to the park. It’s been way too long since I’ve just sat out there and had a picnic. Maybe we could go together?      That sounds like a plan. I’d love to get out of this house for a bit. I’ve been so cooped up. I’ll check my schedule and let you know.      Great. And while we’re at it, can we maybe cook something together? I’ve been craving Thai food, and I think you’d be great at stir-frying.      Only if you promise to not burn the noodles again.

So, I just heard from Helen yesterday. She’s really struggling. The cancer has spread again, and they’re talking about more aggressive treatment. It’s so hard to watch, you know?      I know, it’s heartbreaking. I saw her at the café last week, and she looked so tired. She tried to make small talk, but it was obvious she wasn’t feeling well.      Yeah, and she’s been so positive, but I can tell she’s scared. She mentioned she’s considering moving to the countryside for a while, just to be closer to family and have a calmer environment.      That makes sense. I’ve been thinking about buying a place in the village too. The houses for sale are starting to look more appealing. I mean, the one near the woods is beautiful, but the planning process is taking forever.      I know, it’s so frustrating. There’s so much talk about sustainable development and preserving the village character, but it’s hard to get anything done. I heard the council is considering a new housing development, which might affect some of the older properties.      Exactly. It’s a real dilemma. On one hand, we need more housing, especially with the demand from people like us who are moving out of the city. On the other, we don’t want to lose the community feel of the place. It’s a tightrope walk.      I agree. I was just at the local market and overheard a few people talking about how the village is changing. Some are happy with the new businesses, while others feel it’s becoming too commercialized.      I’ve been thinking about buying a small cottage, maybe something that’s been standing for a few generations. There’s a place on the edge of the village that’s been listed as for sale. It’s a bit run-down, but the land is beautiful.      That sounds like it could work. It might be a good opportunity to invest, but I’d want to make sure it’s a sustainable choice. I’ve seen so many people take on properties without thinking long-term.      True. I’d like to be careful. I’ve been looking into the planning details, and it seems like there are some restrictions on renovations, especially if it’s a listed building. But the location is worth it.      I can see why. If we ever manage to get out of the city, maybe we could help Helen out too.

So, I've been thinking, do you ever just get fed up with the same old stuff? Like, I don’t know, the way the maintenance here is handled. It's like we’re just a bunch of thrown-together students with no real support.      Oh yeah, I'm with you on that. I mean, I get paid to be here, but it feels like I'm just constantly fixing stuff. The heating in this block is a joke. Last week, I had to crawl under the floorboards to fix a pipe and it was freezing.      Come on, I’ve seen you doing that. You’re like the superhero of this place. But seriously, I’m tired of being the one who has to deal with broken locks, water leaks, and the fact that the bin bins are always full. It’s like we’re managing a hotel, not a place where students are supposed to live.      And don’t even get me started on the noise. I mean, I know it’s college, but some people think it’s their personal nightclub. I had to call the police last week because two guys were yelling in the corridor at 2 a.m. I was just on my way to bed.      That’s not even the worst of it. I’ve had to take reports from students who are justifiably upset about the lack of proper lighting in the common areas. And don’t even get me started on the coffee machine. It’s been broken for two months. You’d think they’d at least have a proper espresso machine in a place like this.      And the Wi-Fi? Oh, it’s a joke. I try to work from bed sometimes, and the signal is so weak I can’t even stream a video without it cutting out. I mean, it’s a student residence, not a jungle. Shouldn’t we have basic connectivity?      I know, right? It’s not like we’re not used to being independent. We came here to learn, not to fight off ghosts in the corridors. I just want things to run smoothly sometimes.      Yeah, I get it. I mean, it’s not the end of the world, but it’s exhausting. I just wish we had more respect for the people who are trying to manage this place.      I’m with you. If only we could all just live in peace, without the constant drama and neglect.

So, I was in Antwerp last week, and I ran into this guy from Harlow—wait, you know him? It was this guy I met on the train, and he was totally thrown by my accent. He said, “You sound like you’re from a different county!” I said, “I’m from Gillingham, mate,” and he just stared at me like I’d said something weird.      Oh, I’ve had that before. I was in Brighton once, and a guy from London said, “You sound like you’re from a village!” I said, “I’m from London, actually,” and he said, “No, you sound like you’re from Essex.” I just laughed and left it at that. People always think we’re all the same, but there’s so much regional variation.      Yeah, I’ve noticed that too. I work with a bunch of people from different parts of England, and we all have our own quirks. I mean, I grew up in Harlow, and I swear I still say “chips” instead of “fries.” It’s like a badge of honor, isn’t it?      Exactly! I remember when I was in Germany, and I was trying to order a coffee, and I said, “Ich will einen Kaffee.” The barista just looked confused. Then I said, “I’m from England,” and she said, “Oh, you’re from the south?” I said, “Gillingham, Kent,” and she said, “Oh, I’ve been to Herne Bay. That’s where I used to go for shopping.” I about fell out of my chair.      I remember a time when I was in France, and I told a waiter I was from London, and he said, “You sound like someone from the North.” I told him I was from London, and he said, “No, you’re from the South.” I just said, “Well, I’m British, so you can’t tell me anything.” He laughed and said, “Okay, but you still have a strong accent.”      You know, it’s funny how we still have such strong regional identities. My mum used to say, “You’re not from London, you’re from Harlow,” and it was like she was trying to make me feel like I was from somewhere else. But I like it. It’s part of who I am.      I feel the same way. I was raised in Gillingham, and even though I’ve been to so many places, I still have that accent, that way of speaking.

Hey, you remember that equality vote coming up? I’ve been thinking about it a lot since the news came out. I mean, it’s about equal rights for both genders in the workplace, right?      Yeah, I read about it. It’s been on my mind too. I mean, I know it’s a big deal, but I feel like people are still figuring out what it really means. I’ve been reading some stuff online, and it’s kind of confusing. It’s not like we’re not equal now, is it?      Well, it’s not just about being equal now—it’s about making sure that laws and policies support that equality in the long run. You know, like making sure men and women get the same pay for the same work. I think it’s important, especially for women who’ve been stuck in lower-paying jobs for years.      I get that. But I’ve been thinking, what about in Ireland? People there have different opinions on this, right? Some say it’s a step forward, others say it’s unnecessary. I mean, I know some of my friends up north have different views. What do you think, though? Should we be voting for it?      Honestly, I think we should. It’s about fairness. Plus, I’ve heard that some countries have already done this, and it’s helped make workplaces more inclusive. I don’t know what it’ll do for the future, but I think it’s worth supporting.      Well, I can see your point. I guess I’m just not sure about how it’ll affect everyday people like us. I mean, I’ve been out of the workforce for a while, but I still want to see things change for the better. I just hope it doesn’t make things worse for people like me who are trying to get back on their feet.      I get that. It’s not about changing things overnight, but making sure that people have the same opportunities. You know, like when I was in school, there were a lot of stereotypes about what girls could do. I always thought it was unfair. I mean, I was just trying to play football, and people would say, “You’re too girly for that!”      Oh no, that’s messed up. I remember my brother saying that to me once too. I mean, it’s one thing to have opinions, but it’s another to enforce them like that.

You know, I was talkin’ to the bloke from the corner shop the other day, and he was chatty about lathe tools. He said he used to work in a workshop when he was younger, and he reckons the best tool in the bunch is the centre rest. Says it’s the one that keeps the job steady if you’re not careful.      That sounds familiar. I remember my dad used to work in a machine shop back in the day. He always said the centre rest was the one that kept the lathe from wobblin’ out of control. But I reckon he was just trying to sound like he knew what he was talkin’ about.      You’re both missing the point. The lathe tools—remember? We had an old one at the flat when we were kids, and it was always falling apart. Mum kept trying to fix it, but it was just a disaster waiting to happen. I think the real problem was the microwaved hamster.      Oh, that’s a good one. I still remember the day we tried to cook the hamster. It was a mistake, of course. We thought it was a snack. Turns out, the poor thing was just trying to survive in a microwave.      You know what I remember about that? The smell. There was this funny combination of chicken and something else. I still can’t get it out of my head.      I’m not sure if that’s a smell or a memory. I think it’s more like a nightmare. But the thing is, we were all trying to be helpful. We thought it was a good idea.      Yeah, but we were all in our twenties then. We had more energy and less sense. You know, I was thinking the other day about how we used to cook things in the microwave all the time. Now, I just stick to the oven.      I do the same. The microwave’s a bit of a gimmick, really. It’s not bad for quick snacks, but you can’t trust it for much else.      I disagree. I think the microwave is a marvel of modern technology. It’s fast, efficient, and I’ve seen some really strange things happen in there. Like, once I tried to reheat a cooked chicken and it came out like a balloon.      Oh, you’re one to talk. I had a chicken that turned into a weird, crispy mass.

So, I was just thinking about that mirror-writing thing in the paper the other day. You know, like when you write backwards so it looks normal in the mirror. I’ve always thought it was a bit of a neat trick. Do you do that, Denis?      Honestly, I tried once when I was a kid, but I just ended up with a smudge on the page. Though I did hear that some people use it to keep their handwriting secret, like in diaries. It’s interesting how something so simple can be both a puzzle and a privacy tool.      Oh, I’ve seen that in school. My granddaughter used to write in the mirror all the time. It was like a game to her. I remember she used to write her name in reverse and then flip the paper around, pretending it was magical.      It must be a bit of a fun challenge. I wonder if it’s something people still do these days. Though I suppose with technology, it’s not as necessary anymore. I mean, who needs to write backwards when you can just type it?      True, I guess. But I still think it’s a nice little habit, like a mental exercise. Speaking of mental exercises, have you been keeping up with the cryptic crosswords?      Oh, I’ve been doing them every week. They’re a great way to keep my mind sharp. I even joined a local group last year. It’s a bit of a social thing too. We get together once a month and share tips.      That sounds lovely. I used to do crosswords when I was younger, but life got too busy. Though I did just start doing them again. I’m not very good at the cryptic ones, though. Maybe I should try some easier ones to get back into it.      You should. It’s a great way to unwind after work. Speaking of work, have you heard the latest about the banks and all that debt stuff? I read something about how people are still struggling with mortgage payments and rising house prices.      Oh, I heard that too. It’s such a shame. Even with all the talk about economic recovery, it feels like the burden is still on the people. I sometimes think that the real issue is how the system is designed.      I can see that. It’s frustrating when the government talks about recovery, but the average person is still stuck with those bills.

Okay, I've got a new Lego Ninjago set that I just got for the kids. They've been so excited about it. I think they're ready to start building something big.      Cool! I’ve seen those clips online—they look really cool. Are they doing anything special with it?      Yeah, I saw the new character on YouTube. I want to be the one who builds the dragon! I got to be the dragon in Minecraft too, remember?      Oh, right! You were the dragon in that big Minecraft world we built together. That was amazing. I think the kids are going to love the Ninjago set. They’ve been asking about it all week.      I know, I’ve been helping them build some of the smaller pieces. They’re really into assembling the different parts. Do you think they’ll stick with it? I mean, they’ve been on their tablets a lot lately.      I don’t care about the tablet! I want to build the whole thing, and then we can play with it. I think the dragon is going to be the best part.      That’s the spirit. I think it’s good that they’re using their imagination. But I do worry that they’re spending too much time on electronic toys instead of reading.      You're right. I’ve noticed that too. We’ve tried reading together, but they get distracted so easily. Maybe we can mix it up—read a bit, then build, then have a game.      That’s a good idea. I think we can make a schedule. We’ll read for 20 minutes, then build for 20, and then maybe play a game or watch a short video.      Can we watch the Ninjago videos after we build? I want to see how they do the moves.      Of course! I think that’s a great way to combine both activities. It’ll help them understand how the characters move and fight.      I also want to set up a Minecraft world with them. I’ve been thinking about making a really big castle. Maybe we can build it together.      That sounds fantastic. I’ve been meaning to get back into Minecraft. It’s been a while since I’ve played.      You’ll be the king of the castle! I’ll be the dragon again.      Alright, I’ll take that as a compliment. Let’s get started.

So, how was your trip to the Lake District? I’ve been meaning to go for ages, and it’s on my list of places to visit.      Oh, it was absolutely amazing! We stayed in a tiny cottage near Windermere, and the views were just incredible. I think I got more photos than actual memories, but that’s the thing with holidays—there’s so much to take in.      I’m so jealous! I’ve been wanting to go there for months, but I’ve got exams coming up, so I don’t think I’ll make it this year. Maybe next summer?      You should definitely go. It’s like a dreamy place, especially in the fall. The colors are just so vivid, and the air is crisp. But I’d say go before the crowds come in, otherwise it’s a bit of a nightmare.      Yeah, I agree. We had to park an hour away from the lake, and the roads were so packed. But it was worth it—especially when we got there and had that quiet moment by the water.      I remember when I was younger, we used to go on mini trips to the countryside with our grandparents. It was like a ritual. We’d always end up with mud on our shoes and a huge appetite.      Oh, those were the days. I miss that sense of adventure, even if it was just a day trip. I think I need to plan a little getaway soon. Maybe a weekend with just the girls?      That sounds great! I’d love to join. We could go to somewhere like Keswick or even the Peak District. I’m sure we’d have a great time.      I’d love that. I could use a break from studying, even if it’s just for a couple of days. Do you think you could take me? I’ll help with the planning!      Sounds like a plan. I’ll start looking into some places. Also, we should probably take some photos this time—no more just taking pictures of the views. We need to capture the moments, like the ones we had in the Lake District.      And maybe we could even do a little hiking? I’ve always wanted to try the hikes around the lake. It’s a nice way to get some exercise and enjoy the scenery.      I’m up for that.

So, I just got this sandwich from the café, and it’s the best thing since sliced bread. You guys tried the new falafel wrap? It’s actually really good.      Yeah, I did. It’s not the best thing since sliced bread, but it’s decent. I mean, the falafel was a bit on the spicy side, but I’m used to that.      Honestly, I’d rather just grab a burger. I don’t know, I think it’s just me. I like the simplicity of a burger. But I did try the falafel, and it was okay. Not bad for a shopping centre sandwich.      You’re missing out, though. I’ve been eating these all week. I think the guy who makes them is like a pastry chef. I mean, the bread is fresh, and the hummus is amazing. Wait, did you guys hear about the new military exhibit at the museum?      Yeah, I saw the poster. It’s about the history of the British Army, right?
