I think it’d be a nice touch.      Yeah, I think that’s a great idea. We should also think about some Christmas lights. I saw these really cool ones at the shop the other day.      I like that. It’d really make the place feel festive. Oh, and we could do a little food stall in the café, selling Christmas treats and cookies.      I love it. It’ll be like a mini food market, and people can come in and get all their Christmas fix in one place.      Right, and we can even host a little Christmas party there. It’d be like a mini Christmas market with food, drinks, and music.      We might have to start planning this now.

So, do you think we’ll ever get back to London? It feels like it’s been ages since we left. I can’t wait to see the city again. I’ve missed it.      It’s not that long, really. Just a few more hours. And honestly, I’ve missed it too. The pace, the chaos, the smell of the streets. It’s like a homecoming.      Yeah, and I’ve been thinking about the future lately. You know, like, what’s next? I’ve got this thesis to finish, and after that, I’m not sure if I want to stay in Cambridge or go back to London. Maybe even Oxford?      Oxford is a great place, but it’s a big step. You need to think about what you want in life. Are you looking for a job, or are you looking for a place that suits your personality?      I don’t know. I guess part of me wants to stay close to the university, but I also miss the city. I feel like I’m not growing if I stay in Cambridge. I need something new, something different.      I understand. It’s natural to feel that way. But remember, no matter where you go, you carry the people you love with you. London might be a big place, but it’s also full of opportunities. And you’ve got your own mind, your own drive. Don’t let anyone tell you what you should do.      Thanks, Mum. I know you’re trying to help. It’s just… it’s easier to think about staying than moving. What if I don’t get a job there? What if I end up back here?      You’ll always have a place here. I’ll always be here waiting for you. But don’t forget, life isn’t just about where you live—it’s about what you do with your time. If you go to London, you’ll have the chance to travel, meet new people, and go to all those places you’ve always wanted to see.      You always know how to talk me into something. But seriously, you think I should go?      I think you should choose what makes you happy. Just don’t forget where you came from. We’ll still be here when you’re ready to come back.      Yeah, you’re right. I’ll think about it. Maybe I’ll even try to find an apartment in London.

So, I heard you two are both in the language research field. That’s interesting. I work as a Language Research Co-ordinator, so I guess we're kind of in the same boat.      Yeah, I do too, but in a more administrative role. I’m a Language Research Administrator. I find it fascinating how the language research community is so diverse. I mean, we come from all walks of life, but we’re all tied together by our love for language.      That’s true. It’s amazing how language shapes our understanding of the world. I often think about how dialects and accents reflect our histories and identities. I was born in Aylesbury, Buckinghamshire, and I still hear the Eastern English dialect in my speech. It’s like a part of me.      I’ve heard that the Eastern English dialect is very distinct. I’m from Oswestry, Shropshire, so I grew up with a very different accent. I remember as a child, my mother would say I had the “Yorkshire twang,” which I found amusing.      Oh, I’ve heard that too! It’s funny how people misinterpret accents, especially as we get older and our speech patterns change.      Exactly. I actually lecture on language and culture at the university, so I get to explore these kinds of topics in depth. One of my favorite topics is the influence of history and travel on language. I’ve travelled quite a bit, especially in the Middle East.      That’s so interesting. I’ve always been fascinated by Arab culture and history. I’m currently working on a research project about the linguistic evolution of Arabic, and I’m trying to understand how it’s been shaped by trade and migration.      That sounds like a fantastic project. I’ve always found the intersection of language and history compelling. I’ve also been learning some Chinese, and it’s taught me so much about how language can reflect a culture’s values and structure.      I think learning a new language is one of the best ways to truly understand a culture. I’ve been meaning to learn Mandarin for years, but I’ve always found it a bit overwhelming.      It’s challenging, but rewarding. I’ve been studying it for two years now, and it’s helped me understand more about the history and traditions of China.      That’s amazing. I’ve also been interested in archaeology and how it connects with linguistics.

So, I just saw this viral video about a kid who’s dyslexic and ended up starting a YouTube channel where he explains concepts in a way that makes sense to him. It’s crazy how that’s blowing up. You ever seen it?      Yeah, I saw it too. I mean, it’s impressive, but I still think there’s a lot of stigma around dyslexia. A lot of people still don’t understand that it’s not just about reading backwards. It’s a learning difference, not a lack of intelligence.      Exactly. And I think that’s why it’s so important for young people to be exposed to stories like that. When I was in school, no one ever talked about it. I just kept my head down and tried to pass. But now, with the internet, there's so much more awareness.      That’s true. And I think part of the problem is class. A lot of dyslexia cases go unnoticed in lower socio-economic groups, where education isn’t always prioritized. I’ve worked with a few kids from the inner city who had severe dyslexia but never got the support they needed because their parents didn’t know where to turn.      It’s such a shame. I mean, I remember my first year of university. I was struggling with all the reading, and I thought I was just bad at it. Then I got diagnosed with dyslexia and everything clicked. It was like a weight was lifted.      That’s exactly the kind of story we need more of. I had a kid at my bakery the other day who was having trouble reading the recipes. I asked if he needed help, and he said he couldn’t read the handwriting. I told him I’d help him out. Maybe that’s part of the solution—small acts of support can make a big difference.      You’re right. And I think part of the issue is how we structure education. If we assume that everyone learns the same way, we’re missing out on so many people. As a café owner, I’ve seen how different learning styles affect people’s ability to work with customers or manage the business. Some people just don’t fit into the traditional mold.      Exactly. And it’s not just about education. It’s about recognizing that in the workplace, too.

So, I've been thinking about our health insurance again. I mean, it's been a bit of a mess lately. I had to cancel the last renewal because I couldn't cover the premium, and now we’re stuck with this new plan that doesn't cover as much.      I know, it’s been a nightmare. I was just saying to someone yesterday that I can’t believe how much it's gone up. I mean, we’re both lecturers, we’re not exactly in a financial crisis, but this is just ridiculous.      Exactly. And don’t get me started on the NHS. I had a minor issue with my knee last week, and it took me like three weeks to get an appointment. I mean, I’m not even sure if I’m going to go through with it anymore. I’m thinking of going private.      I’d do it too if I had the money. But I can’t afford it. I keep telling myself that we’ll get through this, but the cost of living is just too high. I mean, even the basics are going up.      I know, and it’s not just us. I was talking to a colleague the other day, and she was saying the same thing. We’re all in the same boat, but still, it feels like we’re sinking. I feel like we're not making enough for the life we're trying to build.      It’s not just about money, though. It’s about the stress. Every time I look at the bills, I just feel so overwhelmed. I feel like I’m constantly trying to make up for the fact that we’re not on the same financial level as people our age.      Yeah, and politics isn’t helping. I mean, the government keeps talking about helping people, but the reality is that nothing is being done. It’s like they’re ignoring us. I feel like we’re getting the short end of the stick.      I couldn’t agree more. I was watching that TV show the other day, and the host was talking about the financial struggles of professionals, and it hit home. I mean, we’re not poor, but we’re not making it. I think it’s time we start looking at other options—maybe even a different job, or maybe we should consider moving somewhere cheaper?

Well, I've just made some proper Sunday roast, and I thought we’d all take a break and have a chat. I’ve been thinking about how things have changed since I was a teacher. Back then, we used to have proper class discussions, and the children would actually listen. Now, it’s all on screens and social media.      I know, it’s crazy how fast everything has changed. I still remember when I was a kid, we had to wait for the TV to come on every Saturday night. Now, I can watch a film on my phone while I’m walking to work. It’s amazing, but also a bit overwhelming.      I’ve noticed that too. My wife still insists on having the radio on during meals, like back in the day. I think it’s a bit of a holdover from when we were young. But I’ve got to admit, I do miss the old days when people actually talked to each other instead of being on their phones.      Oh, I know what you mean. Last week, I was out for a walk, and I saw a group of young people all huddled around a bench, all on their phones. Not a single person was talking to anyone. It’s heartbreaking. I mean, we used to have proper conversations at the park, and now it’s all about the next TikTok trend.      I was just thinking about that the other day. I was helping a colleague with some scientific research, and she mentioned how even in the lab, people are glued to their screens. They’d rather watch a documentary than actually talk about their work. It’s like we’ve lost the art of discussion.      I think it’s all about the Internet. It’s made things so much easier, but it’s also made people more isolated. I remember when I was teaching, I used to encourage students to write essays and debate points. Now, they just want to know what the ‘popular’ opinion is.      Exactly. I remember being a kid and having to write essays by hand. It was a proper effort. Now, you can just type it up and send it in a minute. I think it’s a shame that the process has become so quick.      And think about the holidays. I remember when we used to go on big family trips, and everyone had to bring something.

So, I was just telling my dad about the game I made with the soft toys last night. I told him it was like a superhero mission. I had this stuffed bear as my sidekick and a teddy bear as the enemy.      Sounds like you've got the whole Avengers storyline down, mate. What was the mission?      Well, I had to save the teddy bear from the villain, who was a giant dump truck. I used the bear to block the truck's path, and then I launched the teddy bear with a pillow as a catapult!      That sounds like a proper action movie! I remember when I was your age, I used to build forts out of blankets and cardboard boxes. My brother and I had an entire kingdom in the living room.      Yeah, I used to do that too. I remember once we built a castle out of pillows and a curtain. It was so elaborate—there was even a moat!      You’re like a movie director, Dad. I wish I had a camera to record all of this. Maybe then I could show it to my friends at school.      You know, maybe you could start a little playroom for the toddler. You could teach him the basics of storytelling and pretend play.      Yeah, he’s got a good imagination already. I saw him yesterday trying to build a tower with his toy blocks. He was so focused, it was like he was constructing a spaceship.      Oh, I’ve got an idea! Maybe we can make a game where we all play together. You could be the captain, and I can be the commander. And the toddler can be our robot.      Alright, but only if we can agree on the mission. Should we save the world or just find a lost teddy?      We should go with the lost teddy. It’s a classic. That way, we can all get involved.      Yeah, and we can include the toddler in the team. He’s already got some of the toys.      Alright, team, let’s start planning. We’ll need a map, a mission brief, and a few snacks.      And a few soft toys, of course. That’s the real mission.      Yeah, and no spoilers, okay? We want to keep the mystery alive.      Deal. Now, who wants to be the first to find the teddy?      I’ll go. I’ve got experience with missions.

So, I was just telling my wife about the time I tried to cook Christmas dinner and ended up burning the turkey. She said I should’ve stuck to the horses, they’re a lot more reliable.      Oh, I remember when you tried to ride one and ended up falling into the pond. You were soaked and looked like a dachshund. That was the year we had to buy that new car, wasn’t it?      Yeah, and that car was a nightmare. Had to get it serviced three times before Christmas. I was worried it wouldn’t make it. I’d rather drive a horse now.      You know, I think the horses are nicer. They don’t cost as much in petrol, and they don’t get angry if you don’t clean the windscreen. Though I guess they do have that stink when they’re wet.      Yeah, and they definitely have opinions about everything. One time, I was trying to get into the car and it just stood there, staring at me like, “What’s the rush?”      You know, I tried to take a shortcut through the fields last week and my Mate’s car got stuck in the mud. Took three hours to get it out. I nearly had a heart attack.      That’s why you should’ve just taken the car. You know, the one that was properly serviced and didn’t need a €200 oil change every week.      I had to get mine serviced last week too. The mechanic said the engine was about to give up the ghost. I had to borrow a friend’s car to get to the Christmas party. I nearly missed it.      What about your boyfriend? I heard he’s got a new job. Is he still with you?      Yeah, he’s been working at the art gallery. He’s helping them set up a new exhibition. It’s all about horses and their art. I think it’s called something like ‘Equine Expressions’.      Horses and art? That sounds interesting. I always thought horses were more about running and eating grass.      Well, I heard they’ve got a sculpture made out of horsehair and paint. It’s supposed to look like a horse that’s been through a lot.      I think it’s a bit like the people in the gallery. Beautiful, but a bit too much for me to handle.

Okay, I’ve got this for your birthday. I couldn’t decide what to get you, so I just bought this whole set of cookbooks. You know, since you always talk about trying new recipes.      Oh, that’s very thoughtful. But I thought you were going to get me a proper gift, not a library of food books! I mean, I already have more cookbooks than a restaurant.      You know what? I think it’s brilliant. You’re always saying how you want to cook more and experiment, and now you’ve got the tools. It’s like a birthday gift that actually helps you achieve something. Plus, you can use them for your next dinner party.      Thanks, Chloe. I thought it was a bit much, but I figured if I ever wanted to cook properly, I’d need to start somewhere. I mean, I’ve got the recipes, but I still need the confidence.      I’ll be the judge of that. You’ll have to cook for me sometime. I’m not going to let you off the hook that easily.      I’ll help you. Let’s make a plan. You pick the recipe, I’ll help you shop, and I’ll be your taste tester. You know, to make sure it doesn’t taste like a disaster.      Oh, please. I’d be fine on my own. I just need a little encouragement. I’ve been meaning to try that risotto recipe from the book you gave me last year. I’ve had it on my list for months.      Well, if you’re going to cook for me, you better make sure it’s good. I have a very discerning palate, you know.      Oh, come on, Mark. You’ve never mentioned your palate being discerning. You just told me once that you love scrambled eggs with ketchup.      Ah yes, the man who married a risk-taker. I think you’re just in denial.      Denial? I’m just honest about my taste. I like simple, reliable food. And I know what I like.      So, what about your plans for the weekend? You said you were going to try that new café in Canterbury. Are you going with someone?      I was going to go alone, but now that you mention it, I might take you. I could use the company, and I could use a bit of motivation to actually go.      That’s a deal.

Well, I've been meaning to ask you all, have you noticed how cold it's been this week? Our heating's been out for days now, and it's just getting worse. I’d say we’re in for a real winter this year, and I bet you’re all shivering like a bunch of old dogs.      Oh, I know what you mean. I’ve been keeping a fire going in the stove, but it’s not much use when the wind comes through the cracks. I think it’s one of those days where you just have to chase the warmth wherever it is. You know, like when you’re trying to find the last bit of heat in the fridge, only it’s not in there at all.      You’re not the only one. I had to call the heating company again last night. The man turned up, checked everything, and then said there was a fault with the main supply. I said, “But this is in a mansion, not a small flat!” He just laughed and said it's the national grid. I reckon we’ll all be wearing hats and scarves by next week.      It’s not just the heating, though. I’ve been thinking about life without power. I mean, it’s not like we’re in a remote village or something. But still, no lights, no TV, no fridge. It’s like living in the Stone Age again. I’d even trade the Big Brother show for a bit of electricity.      Oh, I’ve been watching that show again lately. I can’t get enough of it, honestly. It’s like real life, only more dramatic. I told my wife, "If only I had a million pounds and a setup like that, I’d be watching this from my own compound."      That’s probably the only thing that’s keeping you sane, dear. But I for one am glad we still have the dog. He's been keeping us company, and it's a bit warmer with him around. I think he’s starting to think we’re all his flock.      Aye, he’s a good dog. I told him the other day, “You’d be a good housemate, but you’d have to share the goings-on.” But he just wagged his tail and barked.      You know, I’ve been thinking about getting a new dog.

So, I was just thinking about that film we watched last night,  The Favourite . You remember, the one with the queen and the ladies? I couldn’t stop thinking about how mad it was. Not the actual film, but the things that happened in the royal family.      Yeah, I remember. It was so weird how they just sort of ignored the whole thing. Like, the way the queen treated those women. I mean, was it even real? Or was it just the way the media portrayed it?      It was based on real events, I think. But the film made it feel like a soap opera. It’s wild how much drama was in those times. I can’t believe people actually had to deal with that.      It’s funny, isn’t it? Like, if it was today, they’d probably have a reality show about it. I mean,  The Crown  is like that. All the drama, all the details. It’s like they’re just making a book for TV.      Exactly! But I think it’s good that we get to see these stories through films. It’s a way to learn about history, even if it’s dramatised. Though, I do wonder if some of the stuff is just exaggerated for effect.      I suppose. But hey, it’s entertainment. We’re not historians. Just trying to enjoy a good story. Speaking of stories, did you hear about my aunt’s family? They’re still living in the same house in Lewisham that my great-grandparents bought back in the 1950s.      Oh! That’s amazing. Still in the same house? That must be something to be proud of.      Yeah, it is. My cousin said it’s a bit run down, but they’re fixing it up. You know, making it into a sort of heritage home. They’ve even started telling their stories to local kids.      That’s so cool. I wish my family had something like that. My gran used to tell me stories about Doncaster, but I never really got the chance to see it.      I know. It’s sad when family stories get lost. We should start writing down our family history, don’t you think?      Yeah, maybe. I mean, if we don’t, who will remember? I’ve started thinking about it more, especially since I’ve been working with events. It’s like, you have to remember the past to plan the future.      Exactly.

So, I've been thinking about the referendum again, you know? It's like it's been on everyone's lips these past few weeks. I mean, it's not just something you can ignore, is it? It feels like the whole country's got a stake in it.      Yeah, I guess. I mean, I'm not really sure what it all means, honestly. I know Scotland’s got its own government now, but does that mean it's really independent? It feels a bit like it’s just another political drama, you know?      Well, it's not just about drama, lass. It's about identity, national pride, and the future of Scotland. You know what I mean? I’ve been reading about it for years. The more I think about it, the more I feel like Scotland should be its own country. It's got its own culture, its own history, and even its own football team. What’s the point of being part of the UK if we're not even given a say in the big decisions?      I guess that makes sense. But I’m not really sure how it would work. If they vote to leave, how does that affect people like me? I mean, I'm not from Scotland, but I still feel like I’m part of this country. I mean, I’ve lived in York all my life, and I love it here. I don’t know if I’d miss out on anything if Scotland left.      That’s the thing, though. The UK is a union of nations. England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. It’s not just about independence—it’s about representation. You know, I’ve been an examiner for GCSEs for years, and I’ve seen how the system works. It’s not always fair, and it’s not always representative. Scotland has a lot to say, and they shouldn’t be sidelined just because they happen to be a different country.      I can see that. But I still don’t really know what I think. I mean, I’m not that political, to be honest. I just want to keep living my life and not have to worry about all this stuff. But I guess it’s something that's going to affect everybody, even if we don’t think about it every day.      Exactly. That's why it's so important to have the vote.

So, what do you think about that Jeremy Kyle bit? That bloke with the accent, he’s like a giant boulder in a tea shop!      Yeah, honestly, I don’t know what he’s saying half the time. Oh, I used to think he was just being dramatic, but now I’ve started to think he doesn’t even know what he’s saying.      Wait, I’m not even sure if he’s from York or Leicester or somewhere else. Like the ones from Newcastle or somewhere.      Wait, isn’t he from Liverpool? Or was that just my geography teacher trying to tell me a joke?      No, no, no. He’s got that “t” elision, the way he says “that” like it’s “tha.”      Yeah, and the way he drops the “th” sound. “This” becomes “zis.” It’s like he’s trying to sound posh, but all he does is sound like a misunderstood ganger.      I think he’s trying to be the best on the show, but he’s just so…  distinctive . You know, like if a man with a grudge were to host a chat show.      Oh, I don’t know, I think he’s the one who’s actually funny. He just says things in a way that’s so full of drama, it’s like watching a soap opera without the actual characters.      I’m not sure if he’s joking or if he’s just completely lost. But honestly, it’s like he’s trying to be the only person in the room who’s not from the North.      I think he’s trying to be posh. But he’s just got that accent that says, “I know I’m not from here, and I don’t care.”

Can you believe the way they played that last goal? I swear, if that was a real match, I’d be standing up and cheering louder than my mum at the pub.      Oh, I bet you would. You’re always so passionate about football, even when we’re just watching it on the telly. Remember when we tried to play a game with the kids in the garden last summer?      Oh, don’t start! Yeah, and you were the one who kept saying, “Just keep the ball in the back garden, lads!” You were so into it. I think you even screamed at the cat when it ran off with the ball.      I was only trying to teach them the basics! Anyway, enough about the garden. Have you thought about baby names yet? I know you said you wanted to get serious about it after the Olympics.      Honestly, I still haven’t. I keep thinking about it, but I’m just not sure. I mean, it’s one thing to name a dog, but naming a child is a big deal. Have you thought about any names?      I’ve been toying with a few. Maybe something classic, like Oliver or Emma. But I’ve also been thinking about more unique ones. Maybe something with a meaning behind it.      Oh, that’s a good idea. I was thinking about using a name that has a connection to the Olympics. I’ve been reading about Greek names because of the Games. Maybe something like Nikos or Kora.      Kora? That’s beautiful. I like that. I think it has a nice ring to it. But I’m not sure if I’d stick to one name. Maybe something with a surname too?      Yeah, I think that makes sense. I was also thinking about combining a traditional name with a more modern twist. I mean, if you think about it, the Olympics are all about tradition and progress, right?      Exactly. It’s like the whole idea of the Games—balancing the old with the new. You know, I’ve been knitting a little bit over the last few weeks. I even finished a scarf for my mum.      You? Knitting? I didn’t think you were the type.      Yeah, I know!

So, I just watched  The Bee Movie  again with the kids, and it made me think—what if the Queen had a bee as a sidekick? I mean, imagine the royal bee, buzzing around Buckingham Palace, collecting honey and beeswax. It would be  so  British.      That would be  so  cool! I think the Queen's bees would have a very strict hierarchy, like the royal family itself. The queen bee would be the most powerful, and the worker bees would do all the grinding, like the royal servants.      Yeah, but what if the bees were even more  strict ? I heard once that bees are actually really loyal to their hive. My uncle said if you mess with a hive, the bees will rally together and attack you like a royal guard.      Exactly! And if the bees were part of the royal family, they’d probably have their own titles. Maybe a  Bee Duke  or  Bee Duchess ? They’d definitely have a throne made of honeycomb.      I think the Queen would have a  Royal Bee Garden  with all the best flowers. And the only way to get into it would be to be invited by the Queen herself. You can’t just walk in like a regular person.      Wait, but what if someone wanted to be a bee? Would they have to go through a royal选拔? Like a bee version of the Royal Academy?      Maybe. And if they made it, they’d have to do  a lot  of work—like pollinating flowers and being very polite. I mean, bees are the most organized insects in the world. They even have a  honeycomb schedule .      Wait, isn’t there that movie about King Arthur? I think the bees would side with the good guys. Arthur would be like the  bee king .      Yeah, and if Arthur was a bee, he’d probably have a  honey sword  instead of a sword. Like, a sword made of honey and pollen.      I can see it now— The Bee Movie  and  King Arthur  mixed together. Bees fighting the bad guys, with their queen leading the charge. And at the end, they’d fly away, leaving a trail of honey across the kingdom.      I’d pay to see that. I mean, it’d be like a royal bee garden with a battle scene. And the Queen would be there, pronouncing the bee king as the new ruler of the hive.

So, we've just finished off the last of that bin bag from the tip, and now we’re here for a coffee. I can’t believe how much stuff we’ve gotten rid of. It’s a bit scary, honestly.      I know, it’s a bit overwhelming. I mean, when you’ve lived in one place for so long, it feels like your home is part of you. But I think it’s good that we’re doing it. It’s a fresh start, isn’t it?      Yeah, it’s kind of exciting, even though I’m not sure what’s going to happen next. I mean, we’re not even sure if we’re moving or just clearing out. Well, I hope you do. I’ve always wanted to live by the sea. I remember when I was a kid, I used to play by the water near Kendal. It was like a secret world.      That sounds lovely. I think I’d like that too. Maybe we could go on a little road trip one day and see what’s out there. It’s been ages since we’ve had a proper holiday.      Can I come?

So, I was just thinking about that museum we were supposed to go to last week... You know, the one with the Beatles stuff? I kept putting it off because I couldn’t find a parking space. Not even near the museum, mate. It was like trying to park in a rush-hour tube station.      Yeah, I remember. I told you I’d bring the map, but you were so busy texting your colleague about your upcoming interview for the Masters that you forgot. We ended up walking like two miles just to get in, and by the time we got there, we were both sweaty and exhausted.      Yeah, but it was worth it. That display on the Cavern Club was incredible. Oh, I was just so starstruck. I mean, I’ve read all the books, watched every documentary, and now I’m actually standing where the Beatles first performed. It’s surreal. But I still can’t believe we didn’t find a parking space. I think we’re going to have to invest in a car. I mean, with all the shopping we need to do for Christmas and moving house, it’s not practical to rely on public transport anymore.      Yeah, I hear you. But I’m not sure I’m ready to give up the bike yet. Though, honestly, I might just start looking at cars. Especially if we’re moving in a few months. There’s this one company that offers financing for first-time buyers. I think it’s got some good deals. I’ll send you the link. And speaking of moving, have you sorted the furniture yet?      Not really. I’m still trying to decide where to get the furniture from. I’m not sure if I go for online stores or see if there’s a second-hand shop in town. You know, maybe we can go shopping this weekend and check it out. Maybe even grab a coffee at the café near the museum on the way?

Hey, have you seen the new  Stranger Things  season? I think it’s the best one yet. The episodes are so intense, and the music is  amazing —like, I’ve been playing it on repeat all week.      Yup, I binged it over the weekend. I was so hooked, I didn’t even sleep properly. But honestly, the music is genius. I mean, how do they do that? It’s like it’s from the 80s, but it feels  so  modern.      Exactly! I saw a post on Instagram about how the composer is a massive fan of the 80s. I tried the  Star Wars  series, but I was like, “This is so different from the old movies.”      Oh, I got into the  Star Wars  reboots. I watched  The Mandalorian  last night, and I was like, “This is  so  good—I wish I had a subscription.”      You should get a student discount. I think they have one for uni students. Unless you want to switch places and I can have your pizza?      Deal. But only if you promise to watch  Stranger Things  with me this weekend.      Deal, deal. You’re on. But I’m warning you—once we start, we won’t stop.      You know what they say—once you’re in, you’re in.      Exactly. Now, pass me the pizza. I’m starving.      Not until you promise to take me to that cafe on the corner. They have the best coffee and the best pastries.      You’re on. Let’s make it a night out.

So, what do you think about that new Pokémon game, Oisin? I've been trying to get him to play it, but he keeps saying it's too hard.      I don’t even know what it is! I was just watching my dad play it on his phone. It was all Pokémon and stuff. I wanted to play too, but he said I had to wait until I was older.      Yeah, you’re still too young for the hard stuff, Oisin. But maybe next week? I saw a new game on Steam, and I can show you how to play it.      That sounds good. But first, I need to get you some new clothes for school, love. I saw a sale on skinny jeans at the mall, and they look really cool.      Skinny jeans? I thought we were done with that. You know, you can still wear pants without them being tight.      Oh, come on, Mate. I mean, they’re not that bad. Plus, they’re on sale. You can’t argue with that.      Skinnies? Skinnies?      That’s what they call them, Oisin. You can say “skinny jeans,” just like that.      Skinnies. Skinnies.      There you go. You’re getting it!      Speaking of talking, I saw this cool guitar online. I was thinking maybe I could buy it and learn to play. You wanna come over and try it out?      Are you serious? I’ve been dying to learn how to play the guitar! But I don’t have any money.      Maybe I can get a used one. I’ve been saving up from my allowance.      Pleeze, Pleeze go get it!      I think that’s the first time you’ve used ‘please’ properly, Oisin.      Yeah, I think that’s a step forward.      So, what about the ice cream? We were supposed to go to the new store on Tuesday.      Yeah, I remember. I think it’s a good idea. I’ve been craving some chocolate ice cream.      Ice cream! Ice cream!      That’s right, Oisin. We’re going to get ice cream, and then maybe we can all play Pokémon.      What about the ramen? We were supposed to arrange to meet up?      Oh, right! I completely forgot. I’ll call them tomorrow.      Yeah, don’t worry. We’ll get to that. For now, I think we’ve got our plan for the week.      Skinnies! Skinnies!      Alright, Oisin, let’s just say you’re a work in progress.

So, I was just going through the old cupboard, and I came across this box with a label that said “Gardening Set.” You remember that, don’t you? We had it when we were kids, right? I think it was the one with the tiny trowel and a little watering can.      Oh, yes! I remember that vividly. It was one of those plastic sets from the 70s, wasn’t it? You’d think you were a proper gardener, tending to the plastic flowers and all. I still get a laugh thinking about how serious we were about it.      I know! I used to pretend we were growing marigolds and tomatoes. You remember how we’d set up a little patch in the garden with the sticks and stones, and then I’d try to water it with the little can? It would just sprinkle everywhere.      Oh, you were such a mess! I remember the day we tried to plant the “seeds” in the flowerbed, and you ended up with a puddle of water everywhere. Dad had to come out and save the day. He said, “I thought you were raising vegetables, not a flood!”      That was the day! And then we had this other toy, the Bako building set. Do you remember that? It was those wooden blocks with the colored stickers. We used to build everything from houses to castles.      Oh, yes! You’d spend hours just building and rebuilding. I think you had the most elaborate castle in the neighborhood. I remember you even used the blocks to make a little bridge over a bucket of water.      It was a real engineering feat. I used to say I was going to be an architect when I grew up. Though, in hindsight, I think I realized I was just obsessed with building things.      Well, it did show some talent, didn’t it? I mean, we had to sort out all these boxes and stuff. I was going to throw out the Bako set, but I thought maybe we should keep it. It’s part of our history.      Yeah, I agree. I think it’s more than just toys – they’re memories. You know, even though it’s been years, I can still picture the garden, the way the sun used to shine through the trees, and the way we used those toys to escape reality for a bit.      You’re right.

So, I just got home from the park with the baby. The weather was absolutely perfect — not too hot, and the breeze was just right. It was one of those rare days where the baby actually stayed calm for most of the time. No crying, no fussing — just happy little giggles.      That sounds lovely. It’s like the whole city’s stuck in a loop.      Oh, I know! I was on my way to the park and got stuck in the same traffic. It was so frustrating. I’ve never seen so many cars on the road. I had to park two streets away and walk the rest. It turned out for the best, though — the baby was better off walking than sitting in a car for half an hour.      You’re right — sometimes, the unexpected is the best. I was actually thinking about that earlier. I’ve been feeling a bit burnt out with work and I need to get out more. Maybe I should start going to some music gigs again. I remember you mentioned you saw a gig last week. Was it good?      Oh, it was amazing! It was a local indie band, and they were incredible. Speaking of which, have you noticed any changes in the baby lately?      Oh, you know, they’ve started to notice mosquitoes. I swear, every time we go outside, the baby gets a few bites. I’ve been using this new repellent, but I’m not sure it’s working. I’m worried they might get a bit of a reaction.      I’ve had the same issue. I’ve been putting some kind of baby-safe cream on them before we go out, but it’s not foolproof. I guess we’ll just have to be extra careful. Maybe we can go to the park later this week.

Hey, you've been out all day? I was just about to call you. What did you do?      Yeah, I went to the theatre last night. That new play about ghosts was amazing. You wouldn’t believe the set—like, it felt like you were in a haunted house.      Oh, I heard about that. I actually thought it sounded a bit scary. I’ve got a fear of ghosts, honestly. My mum used to tell me stories as a kid about her old house.      You should’ve come. It’s not that bad. I mean, it’s just a play. But honestly, I got a bit nervous during the second act. I kept glancing at the door.      I’m not even sure I’d go to a play like that. But I was thinking about going to a comedy show next week. You up for it?      Sure, why not? I’ve been meaning to get out more. I’ve been stuck at home a lot lately, just trying to figure out what to do next. I’m still waiting on that graduate job application.      That’s tough. I know how it feels. I got rejected from a few places too. But at least I’ve got my golf tournaments. It’s not the same as having a job, but it keeps me busy.      I guess I should be grateful. I mean, I’m not working, but I’m not starving either. I do have some savings. It’s just hard knowing I’m not being used in the workforce.      It’s not easy. I remember when I was just starting out, I was doing part-time stuff too. But I knew I wanted to be a professional golfer. You just have to keep pushing.      I hope I can find something. I’ve been looking into some recruitment agencies. Maybe I can get some experience.      That’s a good idea. You could even try doing some voluntary work. It’ll look good on your CV.      Yeah, I might do that. I’m just trying to stay positive. I know life has a way of throwing curveballs at you, but you’ve got to keep going.      Absolutely. And hey, if you ever want to go to a show or something, I’m always up for it. You know I’ve got a love for the arts.      Thanks. I’ll keep you posted. I’ve got a feeling this week might be the one where things start moving.

So, what’s with the grumpiness today, Seán? You’ve been more grumpy than a bad day at the office.      I don’t know, Dad. I just had this terrible day at school. The teacher kept calling on me and I couldn’t answer anything.      Oh, you’ve been through so much, haven’t you, sweetheart? You know, I was a student once too. But I had to take care of my sister when I was younger, so I skipped a few grades.      Car! Car!      Yeah, he’s got more energy than the sun at noon. But he’s a joy, isn’t he?      He is. But I wish he’d stop jumping on the couch. It’s giving me a sore back, and I’m already exhausted from school.      I know, love. But maybe we can make a deal. You can do your homework early tonight, and then you can have some extra playtime with him.      That sounds fair. But I’m not sure I can do my homework. I’ve been trying to figure out how to do this algebra problem all day.      You know, when I was your age, I didn’t even know what algebra was. I was out playing football all day.      Yeah, well, I’m not as lucky as you were. I have to do the work now.      I know, love. But you’re doing great. You’re getting to the stage where you’re actually thinking about your education. That’s a good thing.      Yeah, he’s got a bright mind. You just need to stick with it.      I hope so. I just wish the school wasn’t so… boring.      Yeah, I remember when I was your age. I had to sit through classes where the teacher would just read from a textbook all day.      That’s the life of a student. But we had to start somewhere, right?      “Twinkle, twinkle, little star,”      He’s got a voice like a little angel, even if he’s got a little more energy than he should.      Yeah, he’s a rare gem. And you, my love, are going to be a great father one day.      Thanks, Mum. I’ll try my best.      To the future, then.      To the future.      And to Seán, who is already the best little brother in the world.      Car! Car!      Yeah, and to the man who’s more of a toddler than the kid.

So, I just saw ANON walking around the garden in his pants this morning. I almost said something, but then I thought—why not let him be? I mean, it’s a holiday home, and it’s not like we’re expecting any visitors.      Oh, that’s hilarious! I swear, if he doesn’t get dressed within the next hour, I’m going to have to start a new tradition. “ANON’s Pajama Day” or something. It would be like a family thing.      Wait, can I ask—what’s ANON even doing? He’s not  always  like this, is he?      No, he’s fine. It’s just… he’s been sleeping in his pants for the past two days. He says it’s “comfortable” and “familiar.” I’ve tried to explain that when you sleep in your pants, you’re not actually getting any rest. You’re just… oversized pajamas with a hole in the back.      Wait, is he doing that on purpose? I mean, he’s not even trying to hide it.      I think he’s trying to live the dream. He says it’s like “the ultimate relaxation.” I don’t know, maybe he’s just trying to prove a point.      Or he’s just trying to win the ‘most quirky relative’ award. We’re in a competition with our cousins, and he’s leading the way.      I think I’d rather have a nightmare than share a room with him.      That’s not fair. He’s not a nightmare—he’s just… different.      Wait—he’s also been talking about doing a house extension. The whole time he’s been dreaming about a bigger kitchen and a new garden. I’m like, “Why not just rent out the house?” But he says he’s  building  it.      Does he have a plan? I mean, how’s he going to do this?      He says he’s got a Pinterest board. He’s even drawn a blueprint. It’s not bad, honestly. He’s got this idea of a “modern rustic” design.      Oh, I see it now. It’s like a mix of a tiny cabin and a luxury mansion.      I’m not sure I like the idea of a “modern rustic” kitchen. What even is that?      It’s like, a combination of wood and concrete, with a really big island. ANON says he wants to cook on it.      Well, if he wants to cook on it, I say he should start with something simple.

So, I've been thinking about redecorating my flat. I've got this beautiful old chandelier from my grandmother’s house in Cairo—she used to live there before she moved to England. It's this intricate brass thing with all these crystal balls. I’ve been trying to figure out how to display it without it looking too  grand . You know, like, I don’t want it to feel like a museum.      That sounds amazing. I’ve always loved antique pieces. But I know you’re not one for flashy decor. I’ve been trying to decide whether to keep my old Welsh cottage style or go more modern. I mean, I’ve got these lovely stone walls, and I’ve been considering painting them a soft green. You know, like the hills around Tredegar.      Soft green? That’s not a bad idea. I’ve actually been thinking about doing something similar. I’ve got these old pictures from my time in Egypt on the walls—desert scenes and things. Maybe I can frame them in a way that gives a sense of place, like a gallery.      That sounds really special. You know, I’ve been working on a research project on the impact of water companies on rural communities in Wales. It’s a bit of a complex issue, but I’m trying to get funding from the university. I was wondering if you’ve ever considered applying for funding for your own projects?      You know, I actually have. I was just looking at the funding proposals for the Hadron Collider project. It’s oddly similar to some of the administrative challenges we face in academia. I mean, you have to justify the research, get approvals, and then deal with the bureaucracy. It’s frustrating but necessary.      Exactly. I’ve been trying to get some of my colleagues to support me. It’s tough, but I think the idea of linking local water policies to environmental sustainability could resonate well. Speaking of which, have you been to Italy lately? I’ve been trying to get a grant for a trip to study the Renaissance architecture there.      I went to Florence last year. The architecture there is incredible. I took some pictures of the Duomo, and I’ve been trying to incorporate some of the gothic elements into my own research presentation. If I can just get the funding, I’d love to go back.

So, I found these boxes of Lego in the attic this morning, and I couldn’t believe it. I thought maybe it was from when I was a kid, but then I realized it was actually from the kids. I even gave it a name— Star Voyager 3000 !      I made a Ninja Turtle too. I used the green pieces for Michelangelo and the red ones for Raphael.      Oh, you’re both doing so well. Though, if I remember correctly, you used to complain about the colours.      Yeah, I used to say the green ones were too boring. But now I love them.      Speaking of builds, I was just thinking—what do you two think about the new  Harry Potter  movie?      I think it’s amazing! The special effects are so cool. I especially loved the part where the Sorcerer’s Stone was revealed.      Yeah, and I think the new  Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles  movie is even better. The action scenes are so intense.      I’ve been meaning to take you two to see the new  The Simpsons  movie. It’s coming up next week.      Really? I’ve been waiting for that! We could watch it after we finish sorting out all these Lego pieces.      Yeah, let’s do that. But after we finish sorting out the Lego, we can go to the cinema.      Sounds like a plan. I’ll even help you sort the Lego if you promise to help me with the renovations at Granny’s.      Deal! But first, we’ve got to eat that Easter chocolate you found in the cupboard.      Oh, right. I forgot about that. I’ll get it.      I’ll help you, though. I think it’s better than the chocolate we had yesterday.      You’re both eating the wrong kind of chocolate. This is the real stuff.      Well, if it’s the real stuff, then we’re in for a treat!      I’m definitely in for a treat. Let’s get that chocolate and start sorting the Lego.

So, I was just telling my granddaughter about the time her nan tried to fix the plumbing in the old house in Hull. She thought she could do it with a spanner and a bit of grit. Okay, so I was thinking about the films  Pan  and  Peter Pan  the other day. I remember when I was a child, I used to watch  Peter Pan  all the time. It was such a magical story. The other versions are more serious. I remember my dad talking about  Pan  being a darker movie. It’s about Captain Hook, right? And the boy who never grows up.      Exactly! And the movie  Pan  is based on J.M. Barrie’s original story. It’s more complicated, though. There’s a lot about the lost boys and the idea of growing up. It’s not just about flying and fairies. Maybe that’s why it’s still so popular. It’s a story that can be read on so many levels. I think I’ll have to watch the live-action version of  Pan  with you sometime.      You’ll love it, I promise. It’s a beautiful adaptation, even if it’s a bit more intense than the original.

So, we've got about 45 minutes before we get to the airport, and I think we're going to be stuck in traffic again. It's always like this in the mornings, isn't it? You’ve always been resourceful. And besides, you’re not alone in this.

Well, I've been meaning to ask you, have you ever tried a Swedish massage? I had one last year and it was absolutely transformative. I think it’s important that we take care of ourselves, especially when we're older. You learn so much – about people, about the world, and sometimes even about yourself. But I’ve always found it strange how much emphasis is placed on female equality these days. Okay, I've got a list of places I want to visit in France. Let me think... Okay, I was thinking of going to Nice, because I love the sea and the atmosphere there. I just got a new phone, man. You know how much I’ve been trying to get one that doesn’t crash every five minutes. I even went to that shop down the road with the guy who runs the café. You know, I was just thinking about those globes we had when I was a kid. I remember the one that was in my uncle’s house, it was this big round thing with all the countries and everything. Maybe you just didn’t have the right kind of education. I remember the time I was trying to find my way through the Underground in London. I got lost for hours. Maybe I should just book a flight out of the country. I mean, it’s not like we’re in the middle of a crisis.

Okay, I've got the beans boiling, and the veggies are starting to soften. What do you think about the weekend plans? I was thinking maybe we could go to that new café in the town center. Well, I've been thinking about the sea a lot lately. I was out walking by the coast the other day, and it just reminded me of how things used to be. So, I've been thinking about getting a new hairstyle. I've had my current one for ages, and honestly, I feel like it's time for a change. You know, I’ve been thinking about moving out of the city for a while. It’s getting too expensive to live in Liverpool, especially with all the rent hikes. I mean, work is important, but so is life.

So, I just wanted to talk through something with you, Sarah. I know it's been a while since we last caught up, and I’ve been feeling a bit stuck with how things are going at home with the kids.      Oh, I know, Jo. I’ve been meaning to call you too. Things have been… complicated with the toddler. I think I’ve been trying to push too hard for her to be independent, but she’s just so clingy. I think I’ve been trying to be the perfect step-parent. Like, I need to prove that I’m just as good as her mom. But maybe that’s not the way to go? You’re right. I just worry that I’m not giving her enough independence. I don’t want to be the one who’s always holding her hand, you know? It builds confidence.      You’re such a good role model, Jo. I feel like I’ve been so caught up in my own insecurities that I’ve forgotten how to let go. I think I need to start trusting myself more, and then she’ll start trusting me.      That’s exactly it. You’re not just a step-mom — you’re a parent, and that’s all that matters.

So, I just got back from the pub, and I had the best time. We were catching up with some old friends, and it reminded me how much I miss hanging out with them. It’s been ages since we all got together properly.      That sounds great. I’ve been meaning to catch up with some folks too, but with my PhD, it's easy to get lost in work. It’ll be the kind of thing that brings everyone together. I think it’s going to be one of those birthdays that people will remember.      Absolutely. So, I just found this really nice set of vintage light fittings on eBay. They look like they’d go really well in the living room. Agreed. Let’s set a time for the viewing and make sure the lights are in the house before we settle in. It’s going to be a great start to our new chapter.

You know, I’ve been thinking about the job-hunting thing again. It’s been a bit of a struggle lately, especially with the whole NHS funding situation. I feel like I’m not getting the right opportunities.      I know what you mean. So, I read this article today about new research into how to get a good night’s sleep. It’s got me thinking—especially with the camping trip we’re planning next weekend. You know, we’ve been talking about going somewhere remote, and I’m kind of worried about how we’ll manage night time without the usual distractions.      Oh, I’ve heard about that research too. I guess we’re both kind of city tourists at heart. But I’m glad we’re not planning to go to a big city this time. We’re thinking about a place with fewer people and more nature—like a place where you can really feel the stars.      That sounds perfect. So, I was just thinking about that hamster we had in secondary school. Remember when it chewed through the entire box of biscuits and then hid in the toilet?      Oh yeah, I still have nightmares about that. But at least we had a good laugh out of it. You know, I think I still have the photo of it on my phone.      I had a hamster too, but it was a bit more of a diva. It refused to eat anything except the carrots we gave it every day. I swear it had a whole personality.      Yeah, mine was the same. It’d only come out at night and run around the wheel, like it was trying to escape the whole place.      Oh no! Wait, does that mean it was a  ginger  hamster?      No, no, no. That was just the guy who kept trying to tell us we had inappropriate music on.      Oh, I know who you’re talking about. The one who tried to trot out a Beethoven playlist during the national anthem.      That was the best. I still remember him trying to explain why the phone was on the table and not in the hamster’s cage.      You know, I’ve been thinking about gingers lately. Like, is it just me, or do they look like they’re always  trying  to be the most interesting person in the room?      Oh, I’ve seen  so  many gingers trying to be the center of attention. Maybe it’s the hair, like it’s just a warning sign.      No, it’s the  soul . They have this way of just waiting for someone to ask them a question and then they’ll tell you a story that’s 10 minutes long.      Yeah, I’ve had that. My best friend is a ginger, and I swear he once told me a story about his grandfather’s cat that started in 1943 and ended in 2020.      You’re not kidding. I’ve seen that. But honestly, I’ve come to like gingers more now. They’ve got that  wild  energy. Like they’re just waiting for the world to catch up with them.      Yeah, and when they’re not being dramatic, they can be really fun. I mean, I know some gingers who have  truly  amazing taste in music.      Exactly. And once you get past the “I know something you don’t” vibe, they’re actually pretty cool.

So, I've just finished my turn in Risk, and I've managed to take over the entire continent of Africa. I think I'm about to win, but I need to be sure I didn't miss any of the instructions. I've been playing this game since I was a kid, but every time there's a new version, it's like learning it all over again. Do you want me to look up the update version rules to make sure we're not breaking any?      I think the easiest way is to just play it by ear. Besides, the last time you looked up the rules, you ended up stealing all of Europe and left me with just Antarctica. It was a mess.      That was an accident! I was just trying to be strategic. I didn't mean to take over the entire continent. But hey, I've been thinking—what if we decide to play the game with some changes? Maybe we could even include some of the topics we’ve been talking about—like the ones about having children, ethics, and Genghis Khan. It could make the game more personal. I mean, if you’re going to have your own child, you have to think about the risks—like, not just in the game, but in real life.

So, I was just thinking, do you ever feel like university is just this endless loop of essays and lectures? I’m starting to wonder if I’m even on the right path.      I know what you mean. I’m in the same boat. My friend’s dad is a teacher, and he keeps saying he wants me to be one too, but I’ve got this massive crush on the marketing department. I’m like, “Dad, I know you want me to be safe, but I don’t wanna chase a dream that might not even work out.”      That’s the thing, isn’t it? Everyone’s like, “Just follow your passion,” but who even knows what that means? I mean, I like writing, but I don’t even know if I’m good enough.      You’re good enough, just like I’m good enough. We’re both in the same boat, right? I mean, look at that guy from  The Crown —he was like, “I didn’t choose this, I got it by accident.” What’s the point of choosing when you can just stumble into something?      You’re so much more optimistic than me. I’m sitting here, thinking, “What if I end up working at McDonald’s and never even get to use my degree?”      I get it. But you’ve got to think about the long game. I mean, what if you end up working at a café and then realize you love it? You might be happier than someone who’s in a high-paying job but hating every minute of it.      Yeah, that’s true. I just don’t wanna regret not trying. I mean, I’m not even sure what I want to do yet.      You know, I once had a professor who said, “If you don’t know what you want to do, just do something you love. If you don’t love it, try something else.” It’s not like you’re stuck forever.      I guess. It’s just… so much pressure. I feel like everyone else has it all figured out, and I’m just… lost.      You’re not lost, you’re just on the way. And besides, if you start thinking about babies, I’m gonna have to tell you about that time my cousin tried to get a baby bird to talk.      Oh no, don’t even.

So, I was thinking about our school project. You remember that thing about climate change and how it affects local ecosystems? I’m not sure I’m even going to do it. It feels like the bigger issues are out of our control. I mean, the government’s still doing nothing about poverty and inequality.      That’s true. It’s frustrating, isn’t it? You hear all these stats and reports, but nothing changes. I remember in one of our history lessons, we talked about how even back in the 19th century, there were movements for change. Maybe we can do something similar now.      I don’t know. I feel like we’re just kids. What can we really do? Sometimes I think about all the things we’re told to care about—like consumerism and saving the planet—and it feels like we’re being manipulated.      I’ve thought about that too. It’s like we’re bombarded with messages telling us to buy this, use that, and never think about the consequences. But maybe that’s just part of the system. If we start questioning it, even a little, we can make a difference.      I guess. But what if we’re just making things worse? Like, if we do something wrong, does it even matter?      It does. If we don’t, who will?      Maybe. I’ll think about it. I just need to get my head around it.      That’s all you need. Just start small. Maybe we could even start a group or something.      Yeah, maybe.

So, I heard you mentioned the recording process last week. How’s it going? You said you were working with some local musicians, right?      Yeah, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. So, I was just thinking about that time we tried to cook lasagna at my flat last year. I swear, it was like a science experiment gone wrong. You tried to use that weird vegetarian sauce from the shop, and I swear it tasted like it had been sitting in a fridge for a month.      Exactly! And then you tried to convince me it was “authentic Italian,” which I think was just your way of avoiding admitting you’d bought it from the wrong aisle.      Touché! Maybe we should stick to something simple, like takeaway? I mean, I still haven’t mastered the art of making a decent stir-fry.      You’re not the only one. I once tried to make a curry and ended up with a soup. I was like, “It’s a new dish—curry soup!”      Oh, I’ve heard that story. You did end up eating it with a spoon, didn’t you?      Yes! To food, friends, and hopefully, not too many fiascos.

So, I've been meaning to ask everyone, what do you think of  The Matrix Resurrections ? I watched it last night and was like,  Wow, this is so different from the first one. Like,  Tenet ? That was just a mess. But I did enjoy the visuals in  Resurrections . The way they blended the real world with the Matrix was pretty cool. So, I just got back from Paris with Emily, and I’m still in shock. The Eiffel Tower was absolutely incredible, but honestly, I think I’ve got a headache from all the walking.      Oh, I bet! Hey, Alice! Nice to see you before class. How’s everything going?      Hi, Jamie! I’m good, thanks. Just got back from a quick trip to Chichester. Just me and my sister. It was a bit of a journey, but the place was worth it. We had a picnic by the canal and watched the fireworks. It was amazing.      Sounds lovely. Yeah, I’ve been applying for a few things. I’ve even been thinking about doing a master’s in linguistics. It’s got to be better than just teaching English every day.      That’s huge. You’ve got the qualifications for it, and you have a passion for it. I’ve been meaning to do something similar, but work has been getting in the way. Okay, so I’ve got this rice and curry thing going on, and I think I’ve got it figured out, but I’m not sure. ANON, I’ve seen this on TV, but I’m not exactly sure how to do it right.      Deer, it’s not that bad, really. Just take it step by step. First, you’ve got to get the rice right. Use a decent brand, one that’s not too sticky. And don’t forget to rinse it properly. You don’t want that gloop on your tongue when you eat it.      Yeah, I tried that once. I rinsed it like three times, and it turned into a slurry. I ended up with a bowl of rice soup. Not fun.      Ah, I know the feeling. But if you’re using a short-grain rice, like basmati or Arborio, it won’t stick. And don’t cook it in the same pot as the curry, or it’ll get too soft. Use a separate pot for the rice, and maybe add some water with a little salt.      Right, I thought about that. But what if I don’t have a separate pot? I’m just cooking in a saucepan.      You can still do it. Just make sure you set the rice aside once it’s cooked. If you’re using a rice cooker, that’s even easier. But if not, just keep an eye on it. Also, the curry—don’t overcook it. You want it to be a bit thick and rich, but not so much that it clings to the rice.      Got it. And the veggies? I had some leftover cauliflower and carrots. Should I add that to the curry or the rice?      Add them to the curry. Cook them down with the coconut milk and spices. You can leave the rice separate for now. Wait, did you know that some people use jalapenos in their rice? It adds a nice kick.      Oh, I’ve tried that once. I put a few in and it was too spicy. My tongue felt like it was on fire.      That’s the beauty of it—if you like it spicy, you go for it. If not, just skip it. And you know what? I’ve heard people say that if you cook the rice too long, it’ll go off. But I’ve never had that issue.      Yeah, maybe that’s just me.

You know, I’ve been thinking about the whole university thing again. I mean, I’ve got a graduate degree, but I’ve been unemployed for over a year now. It's like I’m stuck in this loop. I don’t even know where to start.      I get it. I’m still in sixth form, so I haven’t had to face that yet, but I can see how it’s got to be so confusing. I feel like I’m more connected to this place now. Even though I grew up elsewhere, I’ve been here long enough to feel like it’s home. Plus, I don’t know if I’d be able to go back and get that life again.      Speaking of home, did you guys see that new show on the box last night? It was about a group of friends trying to start a business together. It was really relatable, honestly.

So, I was just telling my cousin about the meeting I had with the venue manager yesterday. You know, trying to book the conference hall for next month. I was so stressed, I almost forgot to bring my laptop.      You're lucky it didn't go that far. I remember when I was your age, I used to get so flustered with work stuff. I still do, honestly. I mean, I'm retired now, but if I had to do that again, I’d probably faint.      You’d have to be more dramatic than that. I mean, I’m the one who has to manage events and coordinate conferences. It’s not like I’m just sitting around doing nothing. I’ve got to make sure everything runs smoothly, from the seating to the catering.      Yeah, I can imagine. You must have a lot of pressure. I’ve made some great contacts and even got to travel a bit. But sometimes I wish I could just knock off early and go for a run like you do every morning.      You know, I used to run too. I’ve been so busy with work that I haven’t even considered going to the gym. Maybe I’ll start with some yoga or something. I heard it’s good for stress.      You should. It’s better than sitting around worrying about deadlines. You know, I used to tell people that if they wanted to live a long life, they should keep moving. It’s the same with friendships, too. You’ve got to keep them active and engaged.      I couldn’t agree more. I think that’s why I value our friendship so much. We’ve been through a lot together, and we always seem to have something to talk about.      And we’ll be there for each other no matter what.

So, lads, I take it you've had enough of clearing up after dinner? I don’t know how you two manage to make this place look like a war zone every night.      Dad, we just picked up the mess from the table. We didn’t  intentionally  trample the living room like it was a battlefield.      Fair enough, but I’m not sure you two are even aware of how much of a mess you’re making. I had to spend half an hour cleaning the kitchen after you two had a “friendly” tennis match in the garden.      Dad, we were just trying to get a bit of exercise. You know how it is—rackets, balls, and then we ended up arguing about who hit the ball harder. It was  very  competitive.      Competitive? You two are like two kids arguing over who gets the last piece of cake. I remember when I was your age, I used to try and beat my dad at tennis every day. He’d always win, but I’d never give up.      Yeah, and how did that turn out for you, Dad? Did you ever win?      Once. I remember it was the summer after my A-levels. I was so proud of myself. I even made a video of it and posted it on Instagram. Let me see... Yeah, it’s still there.      You posted a tennis match on Instagram? That’s not  actually  a photo, is it?      No, it’s a video. You still have that phone from 2012!      It’s not that old. It’s a couple of years ago. Anyway, I digress. So, I heard you two are both on the lookout for girlfriends. Yeah, I think the modern dating world is a bit of a minefield. You get so many people who are all about looks, but not really about getting to know someone. I mean, isn’t that what real relationships are about?      I don’t know.

So, I was just thinking about that time we had to buy new furniture for the flat after the landlord finally agreed to let us redecorate. I mean, it was a bit of a nightmare, honestly. We had to go to that shop in Manchester, and the place was like a zoo. I swear, the salesperson kept trying to upsell us on this fancy sofa that looked like a spaceship.      Oh, I remember that. You were so obsessed with the one with the built-in USB ports. Didn’t even realize it was a bit too modern for the flat. But I guess it made sense at the time. What’s the point of a sofa if you can’t charge your phone while you’re on it?      Aye, and I remember the look on your face when you tried to move it through the door. You looked like you’d just been told your cat had run off with the keys.      I still remember the tip we had to give the delivery guy. He had to climb over the sofa to get in, and it was like he was doing a tightrope walk. I was so nervous it would fall over.      And then there was that time when ANON’s friend’s partner was in the hospital with dementia. You remember how she started trying to organize the furniture like it was a Scout camp? Honestly, I couldn’t tell if she was trying to help or just making it worse.      Aye, she was being a bit of a mess, but in a good way. I think she was just trying to make everything “right” again. It was like the whole family was trying to rearrange themselves, just like the furniture.      And don’t even get me started on the unwanted presents. I still have that glass vase from the beaver scout Christmas party that I haven’t used since 2014. It’s like a ghost of a memory in my living room.      You know what really bugs me though? People who wash your clothes and leave them in the machine without using the right detergent. I’m not saying it’s a crime, but it’s like they’re trying to sabotage your laundry.

Hey Mum, how’s everything going? I’ve been meaning to catch up with you for ages.      Oh, I’m good, love! Just been busy with the school term and trying to get my head around this new project at work. You know how it is.      Yeah, I can imagine. I’ve been feeling the same—switching between work and personal life is a bit of a rollercoaster. Speaking of work, I heard there might be some redundancy at my company.      Oh no, really? That’s not good news. I’ve heard about that too. I think they’re planning to cut back on staff in the administrative department.      Yeah, I’m really worried about it. I’ve been thinking about maybe moving to a different role or even changing jobs. Do you think there’s any chance of getting a new position if I apply for some training?      Well, I think it’s worth looking into. You’re pretty capable, and your project coordination skills are top-notch. You know, I’ve been thinking about getting back into the gym as well. It’s been ages since I last went.      That’s a good idea. I’ve been meaning to start again too. I’ve even been researching some local gym memberships. Maybe we could go together sometime?      That sounds lovely. I’d love to have some time with you. Oh, and I saw you mentioned something about a house extension. What are your plans with that?      I’ve been planning to do it after the holidays, but I’m not sure yet. I’m a bit overwhelmed with the planning and building process. It’s a big project, and I need to be careful with the budget.      It’s a big step, I know. But I’m sure you’ll manage. And have you thought about the weekend plans? I was thinking of going to that new café in town.      I’ve been meaning to check it out. I’ve heard great things about the food. Maybe we could go there together?      That would be brilliant. I’d love to get out and do something fun.      Alright, I’ll make sure to book a table. And what about Grandad? He’s been feeling under the weather lately.      Yes, he’s been a bit off. I think he’s overdoing it with the snacks again. It’s a shame, really.

So, what do you think we should do today, little man? You know, with all the time off from school.      I don’t know... I just want to play with my toys.      Well, you can play with your toys, but maybe we should try something new today. What do you think?      We could go to the park. The weather’s nice, and it’s not too hot. You know, maybe even go for a swim?      Yeah, that sounds like a good idea. But wait, I’ve been meaning to practice my guitar. Maybe I can do that in the afternoon.      Can I watch Stick with Mick while you practice?      Oh, you love that show, don’t you? Well, you can watch it after dinner, but only if you finish your vegetables.      Yeah, that’s a deal. But do you think we could also go to the library? I heard there are some new books about Japan.      Japan? That’s interesting. I’ve never been there, but I’ve heard about their culture and their food.      Yeah, I want to learn more about Japanese culture. Maybe even read some Japanese manga.      What’s manga?      It’s a type of comic book from Japan. They’re really popular there, especially with kids.      I might try reading one. But first, let’s make sure we do some chores around the house.      Yeah, we’ve been meaning to clean the kitchen and do some gardening. Maybe you can help with that, too.      Can I help with the garden? I like digging in the dirt.      That’s a good start. I think we can do some of that today.      Alright, let’s make a plan. After breakfast, you can help with the garden, then we’ll go to the park. In the afternoon, you can watch Stick with Mick, and I’ll practice my guitar. Then we can go to the library.      Okay, I like that plan!      Good, then we’re all set for a fun day. Just don’t forget your lunch!      What’s that? You don’t want to forget your lunch?      No, I just want to make sure we’re all fed and ready for the day.      Okay, I’m not hungry. I just want to play.      Well, we’ll see. But first, let’s eat. Then we can start our day.      Agreed. Let’s make this summer the best one yet.      I’m ready.

So, I just watched this film called  The Dentist , and it’s like...  The Thing , but with a dental chair. Absolute nightmare!      Yeah, I saw that too. I thought it was a satire on dental horror, but then it turned out to be a full-on thriller. You know what really creeped me out? The guy with the missing tooth. Like,  what even is that?       Oh man, I was like, “Wait, is he a patient or a dentist?” I thought he was a patient who  accidentally  became a dentist.      My friend said it was inspired by his cousin’s experience. He said he once had a dentist who looked like he’d been through a war.      Yeah, I’ve had that. I had a dentist who kept asking me if I wanted to be part of a study, like, “We’re testing a new drilling technique, and you’re the first human subject.”      Oh no! Did you sign up?      No, I ran out. But I did get a free root canal.      That’s the spirit! Now, speaking of weird experiences, have you been to Liverpool? I’ve heard your flat’s in the city.      Yeah, I live just a few minutes from the docks. You ever been to the Baltic Triangle? It’s got this cool vibe.      Oh yeah, I used to work there. That’s where I picked up my Liverpool accent, by the way. I used to think I was just being casual, but now I realize it’s  deeply  ingrained.      You’re not the only one. I’ve been told I’ve got a Leicester accent, but I swear I just talk like I was born in the Midlands.      Yeah, but you’re the only one I know who can tell a story about a gig and still make the point about the goth band with the goat.      That was a  huge  moment. That goat had more personality than your entire class at uni.      True. Anyway, I’m thinking of writing a book about the weirdest holidays I’ve had. You want to be in it?      Only if I can be the goat.      Deal. But first, let’s just survive this film. I think I’ve seen enough horror to last a lifetime.      Alright, but you’re the one who suggested it.      Hey, it’s better than watching football.      Yeah, and I’ve  definitely  seen more football than film.

So, how's life treating you these days, love? I've been meaning to ask you how your new job is going. I know you started at the primary school last month, right?      Oh, it's going well, thank you! I'm actually loving it more than I expected. The kids are so full of energy, and I feel like I'm making a real difference. I was so happy to see everyone come together, even though it's been a tough few months for some of us. I know things have been a bit rocky with work and everything else.      I know, it's been a challenging time for a lot of people. But it's good to see you still managing to make time for family and the important things. I was just thinking about our own Christening—remember how we got all dressed up and stayed up until midnight? It felt like the whole family was coming together just like that.      Oh, I remember! That was so much fun. I still have those photos somewhere. I think I need to find them and show them to my students sometime. They might get a laugh out of seeing how we all looked back then.      That would be great. You always had such a way with people, even back then. I'm just glad you're happy and settled. I hope you can take a proper holiday soon. You deserve a break.      Thanks, Mum. I'm planning to take a short trip to the coast with some friends. I'm thinking of somewhere with a beach and a bit of sun. Maybe we can go together sometime?      That sounds perfect. I'd love that. So, how's life treating you these days, Ann? I haven’t seen you in ages. You know, since the last family gathering.      Oh, it’s been a while, Lucy. Life’s been pretty busy, as usual. I’ve been juggling work and family, but I must say, I’m starting to feel the strain. You know how it is with kids and all that.      Definitely, I know exactly how you feel.
